en.title: Herrerasaurus: The Early Hunter of the Dinosaur Age
en.excerpt: Herrerasaurus is likely a genus of saurischian dinosaur from the Late Triassic period. Measuring 6 m (20 ft) long and weighing around 350 kg (770 lb), this genus was one of the earliest dinosaurs from the fossil record.
en.contentMarkdown:
# Herrerasaurus: The Early Hunter of the Dinosaur Age

Few creatures ignite the human imagination like dinosaurs. These animals ruled Earth's landmasses for more than 165 million years, far longer than humans have existed. This article brings you closer to them, from anatomy and behavior to the environments that shaped their lives in the Mesozoic Era.

Herrerasaurus is likely a genus of saurischian dinosaur from the Late Triassic period. Measuring 6 m (20 ft) long and weighing around 350 kg (770 lb), this genus was one of the earliest dinosaurs from the fossil record. Its name means "Herrera's lizard", after the rancher who discovered the first specimen in 1958 in South America. All known fossils of this carnivore have been discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation of Carnian age (late Triassic according to the ICS, dated to 231.4 million years ago) in northwestern Argentina. The type species, Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis, was described by Osvaldo Reig in 1963 and is the only species assigned to the genus. Ischisaurus and Frenguellisaurus are synonyms.

For many years, the classification of Herrerasaurus was unclear because it was known from very fragmentary remains. It was hypothesized to be a basal theropod, a basal sauropodomorph, a basal saurischian, or not a dinosaur at all but another type of archosaur. However, with the discovery of an almost complete skeleton and skull in 1988, Herrerasaurus has been classified as an early saurischian in most of the phylogenies on the origin and early evolution of dinosaurs. It is a member of the Herrerasauridae, a family of similar genera that were among the earliest of the dinosaurian evolutionary radiation.

![Herrerasaurus: The Early Hunter of the Dinosaur Age](/images/topics/dinosaurus.svg)
*Gambar: Herrerasaurus: The Early Hunter of the Dinosaur Age*

## Discovery

Herrerasaurus was named by paleontologist Osvaldo Reig after Victorino Herrera, an Andean goatherd who first noticed its fossils in outcrops near the city of San Juan, Argentina, in 1959. These rocks, which later yielded Eoraptor, are part of the Ischigualasto Formation and date from the late Carnian stage of the Late Triassic period. Reig named a second dinosaur from these rocks in the same publication as Herrerasaurus; this dinosaur, Ischisaurus cattoi, is now considered a junior synonym and a juvenile of Herrerasaurus.

Reig believed Herrerasaurus was an early example of a carnosaur, but this was the subject of much debate over the next 30 years, and the genus was variously classified during that time. In 1970, Steel classified Herrerasaurus as a prosauropod. In 1972, Peter Galton classified the genus as not diagnosable beyond Saurischia. Later, using cladistic analysis, some researchers put Herrerasaurus and Staurikosaurus at the base of the dinosaur tree before the separation between ornithischians and saurischians. Several researchers classified the remains as non-dinosaurian.

Two other partial skeletons with skull material were named Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis by Fernando Novas in 1986, but this species, too, is now thought to be a synonym. Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis was discovered in 1975 and was described by Novas (1986), who considered it a primitive saurischian and possibly a theropod. Novas (1992) and Sereno and Novas (1992) examined the Frenguellisaurus remains and found them referable to Herrerasaurus. Ischisaurus cattoi was discovered in 1960 and described by Reig in 1963. Novas (1992) and Sereno and Novas (1992) reviewed its remains and found them also to be referable to Herrerasaurus.

A complete Herrerasaurus skull was found in 1988 by a team of paleontologists led by Paul Sereno. Based on the new fossils, authors such as Thomas Holtz and José Bonaparte classified Herrerasaurus at the base of the saurischian tree before the divergence between prosauropods and theropods. However, Sereno favored classifying Herrerasaurus (and the Herrerasauridae) as primitive theropods. These two classifications have become the most persistent, with Rauhut (2003) and Bittencourt and Kellner (2004) favoring the early theropod hypothesis, and Max Langer (2004), Langer and Benton (2006), and Randall Irmis and his coauthors (2007) favoring the basal saurischian hypothesis. If Herrerasaurus were indeed a theropod, it would indicate that theropods, sauropodomorphs, and ornithischians diverged even earlier than herrerasaurids, before the middle Carnian, and that "all three lineages independently evolved several dinosaurian features, such as a more advanced ankle joint or an open acetabulum". This view is further supported by ichnological records showing large tridactyl (three-toed) footprints that can be attributed only to a theropod dinosaur. These footprints date from the early Carnian Los Rastros Formation in Argentina, which predates Herrerasaurus by several million years.

The study of early dinosaurs such as Herrerasaurus and Eoraptor, therefore, has important implications for the concept of dinosaurs as a monophyletic group (a group descended from a common ancestor). The monophyly of dinosaurs was explicitly proposed in the 1970s by Galton and Robert T. Bakker, who compiled a list of cranial and postcranial synapomorphies (common anatomical traits derived from the common ancestor). Later authors proposed additional synapomorphies. An extensive study of Herrerasaurus by Sereno in 1992 suggested that of these proposed synapomorphies, only one cranial and seven postcranial features were actually derived from a common ancestor and that the others were attributable to convergent evolution. Sereno's analysis of Herrerasaurus also led him to propose several new dinosaurian synapomorphies.

## Description

Herrerasaurus was a lightly built bipedal carnivore with a long tail and a relatively small head. Adults had skulls up to 56 cm (22 in) long and were up to 6 m (20 ft) in total length and 350 kg (770 lb) in weight. Smaller specimens were about 4.5 m (15 ft) long and weighed about 200 kg (440 lb).

Herrerasaurus was fully bipedal. It had strong hind limbs with short thighs and rather long feet, indicating that it was likely a swift runner. The foot had five toes, but only the middle three (digits II, III, and IV) bore weight. The outer toes (I and V) were small; the first toe had a small claw. The tail, partially stiffened by overlapping vertebral projections, balanced the body and was also an adaptation for speed. The forelimbs of Herrerasaurus were less than half the length of its hind limbs. The upper arm and forearm were rather short, while the manus (hand) was elongated. The first two fingers and the thumb ended in curved, sharp claws for grasping prey. The fourth and fifth digits were small stubs without claws.

Herrerasaurus displays traits that are found in different groups of dinosaurs, and several traits found in non-dinosaurian archosaurs. Although it shares most of the characteristics of dinosaurs, there are a few differences, particularly in the shape of its hip and leg bones. Its pelvis is like that of saurischian dinosaurs, but it has a bony acetabulum (where the femur meets the pelvis) that was only partially open. The ilium, the main hip bone, is supported by only two sacrals, a basal trait. However, the pubis points backwards, a derived trait as seen in dromaeosaurids and birds. Additionally, the end of the pubis has a booted shape, like those in avetheropods; and the vertebral centra have an hourglass shape as found in Allosaurus.

Herrerasaurus had a long, narrow skull that lacked nearly all the specializations that characterized later dinosaurs, and more closely resembled those of more primitive archosaurs such as Euparkeria. It had five pairs of fenestrae (skull openings) in its skull, two pairs of which were for the eyes and nostrils. Between the eyes and the nostrils were two antorbital fenestrae and a pair of tiny, 1-centimeter-long (0.39 in) slit-like holes called promaxillary fenestrae.

Herrerasaurus had a flexible joint in the lower jaw that could slide back and forth to deliver a grasping bite. This cranial specialization is unusual among dinosaurs but has evolved independently in some lizards. The rear of the lower jaw also had fenestrae. The jaws were equipped with large serrated teeth for biting and eating flesh, and the neck was slender and flexible.

According to Novas (1993), Herrerasaurus can be distinguished based on the following features: the presence of a premaxilla-maxilla fenestra, and the dorsal part of laterotemporal fenestra is less than a third as wide as the ventral part; the presence of a ridge on the lateral surface of the jugal bone, and a deeply incised supratemporal fossa that extends across the medial postorbital process; the subquadrate ventral squamosal process has a lateral depression, and the quadratojugal bone overlaps the posterodorsal quadrate face; the pterygoid process of the quadrate has an inturned, trough-shaped ventral margin, and the presence of a slender ribbed posterodorsal dentary process; the surangular bone has a forked anterior process for articulation with the posterodorsal dentary process; the humerus' internal tuberosity is proximally projected and separated from the humeral head by a deep groove (also present in coelophysoids); possesses enlarged hands, which are 60% of the size of the humerus+radius, and the humeral entepicondyle is ridge-like with anterior and posterior depressions; and the posterior border of the ilial peduncle forms a right angle with the dorsal border of the shaft on the ischium.

According to Sereno (1993), Herrerasaurus can be distinguished based on the following features, all of which are unknown in other herrerasaurids: a circular pit is present on the humeral ectepicondyle, a feature also present in Saturnalia; a saddle-shaped ulnar condyle of the humerus, and the articular surface for the ulnare on the ulna is convex; the articular surface of the ulnare is smaller than that of the ulna, a feature unknown in Staurikosaurus and Sanjuansaurus; the centrale is placed distal to the radiale; a broad subnarial process of the premaxilla, and a broad supratemporal depression (noted by Sereno and Novas, 1993); the basal tuber and the occipital condyle are subequal in width (noted by Sereno and Novas, 1993).

## Classification

Herrerasaurus was originally considered to be a genus within Carnosauria, which then included forms similar to Megalosaurus and Antrodemus (the latter is probably equivalent to Allosaurus), even though Herrerasaurus lived many millions of years before them and therefore would have retained multiple primitive features. This carnosaurian classification was amended upon by Rozhdestvensky and Tatarinov in 1964, who classified Herrerasaurus within the family Gryponichidae inside Carnosauria. The same year, Walker published a differing opinion that Herrerasaurus instead was allied with Plateosauridae, although it differed in possessing a pubic boot. Walker also proposed that Herrerasaurus may instead be close to Poposaurus (now considered a pseudosuchian) and the unnamed theropod from the Dockum Group of Texas (now assigned to the rauisuchian Postosuchus). In 1985, Charig noted that Herrerasaurus was of uncertain classification, showing similarities to both "prosauropods" and "carnosaurians". Romer (1966), simply noted that Herrerasaurus was a prosauropod possibly within Plateosauridae. In the description of Staurikosaurus, Colbert noted that there were many similarities between his taxon and Herrerasaurus, but classified them in separate families, with Herrerasaurus in Teratosauridae. In 1970, Bonaparte also proposed similarities between Herrerasaurus and Staurikosaurus, and while classifying them both clearly as in Saurischia, he stated that they appeared as though they could not be placed in a current family.

This was further supported by Benedetto in 1973, who named for the taxa the new family Herrerasauridae, which he classified as saurischians, possibly within Theropoda but not in Sauropodomorpha. However, in 1977 Galton proposed that Herrerasauridae only included Herrerasaurus, and found it to be Saurischian incertae sedis.

Proposed in 1987 by Brinkman and Sues, Herrerasaurus has at times been considered basal to Ornithischia and Saurischia, although Brinkmann and Sues still considered it to be inside Dinosauria. They supported this on the basis that Herrerasaurus has a large pedal digit V, and has a well developed medial wall on the acetabulum. Brinkmann and Sues considered Staurikosaurus and Herrerasaurus to not form a true group called Herrerasauridae, and that instead they were successively more primitive forms. Also, they considered the characters used by Benedetto to be invalid, instead representing only the plesiomorphic state that was found in both taxa. This was disagreed with in 1992 by Novas, who stated many derived synapomorphies of Herrerasauridae, such as a distinct pubic boot, but still classified them as basal to Ornithischia and Saurischia. Novas defined the family as the least common ancestor of Herrerasaurus and Staurikosaurus and all its descendants. A differing definition of Herrerasauridae as the most inclusive clade including Herrerasaurus but not Passer domesticus was first suggested by Sereno (1998), and more closely follows the original inclusion proposed by Benedetto. Another group, Herrerasauria was named by Galton in 1985, and defined as Herrerasaurus but not Liliensternus or Plateosaurus by Langer (2004), who used the node-based definition for Herrerasauridae.

In a revision of basal Dinosauria, Padian and May (1993) discussed the definition of the clade, and redefined it as the latest common ancestor of Triceratops and birds. They also discussed what this definition would do to the most basal taxa, such as Herrerasauridae, and Eoraptor. Padian and May considered that since both Herrerasauridae and Eoraptor lack many diagnostic features of Saurischia or Ornithischia, that they could not be considered inside Dinosauria.

A later 1994 study by Novas instead classified Herrerasaurus within Dinosauria, and strongly supported its position within Saurischia, as well as provided synapomorphies that it shared with Theropoda. Novas found that the primitive features of lacking a brevis fossa and having only two sacral vertebrae were simply reversals found in the genus. In 1996, Novas went further by supporting a theropod position for Herrerasaurus with a phylogenetic analysis, which placed it closer to Neotheropoda than Eoraptor or Sauropodomorpha. Langer (2004) mentioned that this hypothesis was widely accepted, but that more later authors instead preferred to place Herrerasaurus as well as Eoraptor basal to Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha, a clade called Eusaurischia. Langer (2004) conducted a phylogenetic analysis, and found that it was much more likely that Herrerasaurus was a basal saurischian, than either a theropod or a non-dinosaurian. Langer's proposal was supported by multiple studies until the discovery of Tawa, when Nesbitt et al. conducted a more inclusive analysis, and the resulting cladogram placed Herrerasauridae basal to Eoraptor, but closer to Dilophosaurus than Sauropodomorpha. Unlike Nesbitt, Ezcurra (2010) conducted a phylogenetic analysis to place his new taxon Chromogisaurus, and found that Herrerasauridae was basal to Eusaurischia.

In 2010, Alcocer and Martinez described a new taxon of herrerasaurid, Sanjuansaurus. It could be distinguished from Herrerasaurus based on multiple features. In the phylogenetic analysis, Herrerasaurus, Sanjuansaurus and Staurikosaurus all were in a polytomy, and Herrerasauridae was the most primitive group of saurischian, outside Eusaurischia, Eoraptor and Guaibasaurus. In 2011, Martinez et al. described Eodromaeus, a basal theropod from the same formation as Herrerasaurus. In a phylogenetic analysis, Eoraptor was placed within Sauropodomorpha, Herrerasauridae was placed as the most basal theropods, and Eodromaeus was placed as the next most basal. A more recent analysis, by Bittencourt et al. (2014), placed Herrerasauridae in a polytomy with Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha, with Eoraptor also being in an unresolved position. This cladogram is shown below.

Other members of the clade may include Chindesaurus from the Upper Petrified Forest (Chinle Formation) of Arizona, and possibly Caseosaurus from the Tecovas Formation of the Dockum Group in Texas, although the relationships of these animals are not fully understood, and not all paleontologists agree. Other possible basal theropods, Alwalkeria from the Late Triassic Lower Maleri Formation of India, and Teyuwasu, known from very fragmentary remains from the Late Triassic of Brazil, might be related. Paul (1988) noted that it had been incorrectly suggested that Staurikosaurus pricei was a juvenile Herrerasaurus. This claim was refuted when pelvic bones from a juvenile Herrerasaurus were discovered, which upon examination did not resemble the pelvic bones of Staurikosaurus.

## Paleobiology

The teeth of Herrerasaurus indicate that it was a carnivore; its size indicates it would have preyed upon small and medium-sized plant eaters. These might have included other dinosaurs, such as Pisanosaurus, as well as the more plentiful rhynchosaurs and synapsids. The similarity of its dental microwear patterns to those of modern slender-snouted crocodylians and small-bodied broad-snouted crocodylians, however, indicates that Herrerasaurus may have mainly consumed small prey that could have been swallowed whole with very minimal or no oral processing, although the authors of the study concluding this caution that this may be due to the small sample size of Herrerasaurus teeth that underwent dental microwear texture analysis in the study. Herrerasaurus itself may have been preyed upon by giant "rauisuchians" (loricatans) like Saurosuchus; puncture wounds were found in one skull.

Coprolites (fossilized dung) containing small bones but no trace of plant fragments, discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation, have been assigned to Herrerasaurus based on fossil abundance. Mineralogical and chemical analysis of these coprolites indicates that if the referral to Herrerasaurus was correct, this carnivore could digest bone.

Comparisons between the scleral rings of Herrerasaurus and modern birds and reptiles suggest that it may have been cathemeral, active throughout the day at short intervals.

In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, 12 hand bones and 20 foot bones referred to Herrerasaurus were examined for signs of stress fracture, but none were found.

PVSJ 407, a Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis, had a pit in a skull bone attributed by Paul Sereno and Novas to a bite. Two additional pits occurred on the splenial. The areas around these pits are swollen and porous, suggesting the wounds were afflicted by a short-lived non-lethal infection. Because of the size and angles of the wound, it is likely that they were obtained in a fight with another Herrerasaurus.

## Paleoecology

The holotype of Herrerasaurus (PVL 2566) was discovered in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in San Juan, Argentina. It was collected in 1961 by Victorino Herrera, in sediments that were deposited in the Carnian stage of the Triassic period, approximately 231 to 229 million years ago. Over the years, the Ischigualasto Formation produced other fossils ultimately referred to Herrerasaurus. In 1958, A.S. Romer discovered specimen MCZ 7063, originally referred to Staurikosaurus in Carnian sediments. Herrerasaurus specimens PVL 2045 and MLP(4)61, were collected in 1959 and 1960, respectively, in sediments that were deposited in the Norian stage of the Triassic period, approximately 228 to 208 million years ago. However, these specimens are no longer regarded as pertaining to Herrerasaurus. In 1960, Scaglia collected specimen MACN 18.060, originally the holotype of Ischisaurus cattoi, in sediments deposited in the Carnian stage. In 1961, Scaglia collected Herrerasaurus specimen PVL 2558, in the Carnian beds of this formation. In 1990, the Cancha de Bochas Member produced more Herrerasaurus specimens, also from its Carnian beds. Specimen PVSJ 53, originally the holotype of Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis, was collected by Gargiulo & Oñate in 1975 in sediments that were deposited in the Carnian stage.

Although Herrerasaurus shared the body shape of the large carnivorous dinosaurs, it lived during a time when dinosaurs were small and few. It was the time of non-dinosaurian reptiles, not dinosaurs, and a major turning point in the Earth's ecology. The vertebrate fauna of the Ischigualasto Formation and the slightly later Los Colorados Formation consisted mainly of a variety of crurotarsal archosaurs and synapsids. In the Ischigualasto Formation, dinosaurs constituted only about 10% of the total number of fossils, but by the end of the Triassic Period, dinosaurs were becoming the dominant large land animals, and the other archosaurs and synapsids declined in variety and number.

Studies suggest that the paleoenvironment of the Ischigualasto Formation was a volcanically active floodplain covered by forests and subject to strong seasonal rainfalls. The climate was moist and warm, though subject to seasonal variations. Vegetation consisted of ferns (Cladophlebis), horsetails, and giant conifers (Protojuniperoxylon). These plants formed lowland forests along the banks of rivers. Herrerasaurus remains appear to have been the most common among the carnivores of the Ischigualasto Formation. It lived in the jungles of Late Triassic South America alongside other early dinosaurs, such as Sanjuansaurus, Eoraptor, Panphagia, and Chromogisaurus, as well as rhynchosaurs (Scaphonyx), cynodonts (e.g., Exaeretodon, Ecteninion and Chiniquodon), dicynodonts (Ischigualastia), pseudosuchians (e.g., Saurosuchus, Sillosuchus and Aetosauroides), proterochampsids (e.g., Proterochampsa) and temnospondyls (Pelorocephalus).

## Poin-Poin Kunci

- Herrerasaurus was named by paleontologist Osvaldo Reig after Victorino Herrera, an Andean goatherd who first noticed its fossils in outcrops near the city of San Juan, Argentina, in 1959.
- Herrerasaurus was a lightly built bipedal carnivore with a long tail and a relatively small head.
- Herrerasaurus was originally considered to be a genus within Carnosauria, which then included forms similar to Megalosaurus and Antrodemus (the latter is probably equivalent to Allosaurus), even though Herrerasaurus lived many millions of years before them and therefore would have retained multiple primitive features.
- The teeth of Herrerasaurus indicate that it was a carnivore; its size indicates it would have preyed upon small and medium-sized plant eaters.
- The holotype of Herrerasaurus (PVL 2566) was discovered in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in San Juan, Argentina.

## Kesimpulan

Dinosaurs were not movie monsters; they were masterpieces of evolution that filled this planet for tens of millions of generations. The more we study them, the more we realize how surprising the ancient world was, and how many stories still lie buried, waiting to be found.

# Token dan Context Window: Memori AI yang Terbatas


![Token dan Context Window — ilustrasi topik](/images/topics/ai.svg)
*Gambar: Token dan Context Window*

Ketika Anda mengetik pertanyaan panjang ke sebuah asisten AI dan menerima jawaban yang relevan, mudah terbayang bahwa mesin itu "membaca" tulisan Anda seperti manusia. Kenyataannya jauh lebih menarik. Model bahasa tidak bekerja dengan huruf atau kata utuh; ia bekerja dengan *token*—potongan teks kecil yang menjadi satuan hitung paling mendasar dalam seluruh sistem. Dan seberapa banyak token yang bisa dipegang model dalam satu percakapan ditentukan oleh sesuatu yang disebut *context window*.

Dua konsep ini menjelaskan banyak hal yang sering membuat pengguna bingung: mengapa biaya API dihitung per karakter tertentu, mengapa AI lupa isi obrolan yang panjang, dan mengapa dokumen raksasa tidak bisa langsung ditempelkan begitu saja. Artikel ini membedah keduanya dengan bahasa sederhana.

## Apa Itu Token?

Token adalah potongan teks yang dihasilkan proses *tokenisasi*. Potongan itu bisa sekata pendek, satu kata, atau bagian dari kata—tergantung frekuensi kemunculannya dalam data pelatihan. Kata yang sangat umum biasanya menjadi satu token utuh, sementara kata jarang dipecah menjadi beberapa bagian. Sebagai gambaran kasar, satu token dalam bahasa Inggris setara dengan sekitar tiga sampai empat karakter; dalam bahasa Indonesia, angkanya cenderung sedikit lebih tinggi karena struktur katanya lebih kompleks.

Mengapa model tidak langsung memakai huruf atau kata? Huruf membuat urutan terlalu panjang dan kehilangan makna, sedangkan kata utuh menghasilkan kosakata raksasa yang tidak praktis. Token adalah titik tengah yang elegan: cukup pendek untuk fleksibel, cukup panjang untuk membawa makna. Dari jutaan token yang mungkin, model belajar hubungan antarpotongan inilah yang akhirnya memunculkan kesan "memahami" bahasa.

Pemahaman token juga menjelaskan perilaku aneh yang kadang muncul. Model bisa salah menghitung jumlah huruf dalam sebuah kata, misalnya, karena ia melihat kata itu sebagai satu token utuh—notasi abjad bukan cara kerjanya. Ia juga bisa tersendat pada teks berulang atau karakter langka, karena polanya nyaris tak pernah muncul saat pelatihan.

## Context Window: Memori Kerja yang Terbatas

Context window adalah jumlah maksimum token yang dapat diproses model dalam satu kali interaksi. Anggap saja ini meja kerja model: semua bahan—system prompt, seluruh isi percakapan, dokumen yang dilampirkan, dan jawaban yang sedang ditulis—harus muat di atasnya. Ketika percakapan memanjang dan meja penuh, bahan paling awal harus "disingkirkan" atau diringkas agar sisa obrolan tetap terproses.

Ukuran context window berbeda antar-model dan terus bertambah seiring waktu, dari puluhan ribu token pada generasi awal hingga ratusan ribu bahkan jutaan pada model mutakhir. Namun ada dua catatan penting. Pertama, kapasitas besar tidak menjamin kualitas: penelitian dan pengalaman praktis menunjukkan kemampuan model mengingat detail cenderung menurun untuk informasi yang letaknya di tengah konteks panjang—a phenomenon yang sering disebut *lost in the middle*. Kedua, setiap token dalam konteks tetap dihitung sebagai biaya, sehingga "tempel semuanya" bukan strategi yang murah.


![Token dan Context Window — teknologi & produktivitas](/images/topics/teknologi-alt.svg)
*Gambar: Token dan Context Window*

## Implikasi Praktis bagi Pengguna

Memahami token dan context window memberi keuntungan langsung dalam pemakaian sehari-hari:

1. **Kelola percakapan panjang dengan sadar.** Jika sesi sudah sangat panjang dan jawaban mulai kehilangan fokus, mulai obrolan baru lalu ringkas poin penting secara manual.
2. **Tempelkan hanya bagian relevan dari dokumen.** Alih-alih memasukkan 100 halaman, ekstrak bab atau bagian yang benar-benar dibutuhkan.
3. **Perhatikan struktur biaya API.** Karena input dan output sama-sama dihitung per token, prompt yang ringkas dan instruksi yang efisien menekan tagihan secara signifikan.
4. **Letakkan informasi kunci di awal atau akhir prompt**, bagian yang paling kuat diperhatikan model.

Bagi pengembang, kedua konsep ini menjadi dasar arsitektur aplikasi: teknik seperti RAG, ringkasan bertahap, dan manajemen riwayat chat semuanya lahir dari keterbatasan context window.

## Kesimpulan

Token adalah cara AI membaca dunia—potongan-potongan teks kecil yang menyusun segala hal yang Anda tulis dan semua yang ia jawab. Context window adalah ruang kerja tempat potongan-potongan itu berkumpul, dengan ukuran yang terbatas meski terus membesar. Memahami keduanya mengubah cara kita berinteraksi dengan AI: lebih hemat biaya, lebih efisien, dan lebih realistis tentang apa yang model ingat serta apa yang ia lupakan. Pada akhirnya, AI bukanlah perpustakaan tak terbatas; ia rekan kerja brilian dengan meja yang hanya selebar context window-nya.

excerpt: "AI doesn't read letters—it reads tokens. Understanding tokenization and context windows helps you use AI more efficiently."
meta_title: "Tokens and Context Windows Explained Simply"
meta_description: "What tokens and context windows are in AI models, why they matter for cost and answer quality, and how to work within their limits."
category: "teknologi"
tags: ["ai", "llm", "tokenization", "context-window"]

# Tokens and Context Windows: The Limits of AI Memory


![Tokens and Context Windows — ilustrasi topik](/images/topics/ai.svg)
*Image: Tokens and Context Windows*

When you type a long question into an AI assistant and get a relevant answer back, it is tempting to imagine the machine "reading" your text the way a person would. The reality is far more interesting. Language models do not operate on letters or even whole words; they operate on *tokens*—small pieces of text that are the fundamental unit of accounting for the entire system. And how many tokens a model can hold at once is determined by something called the *context window*.

These two concepts explain a lot that puzzles users: why API costs are billed per unit of text, why an AI forgets earlier parts of a long conversation, and why you cannot simply paste in an enormous document. This article unpacks both in plain language.

## What Is a Token?

A token is a chunk of text produced by a process called *tokenization*. A chunk may be as short as one character, as long as one word, or anything in between—depending on how frequently it appeared in the training data. Very common words usually become single tokens, while rare words get split into pieces. As a rough guide, one English token corresponds to about three or four characters; for languages like Indonesian the number tends to run slightly higher because of more complex word structure.

Why not just use letters or whole words? Letters make sequences far too long and strip away meaning; whole words would require an impractically enormous vocabulary. Tokens are an elegant middle ground: short enough to be flexible, long enough to carry meaning. From a vocabulary of thousands of tokens, the model learns the relationships between them—and that web of relationships is what ultimately produces the impression of "understanding" language.

Token awareness also explains odd behaviors that sometimes surface. A model can miscount the letters in a word, for instance, because it sees that word as one indivisible token—letter-level notation is simply not how it works. It can also stumble on repeated text or rare characters, since those patterns barely appeared during training.

## The Context Window: Limited Working Memory

The context window is the maximum number of tokens a model can process in a single interaction. Think of it as the model's desk: everything—system prompt, the full conversation history, attached documents, and the answer being written—must fit on it. When a conversation grows and the desk fills up, the earliest material gets dropped or summarized so the rest can still be processed.

Context window sizes differ between models and keep growing over time, from tens of thousands of tokens in early generations to hundreds of thousands or even millions in cutting-edge systems. Two caveats matter, though. First, large capacity does not guarantee quality: research and practical experience show that models tend to recall details less reliably when information sits in the middle of very long contexts—a phenomenon often called *lost in the middle*. Second, every token in context still counts toward cost, so "just paste everything" is never a cheap strategy.


![Tokens and Context Windows — teknologi & produktivitas](/images/topics/teknologi-alt.svg)
*Image: Tokens and Context Windows*

## What This Means in Practice

Understanding tokens and context windows pays off immediately in daily use:

1. **Manage long conversations deliberately.** If a session has grown huge and answers are losing focus, start fresh and manually summarize the key points.
2. **Paste only relevant document sections.** Instead of feeding 100 pages, extract the chapter or passage you actually need.
3. **Watch your API billing structure.** Since input and output are both billed per token, concise prompts and efficient instructions meaningfully cut costs.
4. **Put critical information at the beginning or end of your prompt**—the positions where models pay closest attention.

For developers, these two concepts underpin application architecture: techniques like RAG, staged summarization, and chat-history management all exist because context windows have limits.

## Conclusion

Tokens are how AI reads the world—small pieces of text composing everything you write and everything it answers. The context window is the workspace where those pieces gather, finite even as it keeps expanding. Grasping both changes how you interact with AI: more cost-efficient, more effective, and more realistic about what the model remembers and what it forgets. In the end, AI is not an unlimited library; it is a brilliant collaborator whose desk is only as wide as its context window.

id.contentMarkdown:
# Velociraptor: Monster Sebenarnya vs Hollywood

Sedikit makhluk yang memicu imajinasi manusia sebesar dinosaurus. Makhluk-makhluk ini menguasai daratan bumi selama lebih dari 165 juta tahun, jauh lebih lama daripada keberadaan umat manusia. Artikel ini mengajak Anda mengenal sosoknya lebih dekat, dari anatomi dan perilaku hingga lingkungan yang membentuk kehidupan mereka di era Mesozoikum.

Velociraptor (; lit. 'pencuri cepat') adalah genus dinosaurus dromaeosaurid kecil yang hidup di Asia selama zaman Kapur Akhir, sekitar 75 juta hingga 71 juta tahun yang lalu (mya). Dua spesies kini dikenali, walaupun yang lain telah ditetapkan pada masa lalu. Jenis spesiesnya adalah V. mongoliensis, dinamai dan dideskripsikan pada tahun 1924. Fosil spesies ini telah ditemukan di Formasi Djadochta, Mongolia. Spesies kedua, V. osmolskae, dinamakan pada tahun 2008 untuk bahan tengkorak dari Formasi Bayan Mandahu, China. Rekor yang mungkin diketahui dari Formasi Nemegt.

Lebih kecil dari dromaeosaurid lain seperti Deinonychus dan Achillobator, Velociraptor memiliki panjang sekitar 1,5–2,07 m (4,9–6,8 kaki) dengan massa tubuh sekitar 14,1–19,7 kg (31–43 lb). Meskipun demikian, ia memiliki banyak ciri anatomi yang sama. Ia adalah karnivora berbulu berkaki dua dengan ekor panjang dan cakar berbentuk sabit yang membesar di setiap kaki belakangnya, yang diperkirakan digunakan untuk menjegal dan menahan mangsa. Velociraptor dapat dibedakan dari dromaeosaurid lain berdasarkan tengkoraknya yang panjang dan rendah, dengan moncong yang menghadap ke atas.

Velociraptor (biasa disebut "raptor") adalah salah satu genera dinosaurus yang paling dikenal masyarakat umum karena perannya yang menonjol dalam film Jurassic Park. Kenyataannya, Velociraptor kira-kira seukuran kalkun, jauh lebih kecil dari reptil yang panjangnya sekitar 2 m (6,6 kaki) dan berat 90 kg (200 lb) yang terlihat di novel dan film (yang didasarkan pada anggota genus terkait Deinonychus). Saat ini, Velociraptor terkenal di kalangan ahli paleontologi, dengan lebih dari selusin kerangka fosil yang telah dideskripsikan. Salah satu spesimen yang sangat terkenal melestarikan Velociraptor yang terkunci dalam pertempuran dengan Protoceratops.

![Velociraptor: Monster Sebenarnya vs Hollywood](/images/topics/dinosaurus.svg)
*Gambar: Velociraptor: Monster Sebenarnya vs Hollywood*

## Sejarah penemuan

Selama ekspedisi Museum Sejarah Alam Amerika ke Flaming Cliffs (Bayn Dzak atau Bayanzag) dari Formasi Djadochta, Gurun Gobi, pada tanggal 11 Agustus 1923, Peter Kaisen menemukan fosil Velociraptor pertama yang diketahui sains—tengkorak yang hancur namun lengkap, terkait dengan satu cakar manual dan ruas yang bersebelahan (AMNH 6515). Pada tahun 1924, presiden museum Henry Fairfield Osborn menetapkan tengkorak dan bagian manus sebagai spesimen tipe genus barunya, Velociraptor. Nama ini berasal dari kata Latin velox ('cepat') dan raptor ('perampok' atau 'penjarah') dan mengacu pada sifat kursorial hewan dan pola makan karnivora. Osborn menamai jenis spesies tersebut V. mongoliensis menurut negara asalnya. Awal tahun itu, Osborn secara informal menyebutkan hewan tersebut dalam artikel pers populer, dengan nama "Ovoraptor djadochtari" (jangan bingung dengan nama serupa Oviraptor), yang akhirnya berubah menjadi V. mongoliensis selama deskripsi formalnya.

Ketika tim Amerika Utara dilarang masuk ke Mongolia yang komunis selama Perang Dingin, ekspedisi ilmuwan Soviet dan Polandia, bekerja sama dengan rekan-rekan Mongolia, menemukan beberapa spesimen Velociraptor lagi. Yang paling terkenal adalah bagian dari spesimen "Fighting Dinosaurs" (MPC-D 100/25; sebelumnya IGM, GIN, atau GI SPS), ditemukan oleh tim Polandia-Mongolia pada tahun 1971. Fosil tersebut mengawetkan Velociraptor dalam pertempuran melawan Protoceratops. Ini dianggap sebagai harta nasional Mongolia, dan pada tahun 2000 dipinjamkan ke Museum Sejarah Alam Amerika di New York City untuk pameran sementara.

Antara tahun 1988 dan 1990, tim gabungan Tiongkok-Kanada menemukan sisa-sisa Velociraptor di Tiongkok utara. Ilmuwan Amerika kembali ke Mongolia pada tahun 1990, dan ekspedisi gabungan Mongolia-Amerika ke Gobi, yang dipimpin oleh Museum Sejarah Alam Amerika dan Akademi Ilmu Pengetahuan Mongolia, menemukan beberapa kerangka yang terpelihara dengan baik. Salah satu spesimen tersebut, MPC-D 100/980, dijuluki "Ichabodcraniosaurus" oleh tim Norell karena spesimen yang cukup lengkap ditemukan tanpa tengkoraknya (sebuah singgungan pada karakter Washington Irving, Ichabod Crane). Walaupun Norell dan Makovicky untuk sementara menganggapnya sebagai spesimen Velociraptor mongoliensis, ia dinamakan sebagai spesies baru Shri devi pada tahun 2021.

Pada tahun 1999, Rinchen Barsbold dan Halszka Osmólska melaporkan spesimen Velociraptor remaja (GIN atau IGM 100/2000), yang diwakili oleh kerangka lengkap termasuk tengkorak individu muda. Ditemukan di lokasi Tugriken Shireh Formasi Djadochta selama konteks Ekspedisi Paleontologi Mongolia-Jepang. Rekan penulis menyatakan bahwa penjelasan rinci tentang spesimen ini dan spesimen lainnya akan dipublikasikan di kemudian hari.

### Spesies tambahan

Rahang atas dan lakrimal (tulang penyangga gigi utama rahang atas, dan tulang yang membentuk tepi anterior rongga mata) yang ditemukan dari Formasi Bayan Mandahu pada tahun 1999 oleh Ekspedisi Dinosaurus Sino-Belgia ditemukan berkaitan dengan Velociraptor, tetapi tidak termasuk jenis spesies V. mongoliensis. Pascal Godefroit dan rekannya menamai tulang-tulang ini V. osmolskae (untuk ahli paleontologi Polandia Halszka Osmólska) pada tahun 2008. Namun, penelitian tahun 2013 mencatat bahwa meskipun "bentuk rahang atas yang memanjang di V. osmolskae mirip dengan V. mongoliensis," analisis filogenetik menemukan bahwa tulang tersebut lebih mirip dengan Linheraptor, sehingga membuat genus tersebut parafiletik; dengan demikian, V. osmolskae mungkin sebenarnya bukan milik genus Velociraptor dan memerlukan penilaian ulang.

Ahli paleontologi Mark A. Norell dan Peter J. Makovicky pada tahun 1997 mendeskripsikan spesimen V. mongoliensis yang baru dan terpelihara dengan baik, yaitu MPC-D 100/985 yang dikumpulkan dari lokasi Tugrik Shireh pada tahun 1993, dan MPC-D 100/986 yang dikumpulkan pada tahun 1993 dari lokasi Chimney Buttes. Tim secara singkat menyebutkan spesimen lain, MPC-D 100/982, yang pada saat publikasi ini masih belum dideskripsikan. Pada tahun 1999 Norell dan Makovicky memberikan lebih banyak wawasan mengenai anatomi Velociraptor dengan spesimen tambahan. Diantaranya, MPC-D 100/982 sebagian dideskripsikan dan digambarkan, dan dirujuk ke V. mongoliensis terutama berdasarkan kesamaan tengkorak dengan tengkorak holotipe, meskipun mereka menyatakan bahwa terdapat perbedaan antara daerah panggul spesimen ini dan spesimen Velociraptor lainnya. Spesimen yang relatif terpelihara dengan baik termasuk tengkoraknya ditemukan dan dikumpulkan pada tahun 1995 di lokasi Bayn Dzak (khususnya di sub-lokalitas "Gunung Berapi"). Martin Kundrát dalam abstrak tahun 2004 membandingkan neurokranium MPC-D 100/982 dengan spesimen Velociraptor lainnya, MPC-D 100/976. Dia menyimpulkan bahwa keseluruhan morfologi yang pertama lebih diturunkan (maju) dibandingkan yang kedua, menunjukkan bahwa mereka dapat mewakili taksa yang berbeda.

Mark J. Powers dalam tesis masternya tahun 2020 menjelaskan secara lengkap MPC-D 100/982, yang ia simpulkan mewakili spesies Velociraptor baru dan ketiga. Spesies yang dianggapnya berbeda ini dinyatakan berbeda dari spesies Velociraptor lainnya karena memiliki morfologi rahang atas yang dangkal. Powers dan rekannya juga pada tahun 2020 menggunakan analisis morfometrik untuk membandingkan beberapa rahang atas dromaeosaurid, dan menemukan rahang atas MPC-D 100/982 sangat berbeda dari spesimen yang dirujuk Velociraptor. Mereka mengindikasikan bahwa spesimen ini, berdasarkan hasil ini, mewakili spesies yang berbeda. Pada tahun 2021 Powers bersama tim menggunakan Analisis Komponen Utama untuk memisahkan dromaeosaurid maxillae, terutama menemukan bahwa MPC-D 100/982 berada di luar variabilitas instraspesifik V. mongoliensis, dengan alasan bahwa spesies tersebut berbeda. Mereka menilai baik V. mongoliensis maupun spesies baru ini terpisah secara ekologis berdasarkan anatomi tengkoraknya. Tim dalam abstrak tahun 2021 lainnya memperkuat kembali pemisahan tingkat spesies, dengan mencatat bahwa perbedaan tambahan dapat ditemukan di bagian belakang.

## Keterangan

Velociraptor adalah dromaeosaurid berukuran kecil hingga sedang, dengan orang dewasa berukuran panjang antara 1,5–2,07 m (4,9–6,8 kaki), tinggi pinggul sekitar 0,5 m (1,6 kaki), dan berat sekitar 14,1–19,7 kg (31–43 lb). Beberapa perkiraan menunjukkan bahwa Velociraptor mungkin lebih besar, kemungkinan mencapai panjang sekitar 2,5 m (8 kaki) dan berat hingga 28 kg (60 lb).

Kenop bulu ayam yang menonjol—tempat menempelnya bulu "sayap" dan indikator langsung penutup bulu—telah dilaporkan dari ulna spesimen Velociraptor tunggal (IGM 100/981), yang mewakili hewan yang diperkirakan memiliki panjang 1,5 m (4,9 kaki) dan berat 15 kg (33 lb). Jarak dari 6 kenop yang diawetkan menunjukkan bahwa mungkin ada 8 kenop tambahan, sehingga totalnya ada 14 kenop bulu ayam yang mengembangkan bulu sekunder besar (bulu "sayap" yang berasal dari lengan bawah). Namun, nomor spesimen telah diperbaiki menjadi IGM 100/3503 dan rujukannya ke Velociraptor mungkin memerlukan evaluasi ulang, menunggu studi lebih lanjut. Walaupun begitu, terdapat bukti filogenetik yang kuat dari kerabat dromaeosaurid lain yang menunjukkan adanya bulu di Velociraptor, termasuk dromaeosaurid seperti Daurlong, Microraptor, atau Zhenyuanlong.

### Tengkorak

Tengkorak Velociraptor agak memanjang dan panjangnya mencapai 23 cm (9,1 in). Bentuknya unik melengkung ke atas di daerah moncong, cekung di permukaan atas, dan cembung di permukaan bawah. Moncongnya, yang menempati sekitar 60% dari keseluruhan panjang tengkorak, sangat sempit dan sebagian besar dibentuk oleh tulang hidung, premaxilla, dan maxilla. Premaxilla adalah tulang paling anterior di tengkorak, dan lebih panjang daripada tinggi. Sementara ujung posteriornya bergabung dengan hidung, badan utama premaxilla menyentuh rahang atas. Rahang atas berbentuk hampir segitiga dan merupakan elemen terbesar dari moncongnya. Pada bagian tengah atau badan utamanya terdapat cekungan yang menimbulkan lubang kecil berbentuk lonjong hingga melingkar yang disebut fenestra rahang atas. Padahal di depan fenestra ini ada dua bukaan kecil yang disebut fenestra promaxillary. Batas posterior rahang atas membentuk (terutama) fenestra antorbital, salah satu dari beberapa lubang besar di tengkorak. Baik premaxilla maupun maxilla memiliki beberapa alveoli (soket gigi) di permukaan bawahnya. Di atas rahang atas dan bersentuhan dengan premaksila terdapat tulang hidung. Itu adalah tulang tipis/sempit dan memanjang yang berkontribusi pada permukaan atas moncong. Bersama-sama, tulang premaxilla dan hidung membentuk naris atau narial fenestra (lubang hidung), yang relatif besar dan melingkar. Ujung posterior hidung disatukan oleh tulang frontal dan lakrimal.

Daerah belakang atau posterior tengkorak dibangun oleh tulang frontal, lakrimal, postorbital, jugal, parietal, kuadrat, dan quadratojugal. Bagian depannya adalah elemen besar, berbentuk agak persegi panjang jika dilihat dari atas. Di ujung posteriornya, tulang ini bersentuhan dengan parietal, dan elemen tersebut merupakan bagian utama atap tengkorak. Lakrimal adalah tulang berbentuk T dan tubuh utamanya tipis dan halus. Ujung bawahnya bertemu dengan jugal (sering disebut tulang pipi), yang merupakan elemen besar berbentuk sub-segitiga. Batas bawahnya lurus/horizontal. Postorbital terletak tepat di atas jugal: tulang berbentuk T yang kekar dan kuat. Secara keseluruhan, orbital atau fenestra orbital (rongga mata)—dibentuk oleh lakrimal, jugal, frontal, dan postorbital—berbentuk besar dan hampir melingkar, lebih panjang daripada tinggi. Jika dilihat dari atas, terdapat sepasang lubang besar dan membulat di dekat bagian belakang tengkorak (fenestrae temporal), yang komponen utamanya adalah postorbital dan squamosal. Di belakang jugal, tulang berbentuk T terbalik (juga terlihat pada dromaeosaurid lain), yang dikenal sebagai quadratojugal, dikembangkan. Sementara ujung atas quadratojugal bergabung dengan skuamosa, suatu elemen yang bentuknya tidak beraturan, sisi dalamnya bertemu dengan kuadrat. Yang terakhir ini sangat penting untuk artikulasi dengan rahang bawah. Tulang paling posterior adalah tulang oksipital dan proyeksinya adalah kondilus oksipital: tonjolan bulat dan bulat yang bertemu dengan vertebra pertama leher.

Rahang bawah Velociraptor sebagian besar terdiri dari tulang gigi, splenial, sudut, surangular, dan artikular. Dokter gigi adalah elemen yang sangat panjang, melengkung lemah, dan sempit yang mengembangkan beberapa alveoli di permukaan atasnya. Di ujung posteriornya bertemu dengan bentuk persegi panjang. Ia memiliki lubang kecil di dekat ujung posteriornya, yang disebut foramen surangular atau fenestra. Kedua tulang tersebut merupakan elemen terbesar dari rahang bawah Velociraptor, yang berkontribusi terhadap keseluruhan panjangnya. Di bawah mereka ada splenial dan sudut yang lebih kecil, yang diartikulasikan erat satu sama lain. Artikular, terletak di sisi dalam surangular, adalah elemen kecil yang menghubungkan kuadrat tengkorak atas, memungkinkan artikulasi dengan rahang bawah. Sebuah lubang memanjang hampir berbentuk oval berkembang di tengah rahang bawah (fenestra mandibula), dan dihasilkan oleh sambungan tulang gigi, surangular, dan sudut.

Gigi Velociraptor cukup homodont (bentuknya sama) dan memiliki beberapa dentikel (gerigi), masing-masing bergerigi lebih kuat di bagian belakang daripada bagian depan. Premaxilla memiliki 4 alveoli (artinya 4 gigi telah berkembang), dan maxilla memiliki 11 alveoli. Di dokter gigi, terdapat antara 14-15 alveoli. Semua gigi yang ada di premaxilla memiliki lengkungan yang buruk, dan dua gigi pertama adalah yang terpanjang, dengan gigi kedua memiliki karakteristik berukuran besar. Gigi rahang atas lebih ramping, melengkung, dan yang paling menonjol, ujung bawah lebih bergerigi dibandingkan gigi atas.

### Kerangka pascakranial

Lengan Velociraptor dibentuk oleh humerus (tulang lengan atas), radius dan ulna (tulang lengan bawah), serta manus (tangan). Velociraptor, seperti dromaeosaurid lainnya, memiliki manus besar dengan tiga jari memanjang (jari), yang berakhir dengan ungual (tulang cakar) yang sangat melengkung yang konstruksi dan kelenturannya mirip dengan tulang sayap burung modern. Digit kedua adalah yang terpanjang dari tiga digit yang ada, sedangkan digit pertama adalah yang terpendek. Struktur tulang karpal (pergelangan tangan) mencegah pronasi pergelangan tangan dan memaksa manus dipegang dengan permukaan palmar menghadap ke dalam (medial), bukan ke bawah. Anatomi pes (kaki) Velociraptor terdiri dari metatarsus—sebuah elemen besar yang terdiri dari tiga metatarsal yang ukuran metatarsal pertama sangat mengecil—dan empat jari yang membentuk ungual besar. Digit pertama, seperti pada theropoda lainnya, adalah dewclaw kecil. Digit kedua, yang membuat Velociraptor paling terkenal, telah banyak dimodifikasi dan ditarik keluar dari tanah, yang menyebabkan Velociraptor dan dromaeosaurid lainnya hanya berjalan dengan digit ketiga dan keempat. Ia memiliki cakar yang relatif besar dan berbentuk sabit, khas dinosaurus dromaeosaurid dan troodontid. Cakar yang membesar ini, yang dapat tumbuh hingga panjang lebih dari 6,5 cm (2,6 inci) di sekitar tepi luarnya, kemungkinan besar merupakan alat predator yang digunakan untuk menahan mangsa yang sedang berjuang.

Seperti pada dromaeosaurus lainnya, ekor Velociraptor memiliki prezygapophyses (tonjolan tulang panjang) pada permukaan atas tulang belakang, serta tendon keras di bawahnya. Prezygapophyses dimulai pada vertebra ekor kesepuluh (ekor) dan meluas ke depan untuk menopang empat hingga sepuluh vertebra tambahan, tergantung pada posisi di ekor. Dulunya dianggap membuat ekor menjadi kaku sepenuhnya, memaksa seluruh ekor bertindak sebagai satu kesatuan seperti batang. Namun, setidaknya satu spesimen telah mempertahankan serangkaian tulang ekor utuh yang melengkung ke samping menjadi bentuk S, menunjukkan bahwa terdapat fleksibilitas horizontal yang jauh lebih besar daripada yang diperkirakan sebelumnya.

## Klasifikasi

Velociraptor adalah anggota kelompok Eudromaeosauria, subkelompok turunan dari keluarga Dromaeosauridae yang lebih besar. Ia sering ditempatkan dalam subfamilinya sendiri, Velociraptorinae. Dalam taksonomi filogenetik, Velociraptorinae biasanya didefinisikan sebagai "semua dromaeosaurus yang berkerabat dekat dengan Velociraptor dibandingkan dengan Dromaeosaurus." Namun klasifikasi dromaeosaurid sangat bervariasi. Awalnya, subfamili Velociraptorinae didirikan semata-mata untuk menampung Velociraptor. Analisis lain sering kali mencakup genera lain, biasanya Deinonychus dan Saurornitholestes, dan yang terbaru adalah Tsaagan. Beberapa penelitian yang diterbitkan pada tahun 2010-an, termasuk versi analisis yang diperluas yang menemukan dukungan untuk Velociraptorinae, gagal untuk menyelesaikannya sebagai kelompok yang berbeda, melainkan menyatakan bahwa itu adalah tingkat parafiletik yang memunculkan Dromaeosaurinae.

Ketika pertama kali dideskripsikan pada tahun 1924, Velociraptor ditempatkan dalam keluarga Megalosauridae, seperti halnya sebagian besar dinosaurus karnivora pada saat itu (Megalosauridae, seperti Megalosaurus, berfungsi sebagai semacam takson 'tempat sampah', tempat banyak spesies yang tidak berkerabat dikelompokkan menjadi satu). Seiring bertambahnya penemuan dinosaurus, Velociraptor kemudian dikenal sebagai dromaeosaurid. Semua dromaeosaurid juga telah dirujuk ke keluarga Archaeopterygidae oleh setidaknya satu penulis (yang pada dasarnya menjadikan Velociraptor burung yang tidak bisa terbang). Dahulu, spesies dromaeosaurid lain, termasuk Deinonychus antirrhopus dan Saurornitholestes langstoni, terkadang diklasifikasikan dalam genus Velociraptor. Karena Velociraptor adalah yang pertama diberi nama, spesies ini berganti nama menjadi Velociraptor antirrhopus dan V. langstoni. Pada tahun 2008, satu-satunya spesies Velociraptor yang dikenali saat ini adalah V. mongoliensis dan V. osmolskae. Namun, beberapa penelitian menemukan "V." osmolskae berkerabat jauh dengan V. mongoliensis.

Berikut hasil filogeni Eudromaeosauria berdasarkan analisis filogenetik yang dilakukan James G. Napoli dan tim pada tahun 2021 saat mendeskripsikan Kuru yang menunjukkan posisi Velociraptor:

### Bulu

Pada tahun 2007 Alan H. Turner dan rekannya melaporkan keberadaan enam kenop bulu ayam di ulna spesimen Velociraptor yang dirujuk (IGM 100/981) dari lokasi Ukhaa Tolgod di Formasi Djadochta. Turner dan rekannya menafsirkan keberadaan bulu pada Velociraptor sebagai bukti yang menentang gagasan bahwa maniraptoran yang lebih besar dan tidak bisa terbang kehilangan bulunya karena ukuran tubuh yang lebih besar. Selain itu, mereka mencatat bahwa tombol-tombol bulu ayam hampir tidak pernah ditemukan pada spesies burung yang tidak bisa terbang saat ini, dan bahwa kehadiran mereka di Velociraptor (diduga tidak bisa terbang karena ukurannya yang relatif besar dan kaki depan yang pendek) adalah bukti bahwa nenek moyang dromaeosaurid bisa terbang, membuat Velociraptor dan anggota besar keluarga ini tidak bisa terbang untuk kedua kalinya, meskipun ada kemungkinan bulu sayap besar yang disimpulkan pada nenek moyang Velociraptor memiliki tujuan selain terbang. Bulu Velociraptor yang tidak bisa terbang mungkin digunakan untuk pajangan, untuk menutupi sarangnya saat merenung, atau untuk menambah kecepatan dan daya dorong saat berlari di lereng yang miring.

Karena kehadiran dromaeosaurid lain di Ukhaa Tolgod, Tsaagan, Napoli dan tim telah mencatat bahwa rujukan spesimen ini ke Velociraptor saat ini sedang menjalani pemeriksaan ulang.

### Indra

Pemeriksaan pada endokranium Velociraptor menunjukkan bahwa ia mampu mendeteksi dan mendengar rentang frekuensi suara yang luas (2.368–3.965 Hz) dan sebagai hasilnya dapat melacak mangsa dengan mudah. Pemeriksaan endokranium juga semakin memperkuat teori bahwa dromaeosaurus adalah predator yang gesit dan gesit. Bukti fosil yang menunjukkan bahwa Velociraptor sedang memulung juga menunjukkan bahwa ia adalah hewan oportunistik dan aktif menjadi predator, memakan bangkai pada saat kekeringan atau kelaparan, jika kesehatannya buruk, atau bergantung pada usia hewan tersebut.

### Makanan

Pada tahun 2020, Powers dan rekannya memeriksa ulang rahang atas beberapa taksa eudromaeosaurus dan menyimpulkan bahwa sebagian besar eudromaeosaurus Asia dan Amerika Utara dipisahkan berdasarkan morfologi moncong dan strategi ekologi. Mereka menemukan rahang atas sebagai referensi yang dapat diandalkan ketika menyimpulkan bentuk premaxilla dan keseluruhan moncong. Misalnya, sebagian besar spesies Asia memiliki moncong memanjang berdasarkan rahang atas (yaitu velociraptorines), yang menunjukkan pola makan selektif pada Velociraptor dan kerabatnya, seperti memangsa mangsa kecil dan cepat. Sebaliknya, sebagian besar eudromaeosaurus Amerika Utara, kebanyakan dromaeosaurus, memiliki morfologi rahang atas yang kuat dan dalam. Walau bagaimanapun, dromeosurine Achillobator yang besar adalah pengecualian unik untuk taksa Asia dengan rahang atasnya yang dalam.

Manabu Sakamoto pada tahun 2022 melakukan kerangka pemodelan prediktif filogenetik Bayesian untuk memperkirakan parameter otot rahang dan kekuatan gigitan beberapa archosaurus yang telah punah, berdasarkan lebar tengkorak dan hubungan filogenetik antar kelompok. Di antara taksa yang dipelajari, Velociraptor dinilai dengan kekuatan gigitan 304 N, lebih rendah dibandingkan dromaeosaurid lain seperti Dromaeosaurus (885 N) atau Deinonychus (706 N).

### Perilaku predator

Spesimen "Fighting Dinosaurs", yang ditemukan pada tahun 1971, mengawetkan Velociraptor mongoliensis dan Protoceratops andrewsi dalam pertempuran dan memberikan bukti langsung adanya perilaku predator. Saat awal diberitakan, ada hipotesis bahwa kedua hewan tersebut tenggelam. Namun, karena hewan-hewan tersebut terawetkan di endapan bukit pasir kuno, kini diperkirakan bahwa hewan-hewan tersebut terkubur di dalam pasir, baik dari bukit pasir yang runtuh atau dalam badai pasir. Pemakaman pasti dilakukan dengan sangat cepat, dilihat dari pose-pose pengawetan hewan-hewan tersebut yang terlihat seperti aslinya. Bagian dari Protoceratops hilang, yang dipandang sebagai bukti pemulungan oleh hewan lain. Perbandingan antara cincin scleral Velociraptor, Protoceratops, dan burung serta reptil modern menunjukkan bahwa Velociraptor mungkin aktif di malam hari, sedangkan Protoceratops mungkin bersifat cathemeral, aktif sepanjang hari dalam interval pendek, menunjukkan bahwa pertarungan mungkin terjadi saat senja atau saat kondisi cahaya redup.

Cakar khasnya, pada jari kedua dromaeosaurid, secara tradisional digambarkan sebagai senjata tebas; dugaan penggunaannya adalah untuk memotong dan mengeluarkan isi perut mangsanya. Dalam spesimen "Fighting Dinosaurs", Velociraptor terletak di bawahnya, dengan salah satu cakar sabitnya tampaknya tertanam di tenggorokan mangsanya, sementara paruh Protoceratops dijepit di kaki depan kanan penyerangnya. ## Poin-Poin Kunci

- Selama ekspedisi Museum Sejarah Alam Amerika ke Flaming Cliffs (Bayn Dzak atau Bayanzag) dari Formasi Djadochta, Gurun Gobi, pada tanggal 11 Agustus 1923, Peter Kaisen menemukan fosil Velociraptor pertama yang diketahui sains—tengkorak yang hancur namun lengkap, terkait dengan satu cakar manual dan ruas yang bersebelahan (AMNH 6515).
- Rahang atas dan lakrimal (tulang penyangga gigi utama rahang atas, dan tulang yang membentuk tepi anterior rongga mata) yang ditemukan dari Formasi Bayan Mandahu pada tahun 1999 oleh Ekspedisi Dinosaurus Sino-Belgia ditemukan berkaitan dengan Velociraptor, tetapi tidak termasuk jenis spesies V.
- Velociraptor adalah dromaeosaurid berukuran kecil hingga sedang, dengan orang dewasa berukuran panjang antara 1,5–2,07 m (4,9–6,8 kaki), tinggi pinggul sekitar 0,5 m (1,6 kaki), dan berat sekitar 14,1–19,7 kg (31–43 lb).
- Tengkorak Velociraptor agak memanjang dan panjangnya mencapai 23 cm (9,1 in).
- Lengan Velociraptor dibentuk oleh humerus (tulang lengan atas), radius dan ulna (tulang lengan bawah), serta manus (tangan).
- Velociraptor adalah anggota kelompok Eudromaeosauria, subkelompok turunan dari keluarga Dromaeosauridae yang lebih besar.

## Kesimpulan

Dinosaurus bukan sekadar monster dari film; mereka adalah mahakarya evolusi yang mengisi planet ini selama puluhan juta generasi. Semakin kita mempelajarinya, semakin kita menyadari bahwa dunia purba itu penuh dengan kejutan, dan banyak cerita yang masih terkubur menunggu untuk ditemukan.

en.contentMarkdown:
# Velociraptor: The Real Monster vs Hollywood

Few creatures ignite the human imagination like dinosaurs. These animals ruled Earth's landmasses for more than 165 million years, far longer than humans have existed. This article brings you closer to them, from anatomy and behavior to the environments that shaped their lives in the Mesozoic Era.

Velociraptor (; lit. 'swift thief') is a genus of small dromaeosaurid dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous epoch, about 75 million to 71 million years ago (Mya). Two species are currently recognized, although others have been assigned in the past. The type species is V. mongoliensis, named and described in 1924. Fossils of this species have been discovered in the Djadochta Formation, Mongolia. A second species, V. osmolskae, was named in 2008 for skull material from the Bayan Mandahu Formation, China. A possible record is known from the Nemegt Formation.

Smaller than other dromaeosaurids like Deinonychus and Achillobator, Velociraptor was about 1.5–2.07 m (4.9–6.8 ft) long with a body mass of around 14.1–19.7 kg (31–43 lb). It nevertheless shared many of the same anatomical features. It was a bipedal, feathered carnivore with a long tail and an enlarged sickle-shaped claw on each hindfoot, which is thought to have been used to tackle and restrain prey. Velociraptor can be distinguished from other dromaeosaurids by its long and low skull, with an upturned snout.

Velociraptor (commonly referred to as "raptor") is one of the dinosaur genera most familiar to the general public due to its prominent role in the Jurassic Park films. In reality, Velociraptor was roughly the size of a turkey, considerably smaller than the approximately 2 m (6.6 ft) long and 90 kg (200 lb) reptiles seen in the novels and films (which were based on members of the related genus Deinonychus). Today, Velociraptor is well known to paleontologists, with over a dozen described fossil skeletons. One particularly famous specimen preserves a Velociraptor locked in combat with a Protoceratops.

![Velociraptor: The Real Monster vs Hollywood](/images/topics/dinosaurus.svg)
*Gambar: Velociraptor: The Real Monster vs Hollywood*

## History of discovery

During an American Museum of Natural History expedition to the Flaming Cliffs (Bayn Dzak or Bayanzag) of the Djadochta Formation, Gobi Desert, on 11 August 1923, Peter Kaisen discovered the first Velociraptor fossil known to science—a crushed but complete skull, associated with one manual claw and adjoining phalanges (AMNH 6515). In 1924, museum president Henry Fairfield Osborn designated the skull and part of the manus as the type specimen of his new genus, Velociraptor. This name is derived from the Latin words velox ('swift') and raptor ('robber' or 'plunderer') and refers to the animal's cursorial nature and carnivorous diet. Osborn named the type species V. mongoliensis after its country of origin. Earlier that year, Osborn had informally mentioned the animal in a popular press article, under the name "Ovoraptor djadochtari" (not to be confused with the similarly named Oviraptor), eventually changed into V. mongoliensis during its formal description.

While North American teams were shut out of communist Mongolia during the Cold War, expeditions by Soviet and Polish scientists, in collaboration with Mongolian colleagues, recovered several more specimens of Velociraptor. The most famous is part of the "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen (MPC-D 100/25; formerly IGM, GIN, or GI SPS), discovered by a Polish-Mongolian team in 1971. The fossil preserves a Velociraptor in battle against a Protoceratops. It is considered a national treasure of Mongolia, and in 2000 it was loaned to the American Museum of Natural History in New York City for a temporary exhibition.

Between 1988 and 1990, a joint Chinese-Canadian team discovered Velociraptor remains in northern China. American scientists returned to Mongolia in 1990, and a joint Mongolian-American expedition to the Gobi, led by the American Museum of Natural History and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences, turned up several well-preserved skeletons. One such specimen, MPC-D 100/980, was nicknamed "Ichabodcraniosaurus" by Norell's team because the fairly complete specimen was found without its skull (an allusion to the Washington Irving character Ichabod Crane). While Norell and Makovicky provisionally considered it a specimen of Velociraptor mongoliensis, it was named as a new species Shri devi in 2021.

In 1999, Rinchen Barsbold and Halszka Osmólska reported a juvenile Velociraptor specimen (GIN or IGM 100/2000), represented by a complete skeleton including the skull of a young individual. It was found at the Tugriken Shireh locality of the Djadochta Formation during the context of the Mongolian-Japanese Palaeontological Expeditions. The coauthors stated that detailed descriptions of this and other specimens would be published at a later date.

### Additional species

Maxillae and a lacrimal (the main tooth-bearing bones of the upper jaw, and the bone that forms the anterior margin of the eye socket, respectively) recovered from the Bayan Mandahu Formation in 1999 by the Sino-Belgian Dinosaur Expeditions were found to pertain to Velociraptor, but not to the type species V. mongoliensis. Pascal Godefroit and colleagues named these bones V. osmolskae (for Polish paleontologist Halszka Osmólska) in 2008. However, the 2013 study noted that while "the elongate shape of the maxilla in V. osmolskae is similar to that of V. mongoliensis," phylogenetic analysis found it to be closer to Linheraptor, making the genus paraphyletic; thus, V. osmolskae might not actually belong to the genus Velociraptor and requires reassessment.

Paleontologists Mark A. Norell and Peter J. Makovicky in 1997 described new and well preserved specimens of V. mongoliensis, namely MPC-D 100/985 collected from the Tugrik Shireh locality in 1993, and MPC-D 100/986 collected in 1993 from the Chimney Buttes locality. The team briefly mentioned another specimen, MPC-D 100/982, which by the time of this publication remained undescribed. In 1999 Norell and Makovicky provided more insights into the anatomy of Velociraptor with additional specimens. Among these, MPC-D 100/982 was partially described and figured, and referred to V. mongoliensis mainly based on cranial similarities with the holotype skull, although they stated that differences were present between the pelvic region of this specimen and other Velociraptor specimens. This relatively well-preserved specimen including the skull was discovered and collected in 1995 at the Bayn Dzak locality (specifically at the "Volcano" sub-locality). Martin Kundrát in a 2004 abstract compared the neurocranium of MPC-D 100/982 to another Velociraptor specimen, MPC-D 100/976. He concluded that the overall morphology of the former was more derived (advanced) than the latter, suggesting that they could represent distinct taxa.

Mark J. Powers in his 2020 master thesis fully described MPC-D 100/982, which he concluded to represent a new and third species of Velociraptor. This species, which he considered distinct, was stated to mainly differ from other Velociraptor species in having a shallow maxilla morphology. Powers and colleagues also in 2020 used morphometric analyses to compare several dromaeosaurid maxillae, and found the maxilla of MPC-D 100/982 to strongly differ from specimens referred to Velociraptor. They indicated that this specimen, based on these results, represents a different species. In 2021 Powers with team used Principal Component Analysis to separate dromaeosaurid maxillae, most notably finding that MPC-D 100/982 falls outside the instraspecific variability of V. mongoliensis, arguing for a distinct species. They considered that both V. mongoliensis and this new species were ecologically separated based on their skull anatomy. The team in another 2021 abstract reinforced again the species-level separation, noting that additional differences can be found in the hindlimbs.

## Description

Velociraptor was a small to medium-sized dromaeosaurid, with adults measuring between 1.5–2.07 m (4.9–6.8 ft) long, approximately 0.5 m (1.6 ft) high at the hips, and weighing about 14.1–19.7 kg (31–43 lb). Some estimates suggest that Velociraptor may have been larger, possibly reaching lengths of about 2.5 m (8 ft) and weighing up to 28 kg (60 lb).

Prominent quill knobs—attachment site of "wing" feathers and direct indicator of a feather covering—have been reported from the ulna of a single Velociraptor specimen (IGM 100/981), which represents an animal of estimated 1.5 m (4.9 ft) long and 15 kg (33 lb) in weight. The spacing of 6 preserved knobs suggests that 8 additional knobs may have been present, giving a total of 14 quill knobs that developed large secondaries ("wing" feathers stemming from the forearm). However, the specimen number has been corrected to IGM 100/3503 and its referral to Velociraptor may require reevaluation, pending further study. Nevertheless, there is strong phylogenetic evidence from other dromaeosaurid relatives that indicates the presence of feathers in Velociraptor, including dromaeosaurids such as Daurlong, Microraptor, or Zhenyuanlong.

### Skull

The skull of Velociraptor was rather elongated and grew up to 23 cm (9.1 in) long. It was uniquely up-curved at the snout region, concave on the upper surface, and convex on the lower surface. The snout, which occupied about 60% of the entire skull length, was notably narrow and mainly formed by the nasal, premaxilla, and maxilla bones. The premaxilla was the anteriormost bone in the skull, and it was longer than taller. While its posterior end joined the nasal, the main body of the premaxilla touched the maxilla. The maxilla was nearly triangular in shape and the largest element of the snout. On its center or main body, there was a depression developing a small oval to circular-shaped hole, called maxillary fenestra. Though in front of this fenestra were two small openings, referred to as promaxillary fenestrae. The posterior border of the maxilla formed (predominantly) the antorbital fenestra, one of the several large holes in the skull. Both premaxilla and maxilla had several alveoli (tooth sockets) on their bottom surfaces. Above the maxilla and making contact with the premaxilla, there was the nasal bone. It was a thin/narrow and elongated bone contributing to the top surface of the snout. Together, both premaxilla and nasal bones gave form to the naris or narial fenestra (nostril opening), which was relatively large and circular. The posterior end of the nasal was joined by the frontal and lacrimal bones.

The back or posterior region of the skull was built by the frontal, lacrimal, postorbital, jugal, parietal, quadrate, and quadratojugal bones. The frontal was large element, having a vaguely rectangular shape when seen from above. On its posterior end, this bone was in contact with the parietal, and such elements were the main bodies of the skull roof. The lacrimal was a T-shaped bone and its main body was thin and delicated. Its lower end meet the jugal (often called cheek bone), which was a large, sub-triangular-shaped element. Its lower border was notably straight/horizontal. The postorbital was located just above the jugal: a stocky and strongly T-shaped bone. As a whole, the orbit or orbital fenestra (eye socket)—formed by the lacrimal, jugal, frontal, and postorbital—was large and near circular in shape, being longer than taller. When seen from above, a pair of large and markedly rounded holes were present near the rear of the skull (the temporal fenestrae), whose main components were the postorbital and squamosal. Behind the jugal, an inverted T-shaped bone (also seen in other dromaeosaurids), known as the quadratojugal, was developed. While the upper end of the quadratojugal joined the squamosal, an irregularly-shaped element, its inner side meet the quadrate. The latter was of great importance for the articulation with the lower jaw. The posteriormost bone was the occipital bone and its projection the occipital condyle: a rounded and bulbous protuberance that meet the first vertebra of the neck.

The lower jaw of Velociraptor comprised mainly the dentary, splenial, angular, surangular, and articular bones. The dentary was a very long, weakly curved, and narrow element that developed several alveoli on its top surface. On its posterior end, it meet the surangular. It had a small hole near its posterior end, called surangular foramen or fenestra. Both bones were the largest elements of the lower jaw of Velociraptor, contributing to virtually its entire length. Below them were the smaller splenial and angular, closely articulated to each other. The articular, located on the inner side of the surangular, was a small element that joined the quadrate of the upper skull, enabling the articulation with the lower jaw. An elongated, near oval-shaped hole was developed in the center of the lower jaw (the mandibular fenestra), and it was produced by the joint of the dentary, surangular, and angular bones.

The teeth of Velociraptor were fairly homodont (equal in shape) and had several denticles (serrations), each more strongly serrated on the back edge than the front. The premaxilla had 4 alveoli (meaning that 4 teeth were developed), and the maxilla had 11 alveoli. At the dentary, between 14–15 alveoli were present. All teeth present at the premaxilla were poorly curved, and the two first teeth were the longest, with the second having a characteristic large size. The maxillary teeth were more slender, recurved, and most notably, the lower end was strongly more serrated than the upper one.

### Postcranial skeleton

The arm of Velociraptor was formed by the humerus (upper arm bone), radius and ulna (forearm bones), and manus (hand). Velociraptor, like other dromaeosaurids, had a large manus with three elongated digits (fingers), which ended up in strongly curved unguals (claw bones) that were similar in construction and flexibility to the wing bones of modern birds. The second digit was the longest of the three digits present, while the first was shortest. The structure of the carpal (wrist) bones prevented pronation of the wrist and forced the manus to be held with the palmar surface facing inward (medially), not downward. The pes (foot) anatomy of Velociraptor consisted of the metatarsus—a large element composed of three metatarsals of which the first one was extremely reduced in size—and four digits that developed large unguals. The first digit, as in other theropods, was a small dewclaw. The second digit, for which Velociraptor is most famous, was highly modified and held retracted off the ground, which caused Velociraptor and other dromaeosaurids to walk on only their third and fourth digits. It bore a relatively large, sickle-shaped claw, typical of dromaeosaurid and troodontid dinosaurs. This enlarged claw, which could grow to over 6.5 cm (2.6 in) long around its outer edge, was most likely a predatory device used to restrain struggling prey.

As in other dromaeosaurs, Velociraptor tails had prezygapophyses (long bony projections) on the upper surfaces of the vertebrae, as well as ossified tendons underneath. The prezygapophyses began on the tenth tail (caudal) vertebra and extended forward to brace four to ten additional vertebrae, depending on position in the tail. These were once thought to fully stiffen the tail, forcing the entire tail to act as a single rod-like unit. However, at least one specimen has preserved a series of intact tail vertebrae curved sideways into an S-shape, suggesting that there was considerably more horizontal flexibility than once thought.

## Classification

Velociraptor is a member of the group Eudromaeosauria, a derived sub-group of the larger family Dromaeosauridae. It is often placed within its own subfamily, Velociraptorinae. In phylogenetic taxonomy, Velociraptorinae is usually defined as "all dromaeosaurs more closely related to Velociraptor than to Dromaeosaurus." However, dromaeosaurid classification is highly variable. Originally, the subfamily Velociraptorinae was erected solely to contain Velociraptor. Other analyses have often included other genera, usually Deinonychus and Saurornitholestes, and more recently Tsaagan. Several studies published during the 2010s, including expanded versions of the analyses that found support for Velociraptorinae, have failed to resolve it as a distinct group, but rather have suggested it is a paraphyletic grade which gave rise to the Dromaeosaurinae.

When first described in 1924, Velociraptor was placed in the family Megalosauridae, as was the case with most carnivorous dinosaurs at the time (Megalosauridae, like Megalosaurus, functioned as a sort of 'wastebin' taxon, where many unrelated species were grouped together). As dinosaur discoveries multiplied, Velociraptor was later recognized as a dromaeosaurid. All dromaeosaurids have also been referred to the family Archaeopterygidae by at least one author (which would, in effect, make Velociraptor a flightless bird). In the past, other dromaeosaurid species, including Deinonychus antirrhopus and Saurornitholestes langstoni, have sometimes been classified in the genus Velociraptor. Since Velociraptor was the first to be named, these species were renamed Velociraptor antirrhopus and V. langstoni. As of 2008, the only currently recognized species of Velociraptor are V. mongoliensis and V. osmolskae. However, several studies have found "V." osmolskae to be distantly related to V. mongoliensis.
