# Shinto: Eight Million Kami and Humanity's Bond with Nature


![Shinto — ilustrasi topik](/images/topics/torii.svg)
*Image: Shinto*

Imagine standing before a glowing vermillion gate rising straight out of the sea—the **torii** of Itsukushima Shrine in Hiroshima Prefecture, one of Japan's most famous. At high tide, the gate appears to float on the bay, separating the human world from something far greater. Behind it, a green island stands quietly. The Japanese believe: passing through a torii means stepping into the realm of the ***kami***—spirits that inhabit all things.

This is **Shinto**, Japan's indigenous religion, strange and captivating at once: it has no single founder, no canonical scripture, not even an agreed-upon definition. Yet it is numerically Japan's largest religion, with around **100,000 public shrines** scattered from Hokkaido to Okinawa. How can a belief system without doctrine survive for millennia? The answer may lie precisely in that absence of doctrine.

## What Is Shinto? A Religion Without a Founder

Compare it with the major religions we usually know. Christianity has Jesus, Islam has Muhammad, Buddhism has Siddhartha Gautama. All have founding figures and scriptures codifying rules of life. Shinto? It has neither. The word *Shinto* is often broadly translated as *"the way of the kami"*—not a set of rules but a *way*.

Scholars even struggle to define it. According to Joseph Cali and John Dougill, if there were one broad definition worth proposing, it would be that *"Shinto is a belief in kami"*—the supernatural entities at the center of the religion. Japanologist Helen Hardacre wrote that Shinto encompasses doctrines, institutions, ritual, and communal life based on kami worship.

Fascinatingly, many practitioners don't call themselves adherents of a "religion." They prefer seeing Shinto as a *way*—custom or tradition handed down through generations. Scholars rarely use the term "Shintoist" either, since it has no direct equivalent in Japanese. There's even sharp academic debate: historian Kuroda Toshio concluded that *"before modern times Shinto did not exist as an independent religion,"* while several scholars argue Shinto as a distinct religion was essentially "invented" in the 19th century Meiji era.

But whatever the label, one thing is certain: veneration of the kami has pulsed through Japanese soil long before the word "Shinto" became popular.

### A Friendly Polytheism

Shinto is **polytheistic** and **animistic**—believing in many gods and spirits within all things. Unlike Western religions that tend toward exclusivity, Japan has long accepted practicing multiple religions simultaneously. Japanese faith is deeply **pluralistic**: you can be born with Shinto ritual, marry in a white Christian church, and be buried with Buddhist rites—without anyone feeling contradiction.

This proves Shinto isn't about "right vs wrong" but about harmony. It places little emphasis on specific moral codes or particular afterlife beliefs—its focus is simpler and more humane: how to maintain good relations with the world around us.

## Kami: Spirits Inhabiting Everything

The core of Shinto's entire architecture is the concept of ***kami***. Simply put, kami can be understood as spirits or supernatural entities believed to inhabit all things—including forces of nature and prominent landscape features. A gaping volcano? It has its kami. An eight-hundred-year-old cedar tree? A kami dwells there. A roaring waterfall, a charismatic boulder, the sun that feeds rice paddies—all can be homes for kami.

"Thousands" in this article's title is actually an understatement. Japanese tradition speaks of ***yaoyorozu no kami***—eight million kami—an idiom meaning "countless." Eight million isn't a census; it's a poetic way of saying the world is crowded with divine presence. Falling rain is the kami's work; abundant harvests are their blessing; raging storms are their fury.

Important note: kami aren't always "good" or "holy" in a moral sense. They are forces—sometimes generous, sometimes dangerous. Humanity's relationship with them resembles dealing with extremely powerful neighbors: maintained, respected, gifted, and petitioned.

### From Palace Altars to Kitchen Shelves

Kami worship happens across three levels of space. First, ***jinja***—public shrines staffed by priests called ***kannushi***, who oversee offerings of food and drink to the specific kami enshrined there. Second, family altars. Third, ***kamidana***—"god shelves"—small household altars where families make simple daily offerings.

These offerings cultivate harmony between humans and kami while soliciting blessings. At public shrines you'll also find forms of divination and religious objects like **amulets** (*omamori*) for safe travel, exam success, or smooth childbirth. It feels profoundly human: spirituality rolling up its sleeves for everyday affairs.

## Purity Above All

If one core idea must represent Shinto, it's **purity**. Shinto places major conceptual focus on ensuring purity—largely through cleaning practices such as ritual washing and bathing, especially before worship.

The logic is beautiful: the physical and spiritual worlds touch constantly, and in that contact, impurities—physical and spiritual alike—can cling. Death, blood, illness, even moral failure leave stains called *kegare*. To approach kami, humans must cleanse them. That's why every shrine entrance has a water pavilion (*temizuya*) where visitors rinse hands and mouth before approaching the altar. It's also the root of practices like ***misogi***—ritual bathing under cold waterfalls still performed today.

Purity also explains the Japanese aesthetics we recognize: Tokyo's spotless streets, the habit of removing shoes indoors, the love of clean simple objects. Many say Shinto's soul pulses behind all of it—the ancient conviction that a clean environment is one where kami wish to linger.

## Long History: From Yayoi Rice Fields to the Meiji State

Roots of kami veneration trace back to the **Yayoi period** (roughly 300 BC–250 AD)—when Japan's ancestors began wet-field rice cultivation. It makes sense: for farmers whose lives depended on rain and sun, nature wasn't backdrop but a living partner requiring constant care.

The first written records of kami worship appeared much later, in the 8th century, in two legendary texts: the ***Kojiki*** and ***Nihon Shoki***. There, kami mythology was recorded—tales of creator deities, the sun goddess Amaterasu, and the imperial lineage.

### Shinbutsu-shugo: When Shinto and Buddhism Merged

Buddhism entered Japan at the end of the Kofun period (300–538 AD) and spread rapidly. Instead of warring, the two traditions embraced. The syncretic process called ***shinbutsu-shugo*** made kami worship and Buddhism functionally inseparable. Kami came to be viewed as part of Buddhist cosmology—even as "protectors of the Dharma"—and were increasingly depicted anthropomorphically.

For centuries, mixed houses of worship stood everywhere: Buddhist temples with miniature Shinto shrines in their grounds, and vice versa. Syncretism was adopted even by the Imperial household. Imagine a spirituality flexible enough for two great religious systems to share a roof.

All of that ended drastically in the **Meiji** era (1868–1912). The new nationalist government expelled Buddhist influence from kami worship and formed **State Shinto**. Some historians actually regard this as the birth of Shinto as a standalone "religion." Shrines came under growing government influence, citizens were encouraged to worship the emperor as a kami, and when the Empire of Japan formed in the early 20th century, Shinto was exported to other parts of East Asia.

Japan's defeat in **World War II** changed everything: Shinto was formally separated from the state. Torii gates returned to being purely spiritual symbols rather than political instruments. The wounds of the State Shinto era remain an important lesson about how easily spirituality can be hijacked for power.


![Shinto](/images/topics/budaya-alt.svg)
*Image: Shinto*

## Everyday Practice: Festivals, Dances, and Amulets

For modern Japanese people, Shinto lives most vividly not in textbooks but in the calendar. **Kami festivals** (matsuri) fill every season: sacred palanquins paraded through town, taiko drums thundering, communities gathering not for formal "worship" but celebration together.

There's also ***kagura***—ancient ritual dance performed to entertain the kami, ancestral root of Japanese performing arts. Life-passage rites carry Shinto flavor too: babies brought to shrines weeks after birth, children celebrating Shichi-go-san, and many couples choosing Shinto weddings in white *shiromuku* robes.

Daily life carries subtler traces: hands clapped twice before the kamidana altar at home, new-year luck charms hung up, small amulets dangling from students' backpacks facing exams. Shinto works quietly, like breathing—rarely named, always needed.

### Living Alongside Buddha

One striking statistic: most of Japan's population takes part in both Shinto **and** Buddhist activities, especially festivals. This reflects a common view in Japanese culture that beliefs and practices of different religions need not be exclusive. Aspects of Shinto have even been absorbed into various Japanese new religious movements.

In practice: New Year is celebrated at Shinto shrines (*hatsumode*), funerals handled by Buddhist rites—and both proceed peacefully in the same person's life. To Western minds used to "one true religion" dichotomies, this seems paradoxical. To Japan, it's simply logic: why choose when you can take the best of both?

## Reading the Language of Shrine Architecture

Once you know jinja's architectural vocabulary, every visit transforms from photo-op into symbol-reading. Shinto shrine anatomy stays consistent across Japan:

The ***torii*** is the most iconic gate—the boundary between the profane world and the kami's sacred zone. Its signature vermillion isn't mere aesthetics; bright red is believed to repel negative energy. Some of the grandest torii stand over water (like Itsukushima's) or tower on mountain slopes (like Hakone's), each asserting the same claim: "from this point, you enter another realm."

Past the torii, visitors meet the ***temizuya***—water pavilion for rinsing hands and mouth. Then a stone path (the ***sando***) leads toward the main buildings, often walked slightly off-center: the middle path is believed to be "the kami's road," and courtesy yields it to them.

At the complex's heart stands the ***honden***—most sacred building housing the kami's physical embodiment (*shintai*), usually a mirror, sword, or jewel, nearly always closed to the public. Before it sits the ***haiden***, worship hall where visitors pray, with an occasional ***heiden***—offering hall—between them. Note the roofline: curved silhouettes with lifted ends and crossed wooden planks (***chigi***) at the ridge are Shinto architecture's signature, recognizable even from afar.

All elements work as one spatial narrative: outer world → purification → approach → sanctity. Shinto architecture doesn't dictate belief; it choreographs how your body moves toward respect.

## Shrine Etiquette: A Quick Guide

Since so many travelers want to honor tradition without misstepping, here's the basic protocol valid at nearly every jinja:

1. **At the temizuya**: hold the ladle with your right hand, rinse your left; switch hands and repeat; then pour water into your left palm, rinse your mouth lightly (don't swallow or touch the ladle with lips), rinse the left palm again, and stand the ladle upright so remaining water runs down the handle.
2. **At the haiden altar**: the unwritten law follows the pattern *ni-rei ni-hakushu ichi-rei*—two bows, two claps, one bow. Toss a coin (5 yen is favored for its homophone with "good fortune"), ring the bell if present, then follow the pattern sincerely—no perfection needed, just honesty.
3. **Omikuji and omamori**: draw paper fortunes (omikuji); if results are poor, custom allows tying them to a dedicated rack so "bad luck stays behind at the shrine." Omamori charms may go home—but get replaced each new year.
4. **Ema**: write wishes on small wooden plaques painted with horses, hang them on racks. Yes—wish-writing lives here too, distant cousin of Tanabata's tanzaku.
5. **Better avoided**: photographing inside honden areas, loud talking, cutting through others' prayers, treating shrines as drone playgrounds.

One reassuring note: Japanese people deeply appreciate effort. Wrong sequence by a step? Nobody gets angry. Respectful intent is the language every shrine understands best.

## Time and Space Concepts in Shinto

One dimension of Shinto rarely discussed with tourists: how it views **time**. There's no mandatory weekly worship day like other traditions; instead, Shinto's calendar follows nature's rhythm—planting seasons, harvests, year transitions. Grand festivals (matsuri) are season markers: cherry blossoms open the year, fireworks wave mid-summer, and autumn harvest crowns the gratitude.

Space receives similar treatment. The concept of **kegare** (stain)—and its recoverability—means Shinto knows no eternal sin: stains are temporary conditions that can be washed away, not permanent identities. This is profoundly humane philosophy: a failed person isn't a "sinner" but someone needing cleansing and a fresh start. Purification rites (***harae***) are performed by kannushi waving white paper wands (***haraegushi***) above participants' heads—picture it as an official spiritual "restart".

The third key spatial concept: **boundaries**. The kami's world and humanity's must not mix carelessly—torii, shimenawa ropes with zigzag papers (shide), and layered gates all serve as border managers. Even sumo's national ring gets purified with salt scatterings because its ritual roots run Shinto. These traces run so deep in daily life they often go unnoticed as "religion".

And perhaps that's where true strength lies: Shinto doesn't demand your belief. It's satisfied when you—just for a moment—pause before a tiny roadside shrine, bow slightly, then continue walking. In the view of those eight million kami, such small gestures already suffice to keep the world in harmony.

## Conclusion

Shinto teaches something rare in the modern world: spirituality without obligation. No one will punish you for never reading its scripture—because its scripture is rivers, mountains, and seasons. No one demands exclusive loyalty—because the kami aren't jealous.

At its heart, Shinto is an invitation to see the world differently: forests aren't timber warehouses but spirit dwellings; the water washing your hands before prayer matters as much as the prayer itself; and harmony—with nature, ancestors, and each other—is lifelong work.

A thousand kami, eight million kami, or however many there are—one thing is clear: behind every vermillion torii lies an ancient conviction that remains relevant today. Humans don't stand alone in this universe. We're part of a larger weave, and tending that weave is how we stay human.

# Analisis Data Tanpa Berjuang Sama Excel


![Analisis Data Tanpa Berjuang Sama Excel — ilustrasi topik](/images/topics/vibe-coding.svg)
*Gambar: Analisis Data Tanpa Berjuang Sama Excel*

Hampir semua pekerja kantoran pernah mengalami momen ini: sebuah file berisi ribuan baris data harus diringkas sebelum sore, dan yang tersedia hanyalah Excel beserta ingatan samar tentang VLOOKUP yang dulu diajarkan pelatihan lima tahun lalu. Jam-jam berikutnya habis untuk mencari tutorial, memperbaiki formula error, dan mengulang pivot table yang hasilnya tidak masuk akal.

Vibe coding menawarkan jalur berbeda. Alih-alih menjadi ahli tools spreadsheet, Anda bisa menjelaskan apa yang ingin diketahui dari data dalam bahasa sehari-hari, lalu membiarkan AI menuliskan langkah-langkah teknisnya—entah sebagai formula, script Python, atau petunjuk pengolahan bertahap. Artikel ini membedah pendekatan tersebut secara praktis.

## Mengapa Spreadsheet Sering Menjadi Sumber Penderitaan

Excel dan Google Sheets adalah tools luar biasa, tetapi cara kerjanya menuntut pola pikir tertentu: Anda harus menerjemahkan pertanyaan bisnis menjadi operasi teknis (formula, filter, pivot) dengan tata bahasa yang ketat. Satu tanda kurung salah atau referensi sel tergeser, hasilnya diam-diam keliru tanpa peringatan.

Tiga titik sakit yang paling umum:

1. **Data kotor**: nama produk ditulis beda-beda, tanggal dalam format campuran, spasi tersembunyi di ujung sel.
2. **Formula rapuh**: satu baris disisipkan di tengah tabel, dan seluruh referensi ikut bergeser.
3. **Kurva belajar**: fitur-fitur canggih ada, tapi menemukan dan menguasainya butuh waktu bertahun-tahun.

AI meredakan ketiganya karena bekerja pada tingkat maksud. Anda bilang "hitung total penjualan per bulan, abaikan entri uji coba", dan AI-lah yang menerjemahkan ke operasi konkret.

## Alur Kerja Praktis: Bersihkan, Tanya, Visualisasikan

**Langkah 1: Bersihkan data lebih dulu.** Ini bagian paling tidak glamor namun paling menentukan. Tempelkan contoh data Anda (atau cuplikannya) ke AI dan minta diagnosis: kolom mana yang formatnya tidak konsisten, nilai apa yang tampak janggal, duplikat di mana. Minta juga skrip pembersihnya—biasanya beberapa baris Python dengan library pandas sudah cukup untuk pekerjaan yang manualnya berjam-jam.

**Langkah 2: Ajukan pertanyaan seperti kepada analis junior.** Alih-alih "buatkan SUMIFS", katakan: "Dari data ini, produk mana yang penjualannya paling turun dibanding bulan lalu? Tampilkan sepuluh teratas." AI akan menyusun logika agregasinya. Jika Anda tidak yakin dengan hasilnya, minta ia menjelaskan langkah komputasinya satu per satu—kesempatan belajar gratis sekaligus alat verifikasi.

**Langkah 3: Visualisasikan temuan.** Grafik yang tepat membuat insight terserap jauh lebih cepat daripada tabel angka. Deskripsikan pesan yang ingin disampaikan—"grafik tren bulanan yang menonjolkan dua bulan terburuk"—dan biarkan AI memilih jenis chart beserta kode pembuatnya, baik itu di matplotlib, Plotly, maupun rekomendasi setting chart di spreadsheet.


![Analisis Data Tanpa Berjuang Sama Excel — teknologi & produktivitas](/images/topics/teknologi-alt.svg)
*Gambar: Analisis Data Tanpa Berjuang Sama Excel*

## Contoh Konkret Sehari-hari

Seorang pemilik toko online menerima ekspor penjualan berisi 12.000 baris. Pertanyaannya sederhana: produk mana yang layak diberi diskon akhir bulan? Dengan pendekatan tradisional, ia akan membuka tiga tab tutorial. Dengan vibe coding, urutannya begini:

- Unggah/tempel sampel data, minta AI membersihkan kolom harga dan tanggal.
- Minta ringkasan penjualan per produk per minggu.
- Minta identifikasi produk dengan tren menurun selama empat minggu berturut-turut namun margin tetap sehat.
- Minta grafik perbandingan untuk dilampirkan ke tim.

Total waktu: kurang dari satu jam, termasuk iterasi pertanyaan. Yang penting dicatat: pemilik toko itu tetap yang memutuskan. AI menyajikan angka; interpretasi bisnis dan keputusan akhir tetap milik manusia.

## Jebakan yang Harus Diwaspadai

Kecepatan analisis AI datang dengan risiko yang perlu disadari:

- **Halusinasi angka.** Jika Anda hanya menempel deskripsi data tanpa datanya, AI akan "mengarang" statistik yang terdengar meyakinkan. Selalu sediakan data asli saat analisis, bukan sekadar narasi.
- **Verifikasi silang.** Untuk angka-angka kunci, hitung ulang dengan cara kedua—formula spreadsheet sederhana atau pengecekan manual pada sampel kecil.
- **Privasi data.** Data pelanggan, informasi gaji, atau catatan medis tidak boleh diunggah mentah-mentah ke layanan AI publik. Anonymize dulu: hapus nama, email, dan nomor identitas sebelum data keluar dari lingkungan Anda.
- **Korelasi bukan sebab-akibat.** AI cepat menemukan pola; menilai apakah pola itu bermakna tetap tugas Anda.

Satu kebiasaan yang menyelamatkan banyak orang adalah menyimpan setiap skrip pembersih dan rumus yang dipakai AI sebagai file terpisah. Ketika bulan depan data serupa datang lagi, Anda tinggal menjalankan ulang alur yang sama—dan analisis yang tadinya satu kali jadi berubah menjadi pipeline yang bisa dipakai terus-menerus.

## Kesimpulan

Analisis data tidak lagi mensyaratkan keahlian formula yang dalam atau kursus statistik panjang. Pola kerja baru cukup sederhana: bersihkan data dengan bantuan AI, ajukan pertanyaan dalam bahasa alami, minta visualisasi yang mendukung cerita, lalu verifikasi angka-angka penting.

Peran manusia bergeser dari operator tools menjadi pengambil keputusan—menentukan pertanyaan yang tepat, menilai konteks di balik angka, dan menanggung konsekuensi keputusan. Kombinasi intuisi bisnis Anda dan kecepatan komputasi AI adalah pasangan yang jauh lebih kuat daripada keduanya sendirian. Mulailah dengan satu file data yang selama ini Anda hindari, dan lihat betapa cepatnya rasa takut pada spreadsheet itu luruh.

en.title: Data Analysis Without Fighting Excel
en.contentMarkdown:
---
title: "Data Analysis Without Fighting Excel"
excerpt: "Complex formulas and confusing pivot tables can be replaced by plain conversation. Here's how to use AI to clean, analyze, and visualize your data without the spreadsheet struggle."
meta_title: "Data Analysis with AI, No Excel Drama"
meta_description: "A practical guide to AI-assisted data analysis: cleaning data, generating formulas, asking questions in plain language, visualization, and common pitfalls."
category: "teknologi"
tags: ["vibe-coding", "data-analysis", "ai", "excel", "productivity"]
reading_time: 8
---

# Data Analysis Without Fighting Excel


![Data Analysis Without Fighting Excel — ilustrasi topik](/images/topics/vibe-coding.svg)
*Image: Data Analysis Without Fighting Excel*

Nearly every office worker knows this moment: a file with thousands of rows must be summarized by end of day, and all you have is Excel plus a vague memory of VLOOKUP from a training session five years ago. The next few hours disappear into tutorials, formula errors, and pivot tables that return nonsense.

Vibe coding offers a different path. Instead of becoming a spreadsheet power user, you describe what you want to know in everyday language and let AI handle the technical translation—whether that's a formula, a Python script, or step-by-step processing instructions. This article breaks down the approach practically.

## Why Spreadsheets Become a Source of Suffering

Excel and Google Sheets are remarkable tools, but they demand a particular mindset: you must translate business questions into technical operations (formulas, filters, pivots) using unforgiving syntax. One misplaced parenthesis or shifted cell reference quietly corrupts results without any warning.

Three pain points dominate:

1. **Dirty data**: product names spelled inconsistently, mixed date formats, invisible trailing spaces in cells.
2. **Fragile formulas**: insert one row mid-table and every downstream reference shifts.
3. **Steep learning curve**: powerful features exist, but finding and mastering them takes years.

AI relieves all three because it works at the level of intent. You say "calculate monthly sales totals, excluding test entries," and the AI handles translation into concrete operations.

## A Practical Workflow: Clean, Ask, Visualize

**Step 1: Clean the data first.** It's the least glamorous part and the most decisive. Paste your data (or a sample) into the AI and request a diagnosis: which columns are inconsistent, which values look anomalous, where duplicates hide. Ask for the cleaning script too—usually a handful of Python lines with pandas covers work that would take days manually.

**Step 2: Ask questions like you would ask a junior analyst.** Instead of requesting a SUMIFS, say: "From this data, which products dropped most compared to last month? Show the top ten." The AI assembles the aggregation logic. Unsure about the result? Ask it to explain its computation step by step—free learning and verification at once.

**Step 3: Visualize findings.** The right chart absorbs far faster than a wall of numbers. Describe the message—"a monthly trend chart highlighting the two worst months"—and let AI pick the chart type and write the code, whether matplotlib, Plotly, or recommended settings inside your spreadsheet app.


![Data Analysis Without Fighting Excel — teknologi & produktivitas](/images/topics/teknologi-alt.svg)
*Image: Data Analysis Without Fighting Excel*

## An Everyday Example

An online shop owner receives a sales export with 12,000 rows. The question is simple: which products deserve an end-of-month discount? Traditionally, this means opening three tutorial tabs. With vibe coding, the sequence looks like this:

- Upload/paste a sample and have AI clean the price and date columns.
- Request weekly sales summaries per product.
- Identify products declining four consecutive weeks while maintaining healthy margins.
- Generate comparison charts to attach for the team.

Total time: under an hour, including follow-up questions. Crucially, the owner still decides. AI presents numbers; business interpretation and final calls remain human territory.

## Pitfalls You Must Watch For

AI-speed analysis comes with risks worth acknowledging:

- **Hallucinated numbers.** If you only paste a description without the actual data, AI will confidently invent statistics. Always supply real data when analyzing—never just narrative.
- **Cross-verification.** Recalculate key figures a second way—a simple spreadsheet formula or manual check on a small sample.
- **Data privacy.** Customer records, salary information, or medical notes should never go raw into public AI services. Anonymize first: strip names, emails, and ID numbers before data leaves your environment.
- **Correlation isn't causation.** AI finds patterns quickly; judging whether those patterns matter remains your job.

One habit that saves many people: save every cleaning script and formula the AI produces as a separate file. When similar data arrives next month, you simply rerun the same pipeline—turning a one-off analysis into a repeatable process that keeps paying off.

## Conclusion

Data analysis no longer requires deep formula expertise or long statistics courses. The new working pattern is simple: clean data with AI's help, ask questions in natural language, request visuals that support your story, then verify the critical numbers.

The human role shifts from tool operator to decision-maker—choosing the right questions, weighing context behind figures, owning the consequences. Your business intuition plus AI's computational speed is a pairing far stronger than either alone. Start with one dataset you've been avoiding, and watch how quickly the spreadsheet fear dissolves.

id.contentMarkdown:
# Periode Permian: Pangaea Satu Benua Raksasa

Kehidupan di bumi tidak muncul begitu saja; ia adalah hasil perjalanan panjang penuh percobaan dan kesalahan alam selama miliaran tahun. Artikel ini mengajak Anda menelusuri babak demi babak kisah kehidupan purba, memahami bagaimana molekul sederhana berevolusi menjadi ekosistem yang kompleks, dan melihat jejak-jejak yang masih bisa kita baca hingga hari ini.

Permian ( PUR-mee-ən) adalah periode geologi dan sistem stratigrafi yang berlangsung selama 47 juta tahun, dari akhir Periode Karbon 298,9 juta tahun yang lalu (jutaan tahun yang lalu) hingga awal Periode Trias 251,902 juta tahun yang lalu. Ini adalah periode keenam dan terakhir dari Era Paleozoikum; Periode Trias berikutnya termasuk dalam Era Mesozoikum. Konsep Permian diperkenalkan pada tahun 1841 oleh ahli geologi Sir Roderick Murchison, yang menamakannya setelah wilayah Perm di Rusia.

Permian menyaksikan diversifikasi dua kelompok amniota, sinapsida dan sauropsid (reptil). Dunia pada saat itu didominasi oleh benua super Pangaea, yang terbentuk akibat tumbukan Euramerika dan Gondwana, pada masa Karbon. Pangaea dikelilingi oleh lautan super Panthalassa. Runtuhnya hutan hujan Karbon meninggalkan wilayah gurun yang luas di pedalaman benua. Amniota, yang mampu mengatasi kondisi yang lebih kering ini dengan lebih baik, menjadi dominan menggantikan nenek moyang amfibi mereka.

Berbagai penulis telah mengusulkan setidaknya tiga, dan mungkin empat peristiwa kepunahan besar di Permian, meskipun validitas beberapa kepunahan ini masih diperdebatkan. Akhir dari Permian Awal (Cisuralian) ditandai dengan pergeseran fauna besar-besaran karena sebagian besar garis keturunan sinapsida "pelikosaurus" primitif punah, digantikan oleh therapsida yang lebih maju selama Permian Tengah (Guadalupian), meskipun sifat transisi ini (yang mungkin merupakan peristiwa kepunahan yang dijuluki "Kepunahan Olson") kurang dipahami. Berakhirnya Tahap Capitanian pada akhir Permian Tengah ditandai dengan peristiwa kepunahan massal besar Capitanian, terkait dengan letusan Perangkap Emeishan. Masa Permian (bersama dengan Paleozoikum) berakhir dengan peristiwa kepunahan Permian–Trias (bahasa sehari-hari dikenal sebagai Kematian Besar), kepunahan massal terbesar dalam sejarah bumi (yang merupakan krisis terakhir dari tiga atau empat krisis yang terjadi pada masa Permian), yang menyebabkan hampir 81% spesies laut dan 70% spesies darat punah, terkait dengan letusan Perangkap Siberia. Butuh waktu lama hingga Trias bagi kehidupan untuk pulih dari bencana ini; di darat, ekosistem membutuhkan waktu 30 juta tahun untuk pulih.

![Periode Permian: Pangaea Satu Benua Raksasa](/images/topics/sejarah-alt.svg)
*Gambar: Periode Permian: Pangaea Satu Benua Raksasa*

## Etimologi dan sejarah

Sebelum istilah Permian diperkenalkan, batuan dengan umur yang setara di Jerman dinamai Rotliegend dan Zechstein, dan di Inggris Raya disebut Batu Pasir Merah Baru.

Istilah Permian diperkenalkan ke dalam geologi pada tahun 1841 oleh Sir Roderick Impey Murchison, presiden Geological Society of London, setelah eksplorasi ekstensif Rusia yang dilakukan dengan Édouard de Verneuil di sekitar Pegunungan Ural pada tahun 1840 dan 1841. Murchison mengidentifikasi "rangkaian luas lapisan napal, sekis, batu kapur, batu pasir, dan konglomerat" yang menggantikan strata Karbon di wilayah tersebut. Murchison, bekerja sama dengan ahli geologi Rusia, menamai periode tersebut dengan nama wilayah Perm di sekitar Rusia, yang mengambil namanya dari kerajaan abad pertengahan Permia yang menempati wilayah yang sama ratusan tahun sebelumnya, dan sekarang terletak di wilayah administratif Perm Krai. Antara tahun 1853 dan 1867, Jules Marcou mengakui strata Permian di wilayah yang luas di Amerika Utara dari Sungai Mississippi hingga Sungai Colorado dan mengusulkan nama Dyassic, dari Dyas dan Trias, meskipun Murchison menolaknya pada tahun 1871. Sistem Permian menjadi kontroversial selama lebih dari satu abad setelah penamaan aslinya, dengan Survei Geologi Amerika Serikat hingga tahun 1941 menganggap Permian sebagai subsistem Karbon yang setara dengan Mississippian dan orang Pennsylvania.

## Geologi

Periode Permian dibagi menjadi tiga zaman, dari yang tertua hingga yang termuda, yaitu Cisuralian, Guadalupian, dan Lopingian, yang masing-masing dikenal sebagai Permian Awal, Tengah, dan Akhir. Ahli geologi membagi batuan Permian menjadi kumpulan stratigrafi unit-unit lebih kecil yang disebut tahapan, masing-masing terbentuk selama interval waktu tertentu yang disebut usia. Tahapan dapat ditentukan secara global atau regional. Untuk korelasi stratigrafi global, Komisi Internasional untuk Stratigrafi (ICS) meratifikasi tahapan global berdasarkan Bagian dan Titik Stratotipe Batas Global (GSSP) dari satu formasi (stratotipe) yang mengidentifikasi batas bawah tahapan tersebut. Umur suku Permian dari yang termuda sampai yang tertua adalah:

Selama sebagian besar abad ke-20, Permian terbagi menjadi Permian Awal dan Akhir, dengan Kungurian menjadi tahap terakhir dari Permian Awal. Glenister dan rekan-rekannya pada tahun 1992 mengusulkan skema tripartit, yang menyatakan bahwa zaman Roadian-Capitanian berbeda dari zaman Permian Akhir lainnya, dan harus dianggap sebagai zaman yang terpisah. Perpecahan tripartit diadopsi setelah usulan resmi oleh Glenister dkk. (1999).

Secara historis, sebagian besar biostratigrafi kelautan Permian didasarkan pada ammonoid; namun, lokalitas amonoid jarang terjadi di bagian stratigrafi Permian, dan spesies mempunyai ciri jangka waktu yang relatif lama. Semua GSSP untuk Permian didasarkan pada data kemunculan pertama spesies konodont tertentu, sekelompok chordata tak berahang yang misterius dengan elemen mulut keras seperti gigi. Conodont digunakan sebagai fosil indeks pada sebagian besar zaman Paleozoikum dan Trias.

### Cisuralian

Nama Seri Cisural diambil dari nama strata yang tersingkap di lereng barat Pegunungan Ural di Rusia dan Kazakhstan. Nama tersebut diusulkan oleh J. B. Waterhouse pada tahun 1982 untuk terdiri dari tahapan Asselian, Sakmarian, dan Artinskian. Kungurian kemudian ditambahkan agar sesuai dengan "Permian Bawah" Rusia. Albert Auguste Cochon de Lapparent pada tahun 1900 telah mengusulkan "Seri Ural", tetapi penggunaan istilah ini yang tidak konsisten menyebabkan istilah tersebut kemudian ditinggalkan.

Asselian diberi nama oleh ahli stratigraf Rusia V.E. Ruzhenchev pada tahun 1954, setelah Sungai Assel di selatan Pegunungan Ural. GSSP untuk pangkalan Asselian terletak di lembah Sungai Aidaralash dekat Aqtöbe, Kazakhstan, yang diratifikasi pada tahun 1996. Permulaan tahapan ditentukan oleh kemunculan pertama Streptognathodus postfusus.

Nama Sakmarian mengacu pada Sungai Sakmara di Ural selatan, dan diciptakan oleh Alexander Karpinsky pada tahun 1874. GSSP untuk pangkalan Sakmarian terletak di bagian Usolka di Ural selatan, yang diratifikasi pada tahun 2018. GSSP ditentukan oleh kemunculan pertama Sweetognathus binodosus.

Nama Artinskian diambil dari nama kota Arti di Oblast Sverdlovsk, Rusia. Ia dinamakan oleh Karpinsky pada tahun 1874. Artinskian kini tidak mempunyai GSSP yang pasti. Definisi yang diusulkan untuk dasar Artinskian adalah kemunculan pertama Sweetognathus aff. S.whitei.

Kungurian mengambil namanya dari Kungur, sebuah kota di Perm Krai. Panggung ini diperkenalkan oleh Alexandr Antonovich Stukenberg pada tahun 1890. Kungurian saat ini tidak memiliki GSSP yang pasti. Usulan terbaru menyarankan munculnya Neostreptognathodus pnevi sebagai batas bawah.

### Guadalupe

Nama Seri Guadalupe diambil dari nama Pegunungan Guadalupe di Texas dan New Mexico, tempat rangkaian laut luas pada zaman ini tersingkap. Itu dinamai oleh George Herbert Girty pada tahun 1902.

Roadian dinamai pada tahun 1968 mengacu pada Anggota Formasi Kata Road Canyon di Texas. GSSP untuk dasar Roadian terletak 42,7m di atas dasar Formasi Cutoff di Stratotype Canyon, Pegunungan Guadalupe, Texas, dan diratifikasi pada tahun 2001. Permulaan tahapan ditentukan oleh kemunculan pertama Jinogondolella nankingensis.

Nama Wordian mengacu pada Formasi Kata oleh Johan August Udden pada tahun 1916, Glenister dan Furnish pada tahun 1961 adalah publikasi pertama yang menggunakannya sebagai istilah kronostratigrafi sebagai subtahap dari Tahap Guadalupian. GSSP untuk dasar Wordian terletak di Guadalupe Pass, Texas, di dalam sedimen Anggota Batu Kapur Getaway dari Formasi Cherry Canyon, yang diratifikasi pada tahun 2001. Dasar Wordian ditentukan oleh kemunculan pertama conodont Jinogondolella aserrata.

Nama Capitanian diambil dari nama Capitan Reef di Pegunungan Guadalupe Texas, dinamai oleh George Burr Richardson pada tahun 1904, dan pertama kali digunakan dalam pengertian kronostratigrafi oleh Glenister dan Furnish pada tahun 1961 sebagai sub-tahap dari Panggung Guadalupe. Capitanian diratifikasi sebagai panggung internasional oleh ICS pada tahun 2001. GSSP untuk pangkalan Capitanian terletak di Nipple Hill di tenggara Pegunungan Guadalupe Texas, dan diratifikasi pada tahun 2001, permulaan panggung ditentukan oleh kemunculan pertama Jinogondolella postserrata.

### Lopingian

Lopingian pertama kali diperkenalkan oleh Amadeus William Grabau pada tahun 1923 sebagai "Seri Loping" setelah Leping, Jiangxi, Tiongkok. Awalnya digunakan sebagai unit litostrafik, T.K. Huang pada tahun 1932 mengangkat Lopingian menjadi satu rangkaian, termasuk seluruh endapan Permian di Tiongkok Selatan yang terletak di atas Batu Kapur Maokou. Pada tahun 1995, pemungutan suara oleh Subkomisi Stratigrafi Permian ICS mengadopsi Lopingian sebagai satuan kronostratigrafi standar internasional.

Wuchiapinginan dan Changhsingian pertama kali diperkenalkan pada tahun 1962, oleh J. Z. Sheng sebagai "Formasi Wuchiaping" dan "Formasi Changhsing" dalam deret Lopingian. GSSP untuk pangkalan Wuchiapingian terletak di Penglaitan, Guangxi, Tiongkok dan diratifikasi pada tahun 2004. Batas tersebut ditentukan oleh kemunculan pertama Clarkina postbitteri postbitteri. Changhsingian awalnya berasal dari Batu Kapur Changxing, sebuah unit geologi yang pertama kali dinamai oleh Grabau pada tahun 1923, yang akhirnya berasal dari Kabupaten Changxing, Zhejiang. GSSP untuk pangkalan Changhsingian terletak 88 cm di atas dasar Batu Kapur Changxing di bagian Meishan D, Zhejiang, Tiongkok dan diratifikasi pada tahun 2005, batasnya ditentukan oleh kemunculan pertama Clarkina wangi.

GSSP untuk dasar Trias terletak di dasar Tempat Tidur 27c di bagian Meishan D, dan diratifikasi pada tahun 2001. GSSP ditentukan oleh kemunculan pertama konodont Hindeodus parvus.

### Tahapan wilayah

Panggung Tatarian Rusia mencakup Lopingian, Capitanian, dan sebagian Wordian, sedangkan Kazanian yang mendasarinya mencakup sisa Wordian serta Roadian.

Di Amerika Utara, Permian dibagi menjadi Wolfcampian (yang mencakup tahapan Nealian dan Lenoxian); Leonardian (panggung Hessian dan Katedral); orang Guadalupe; dan Ochoan, sesuai dengan Lopingian.

Skala waktu geologi Selandia Baru membagi Permian menjadi tiga zaman, Pra-Telfordian (tidak terbagi), D'Urville (dibagi menjadi tahap Makarewan, Waiitian, dan Puruhauan), dan Aparima (tahap Flettian, Barrettian, Mangapirian, dan Telfordian). Zaman Pra-Telfordian kira-kira sama dengan tahap Asselian, Sakmarian, dan Artinskian; zaman D'Urville kira-kira sezaman dengan zaman Kunguria dan zaman Guadalupia; dan zaman Aparima sangat dekat dengan zaman Lopingian.

## Paleogeografi

Selama masa Permian, semua daratan utama bumi dikumpulkan menjadi satu superbenua yang dikenal sebagai Pangaea, dengan daratan mikrokontinental Cathaysia di sebelah timur. Pangaea terletak di garis khatulistiwa dan memanjang ke arah kutub, dengan dampak yang sama pada arus laut di satu samudra besar ("Panthalassa", "laut universal"), dan Samudera Paleo-Tethys, samudra luas yang berada di antara Asia dan Gondwana. Benua Cimmeria menjauh dari Gondwana dan melayang ke utara menuju Laurasia, menyebabkan Samudra Paleo-Tethys menyusut. Samudera baru tumbuh di ujung selatannya, Samudera Neotethys, samudra yang mendominasi sebagian besar Era Mesozoikum. Busur magmatik, yang berisi Hainan di ujung paling barat dayanya, mulai terbentuk saat Panthalassa menunjam ke bawah tenggara Tiongkok Selatan. Pegunungan Pangean Tengah, yang mulai terbentuk akibat tumbukan Laurasia dan Gondwana pada zaman Karbon, mencapai ketinggian maksimumnya pada awal Permian sekitar tahun 295 juta tahun yang lalu, sebanding dengan Himalaya saat ini, namun menjadi sangat terkikis seiring berjalannya zaman Permian. Blok Kazakhstania bertabrakan dengan Baltica pada masa Cisuralian, sedangkan Kraton Tiongkok Utara, Blok Tiongkok Selatan, dan Indochina menyatu satu sama lain dan Pangaea pada akhir Permian. Laut Zechstein, laut epikontinental yang hipersalin, ada di tempat yang sekarang menjadi Eropa barat laut.

Interior daratan kontinental yang besar mengalami iklim dengan variasi panas dan dingin yang ekstrim ("iklim kontinental") dan kondisi monsun dengan pola curah hujan musiman yang tinggi. Gurun tampaknya tersebar luas di Pangaea. Kondisi kering seperti itu lebih disukai gymnospermae, tanaman yang bijinya tertutup penutup pelindung, dibandingkan tanaman seperti pakis yang menyebarkan spora di lingkungan yang lebih basah. Pohon modern pertama (tumbuhan runjung, ginkgo, dan sikas) muncul pada zaman Permian.

Tiga wilayah umum yang terkenal karena endapan Permiannya yang luas—Pegunungan Ural (tempat Perm berada), Tiongkok, dan barat daya Amerika Utara, termasuk hamparan merah Texas. Cekungan Permian di negara bagian Texas dan New Mexico, AS, dinamakan demikian karena memiliki salah satu endapan batuan Permian paling tebal di dunia.

### Paleoseanografi

Permukaan laut turun sedikit pada masa awal Permian (Asselian). Permukaan air laut stabil pada ketinggian beberapa puluh meter di atas permukaan laut saat ini pada masa Permian Awal, namun terjadi penurunan tajam yang dimulai pada masa Roadian, yang berpuncak pada permukaan laut terendah di seluruh Paleozoikum pada sekitar permukaan laut saat ini pada masa Wuchiapingian, diikuti oleh sedikit kenaikan pada masa Changhsingian.

## Iklim

Periode Permian lebih dingin dibandingkan periode waktu geologi lainnya, dengan gradien suhu yang sederhana antara kutub dan khatulistiwa. Pada permulaan zaman Permian, Bumi masih berada dalam rumah es Paleozoikum Akhir (LPIA), yang dimulai pada masa Devonian terakhir dan mencakup seluruh periode Karbon, dengan fase paling intens yang terjadi pada bagian akhir zaman Pennsylvania. Tren peningkatan kekeringan yang signifikan dapat diamati selama Cisuralian. Aridifikasi Permian awal paling menonjol di wilayah Pangaea di garis lintang dekat khatulistiwa. Permukaan air laut juga meningkat secara signifikan pada Permian Awal seiring dengan menyusutnya LPIA secara perlahan. Di perbatasan Karbon-Permian, terjadi peristiwa pemanasan. Selain menjadi lebih hangat, iklim menjadi lebih gersang pada akhir Zaman Karbon dan awal Permian. Meskipun demikian, suhu terus mendingin selama sebagian besar Asselian dan Sakmarian, saat LPIA mencapai puncaknya. Pada tahun 287 Ma, suhu menghangat dan lapisan es di Kutub Selatan menyusut dan dikenal sebagai Peristiwa Pemanasan Artinskian (AWE), meskipun gletser tetap ada di dataran tinggi Australia bagian timur, dan mungkin juga di daerah pegunungan di Siberia paling utara. Afrika Selatan juga mempertahankan gletser selama akhir Cisuralian di lingkungan dataran tinggi. AWE juga menyaksikan kekeringan yang sangat besar.

Pada akhir Kungurian, pendinginan kembali terjadi, menghasilkan interval glasial dingin yang berlangsung hingga awal Capitanian, meskipun suhu rata-rata masih jauh lebih tinggi dibandingkan pada awal Cisuralian. Periode keren lainnya dimulai sekitar pertengahan Capitanian. Periode dingin ini, yang berlangsung selama 3–4 Myr, dikenal sebagai Peristiwa Kamura. Hal ini terganggu oleh Ekskursi Termal Emeishan di bagian akhir Capitanian, sekitar 260 juta tahun yang lalu, bersamaan dengan letusan Perangkap Emeishan. Interval perubahan iklim yang cepat ini bertanggung jawab atas peristiwa kepunahan massal Capitanian.

Pada masa awal Wuchiapingian, setelah terbentuknya Perangkap Emeishan, suhu global menurun karena karbon dioksida terkikis dari atmosfer oleh batuan basal di provinsi beku besar tersebut. Mendiang Wuchiapingian menyaksikan akhir dari Zaman Es Paleozoikum Akhir, ketika gletser terakhir di Australia mencair. Berakhirnya zaman Permian ditandai dengan perubahan suhu yang jauh lebih besar dibandingkan dengan perubahan suhu di perbatasan Permian-Trias, yang terjadi bersamaan dengan letusan Perangkap Siberia, yang melepaskan lebih dari 5 teraton CO2, yang berarti dua kali lipat konsentrasi karbon dioksida di atmosfer. Ekskursi -2% δ18O menandakan besarnya perubahan iklim yang ekstrim ini. Interval pelepasan gas rumah kaca yang sangat cepat ini menyebabkan kepunahan massal Permian-Trias, serta menyebabkan terjadinya rumah kaca ekstrem yang bertahan selama beberapa juta tahun hingga zaman geologi berikutnya, Trias.

Iklim Permian juga sangat musiman dan dicirikan oleh megamonsun, yang menghasilkan tingkat kekeringan yang tinggi dan musim yang ekstrim di pedalaman Pangea. Curah hujan di sepanjang tepi barat Samudera Palaeo-Tethys sangat tinggi. Bukti terjadinya megamonsun mencakup keberadaan hutan hujan megamonsun di Cekungan Qiangtang di Tibet, variasi musiman yang sangat besar dalam sedimentasi, bioturbasi, dan pengendapan ichnofosil yang tercatat dalam fasies sedimen di Cekungan Sydney, dan model paleoklimatik iklim bumi berdasarkan perilaku pola cuaca modern yang menunjukkan bahwa megamonsun seperti itu akan terjadi mengingat susunan benua Permian. Meningkatnya kegersangan khatulistiwa yang disebutkan di atas kemungkinan besar disebabkan oleh perkembangan dan intensifikasi megamonsun Pangaean ini.

### biota laut

Endapan laut Permian kaya akan fosil moluska, brakiopoda, dan echinodermata. Brachiopoda sangat beragam selama Permian. Ordo Productida yang punah adalah kelompok brakiopoda Permian yang dominan, mencakup sekitar setengah dari seluruh genera brakiopoda Permian. Brachiopoda juga berperan sebagai insinyur ekosistem penting di kompleks terumbu Permian. Di antara amonoid, Goniatitida merupakan kelompok besar pada Permian Awal-Pertengahan, namun menurun pada Permian Akhir. Anggota ordo Prolecanitida kurang beragam. Ceratitida berasal dari keluarga Daraelitidae dalam Prolecanitida selama pertengahan Permian, dan melakukan diversifikasi secara luas selama Permian Akhir. Hanya tiga famili trilobita yang diketahui yaitu Permian, Proetidae, Brachymetopidae dan Phillipsiidae. Tingkat keanekaragaman, asal muasal dan kepunahan selama Permian Awal rendah. Trilobita mengalami diversifikasi pada masa Kungurian-Wordian, masa terakhir dalam sejarah evolusi mereka, sebelum mengalami penurunan pada masa Permian Akhir. Pada zaman Changhsingian, hanya segelintir (4–6) genera yang tersisa. Karang menunjukkan penurunan keanekaragaman selama Permian Tengah dan Akhir.

### Biota darat

Kehidupan terestrial di Permian mencakup beragam tumbuhan, jamur, artropoda, dan berbagai jenis tetrapoda. Periode tersebut menyaksikan gurun besar menutupi bagian dalam Pangaea. Zona hangat tersebar di belahan bumi utara, tempat munculnya gurun kering yang luas. Batuan yang terbentuk pada masa itu diwarnai merah oleh oksida besi, akibat pemanasan yang intens oleh matahari pada permukaan yang tidak memiliki tutupan vegetasi. Sejumlah jenis tumbuhan dan hewan tua punah atau menjadi unsur marginal.

Permian dimulai dengan flora Karbon yang masih tumbuh subur. Sekitar pertengahan Permian, transisi besar dalam vegetasi dimulai. Pohon lycopoda yang menyukai rawa di zaman Karbon, seperti Lepidodendron dan Sigillaria, secara bertahap digantikan di pedalaman benua oleh pakis berbiji yang lebih maju dan tumbuhan runjung awal sebagai akibat dari runtuhnya hutan hujan Karbon. Pada akhir zaman Permian, rawa-rawa lycopod dan equisete yang mengingatkan pada flora Karbon hanya bertahan di Cathaysia, serangkaian pulau khatulistiwa di Samudera Paleo-Tethys yang kemudian menjadi Tiongkok Selatan.

Zaman Permian menyaksikan radiasi dari banyak kelompok tumbuhan runjung penting, termasuk nenek moyang banyak keluarga masa kini. Hutan yang kaya terdapat di banyak wilayah, dengan beragam kelompok tumbuhan. Benua selatan memiliki hutan pakis berbiji yang luas dari flora Glossopteris. Tingkat oksigen mungkin tinggi di sana. Ginkgos dan sikas juga muncul selama periode ini.

### Serangga

Serangga, yang pertama kali muncul dan melimpah pada masa Karbon, mengalami peningkatan diversifikasi secara dramatis pada masa Permian Awal. Menjelang akhir zaman Permian, terjadi penurunan substansial dalam tingkat asal usul dan kepunahan. Pada awal Permian, telah terjadi perlombaan senjata koevolusi yang aktif antara serangga dan struktur reproduksi tanaman, yang dibuktikan dengan kerusakan tanaman yang disebabkan oleh serangga dan struktur pertahanan tanaman yang bertujuan meminimalkan pemangsaan serangga. Serangga dominan pada Periode Permian adalah perwakilan awal Paleoptera, Polyneoptera, dan Paraneoptera. Palaeodictyopteroidea, yang mewakili kelompok serangga dominan selama Zaman Karbon, menurun selama Permian. Hal ini kemungkinan besar disebabkan oleh persaingan yang dilakukan oleh Hemiptera, karena kesamaan mulut dan ekologinya. Kerabat primitif capung dan capung (Meganisoptera), yang termasuk serangga terbang terbesar sepanjang masa, juga menurun selama Permian. Holometabola, kelompok serangga modern terbesar, juga melakukan diversifikasi selama ini. "Grylloblattidans", sekelompok serangga bersayap yang dianggap berkerabat dengan penjelajah es modern, mencapai puncak keanekaragamannya pada masa Permian, mewakili sepertiga dari seluruh serangga di beberapa lokasi. Mecoptera (kadang-kadang dikenal sebagai lalat kalajengking) pertama kali muncul pada Permian Awal, dan menjadi beragam pada Permian Akhir. Beberapa mecopteran Permian, seperti Mesopsychidae memiliki belalai panjang yang menunjukkan bahwa mereka mungkin melakukan penyerbukan pada gymnospermae. Kumbang paling awal yang diketahui muncul pada awal zaman Permian.

Kumbang awal seperti anggota Permocupedidae kemungkinan besar bersifat xylophagous, memakan kayu yang membusuk. Beberapa garis keturunan seperti Schizophoridae diperluas ke habitat perairan oleh L

## Poin-Poin Kunci

- Sebelum istilah Permian diperkenalkan, batuan dengan umur yang setara di Jerman dinamai Rotliegend dan Zechstein, dan di Inggris Raya disebut Batu Pasir Merah Baru.
- Periode Permian dibagi menjadi tiga zaman, dari yang tertua hingga yang termuda, yaitu Cisuralian, Guadalupian, dan Lopingian, yang masing-masing dikenal sebagai Permian Awal, Tengah, dan Akhir.
- Nama Seri Cisural diambil dari nama strata yang tersingkap di lereng barat Pegunungan Ural di Rusia dan Kazakhstan.
- Nama Seri Guadalupe diambil dari nama Pegunungan Guadalupe di Texas dan New Mexico, tempat rangkaian laut luas pada zaman ini tersingkap.
- Lopingian pertama kali diperkenalkan oleh Amadeus William Grabau pada tahun 1923 sebagai "Seri Loping" setelah Leping, Jiangxi, Tiongkok.
- Panggung Tatarian Rusia mencakup Lopingian, Capitanian, dan sebagian Wordian, sedangkan Kazanian yang mendasarinya mencakup sisa Wordian serta Roadian.

## Kesimpulan

Kisah kehidupan awal bumi mengingatkan kita bahwa kehidupan yang kita lihat hari ini adalah puncak dari rantai peristiwa yang panjang dan rapuh. Dari mikrob purba hingga hutan yang rimbun, setiap loncatan besar lahir dari perubahan kecil yang bertahan melintasi waktu, dan memahaminya membantu kita menghargai betapa istimewanya planet ini.

en.contentMarkdown:
# The Permian Period: Pangaea, One Giant Continent

Life on Earth did not appear by accident; it is the result of a long journey of trial and error spanning billions of years. This article walks you through the chapters of early life, explaining how simple molecules evolved into complex ecosystems, and the traces we can still read today.

The Permian ( PUR-mee-ən) is a geologic period and stratigraphic system which spans 47 million years, from the end of the Carboniferous Period 298.9 Ma (million years ago) to the beginning of the Triassic Period 251.902 Ma. It is the sixth and last period of the Paleozoic Era; the following Triassic Period belongs to the Mesozoic Era. The concept of the Permian was introduced in 1841 by geologist Sir Roderick Murchison, who named it after the region of Perm in Russia.

The Permian witnessed the diversification of the two groups of amniotes, the synapsids and the sauropsids (reptiles). The world at the time was dominated by the supercontinent Pangaea, which had formed with the collision of Euramerica and Gondwana,during the Carboniferous. Pangaea was surrounded by the superocean Panthalassa. The Carboniferous rainforest collapse left behind vast regions of desert within the continental interior. Amniotes, which could better cope with these drier conditions, rose to dominance in place of their amphibian ancestors.

Various authors have proposed at least three, and possibly four major extinction events in the Permian, though the validity of some of these extinctions has been disputed. The end of the Early Permian (Cisuralian) was marked by a major faunal shift as most lineages of primitive "pelycosaur" synapsids became extinct, being replaced by more advanced therapsids during the Middle Permian (Guadalupian), though the nature of this transition (which may have been an extinction event dubbed "Olson's Extinction") is poorly understood. The end of the Capitanian Stage at the end of the Middle Permian was marked by the major Capitanian mass extinction event, associated with the eruption of the Emeishan Traps. The Permian (along with the Paleozoic) ended with the Permian–Triassic extinction event (colloquially known as the Great Dying), the largest mass extinction in Earth's history (which is the last of the three or four crises that occurred in the Permian), in which nearly 81% of marine species and 70% of terrestrial species died out, associated with the eruption of the Siberian Traps. It took well into the Triassic for life to recover from this catastrophe; on land, ecosystems took 30 million years to recover.

![The Permian Period: Pangaea, One Giant Continent](/images/topics/sejarah-alt.svg)
*Gambar: The Permian Period: Pangaea, One Giant Continent*

## Etymology and history

Prior to the introduction of the term Permian, rocks of equivalent age in Germany had been named the Rotliegend and Zechstein, and in Great Britain as the New Red Sandstone.

The term Permian was introduced into geology in 1841 by Sir Roderick Impey Murchison, president of the Geological Society of London, after extensive Russian explorations undertaken with Édouard de Verneuil in the vicinity of the Ural Mountains in the years 1840 and 1841. Murchison identified "vast series of beds of marl, schist, limestone, sandstone and conglomerate" that succeeded Carboniferous strata in the region. Murchison, in collaboration with Russian geologists, named the period after the surrounding Russian region of Perm, which takes its name from the medieval kingdom of Permia that occupied the same area hundreds of years prior, and which is now located in the Perm Krai administrative region. Between 1853 and 1867, Jules Marcou recognised Permian strata in a large area of North America from the Mississippi River to the Colorado River and proposed the name Dyassic, from Dyas and Trias, though Murchison rejected this in 1871. The Permian system was controversial for over a century after its original naming, with the United States Geological Survey until 1941 considering the Permian a subsystem of the Carboniferous equivalent to the Mississippian and Pennsylvanian.

## Geology

The Permian Period is divided into three epochs, from oldest to youngest, the Cisuralian, Guadalupian, and Lopingian, colloquially known as the Early, Middle and Late Permian, respectively. Geologists divide the rocks of the Permian into a stratigraphic set of smaller units called stages, each formed during corresponding time intervals called ages. Stages can be defined globally or regionally. For global stratigraphic correlation, the International Commission on Stratigraphy (ICS) ratify global stages based on a Global Boundary Stratotype Section and Point (GSSP) from a single formation (a stratotype) identifying the lower boundary of the stage. The ages of the Permian, from youngest to oldest, are:

For most of the 20th century, the Permian was divided into the Early and Late Permian, with the Kungurian being the last stage of the Early Permian. Glenister and colleagues in 1992 proposed a tripartite scheme, advocating that the Roadian-Capitanian was distinct from the rest of the Late Permian, and should be regarded as a separate epoch. The tripartite split was adopted after a formal proposal by Glenister et al. (1999).

Historically, most marine biostratigraphy of the Permian was based on ammonoids; however, ammonoid localities are rare in Permian stratigraphic sections, and species characterise relatively long periods of time. All GSSPs for the Permian are based around the first appearance datum of specific species of conodont, an enigmatic group of jawless chordates with hard tooth-like oral elements. Conodonts are used as index fossils for most of the Palaeozoic and the Triassic.

### Cisuralian

The Cisuralian Series is named after the strata exposed on the western slopes of the Ural Mountains in Russia and Kazakhstan. The name was proposed by J. B. Waterhouse in 1982 to comprise the Asselian, Sakmarian, and Artinskian stages. The Kungurian was later added to conform to the Russian "Lower Permian". Albert Auguste Cochon de Lapparent in 1900 had proposed the "Uralian Series", but the subsequent inconsistent usage of this term meant that it was later abandoned.

The Asselian was named by the Russian stratigrapher V.E. Ruzhenchev in 1954, after the Assel River in the southern Ural Mountains. The GSSP for the base of the Asselian is located in the Aidaralash River valley near Aqtöbe, Kazakhstan, which was ratified in 1996. The beginning of the stage is defined by the first appearance of Streptognathodus postfusus.

The Sakmarian is named in reference to the Sakmara River in the southern Urals, and was coined by Alexander Karpinsky in 1874. The GSSP for the base of the Sakmarian is located at the Usolka section in the southern Urals, which was ratified in 2018. The GSSP is defined by the first appearance of Sweetognathus binodosus.

The Artinskian was named after the city of Arti in Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia. It was named by Karpinsky in 1874. The Artinskian currently lacks a defined GSSP. The proposed definition for the base of the Artinskian is the first appearance of Sweetognathus aff. S. whitei.

The Kungurian takes its name after Kungur, a city in Perm Krai. The stage was introduced by Alexandr Antonovich Stukenberg in 1890. The Kungurian currently lacks a defined GSSP. Recent proposals have suggested the appearance of Neostreptognathodus pnevi as the lower boundary.

### Guadalupian

The Guadalupian Series is named after the Guadalupe Mountains in Texas and New Mexico, where extensive marine sequences of this age are exposed. It was named by George Herbert Girty in 1902.

The Roadian was named in 1968 in reference to the Road Canyon Member of the Word Formation in Texas. The GSSP for the base of the Roadian is located 42.7m above the base of the Cutoff Formation in Stratotype Canyon, Guadalupe Mountains, Texas, and was ratified in 2001. The beginning of the stage is defined by the first appearance of Jinogondolella nankingensis.

The Wordian was named in reference to the Word Formation by Johan August Udden in 1916, Glenister and Furnish in 1961 was the first publication to use it as a chronostratigraphic term as a substage of the Guadalupian Stage. The GSSP for the base of the Wordian is located in Guadalupe Pass, Texas, within the sediments of the Getaway Limestone Member of the Cherry Canyon Formation, which was ratified in 2001. The base of the Wordian is defined by the first appearance of the conodont Jinogondolella aserrata.

The Capitanian is named after the Capitan Reef in the Guadalupe Mountains of Texas, named by George Burr Richardson in 1904, and first used in a chronostratigraphic sense by Glenister and Furnish in 1961 as a substage of the Guadalupian Stage. The Capitanian was ratified as an international stage by the ICS in 2001. The GSSP for the base of the Capitanian is located at Nipple Hill in the southeast Guadalupe Mountains of Texas, and was ratified in 2001, the beginning of the stage is defined by the first appearance of Jinogondolella postserrata.

### Lopingian

The Lopingian was first introduced by Amadeus William Grabau in 1923 as the "Loping Series" after Leping, Jiangxi, China. Originally used as a lithostraphic unit, T.K. Huang in 1932 raised the Lopingian to a series, including all Permian deposits in South China that overlie the Maokou Limestone. In 1995, a vote by the Subcommission on Permian Stratigraphy of the ICS adopted the Lopingian as an international standard chronostratigraphic unit.

The Wuchiapinginan and Changhsingian were first introduced in 1962, by J. Z. Sheng as the "Wuchiaping Formation" and "Changhsing Formation" within the Lopingian series. The GSSP for the base of the Wuchiapingian is located at Penglaitan, Guangxi, China and was ratified in 2004. The boundary is defined by the first appearance of Clarkina postbitteri postbitteri The Changhsingian was originally derived from the Changxing Limestone, a geological unit first named by the Grabau in 1923, ultimately deriving from Changxing County, Zhejiang .The GSSP for the base of the Changhsingian is located 88 cm above the base of the Changxing Limestone in the Meishan D section, Zhejiang, China and was ratified in 2005, the boundary is defined by the first appearance of Clarkina wangi.

The GSSP for the base of the Triassic is located at the base of Bed 27c at the Meishan D section, and was ratified in 2001. The GSSP is defined by the first appearance of the conodont Hindeodus parvus.

### Regional stages

The Russian Tatarian Stage includes the Lopingian, Capitanian and part of the Wordian, while the underlying Kazanian includes the rest of the Wordian as well as the Roadian.

In North America, the Permian is divided into the Wolfcampian (which includes the Nealian and the Lenoxian stages); the Leonardian (Hessian and Cathedralian stages); the Guadalupian; and the Ochoan, corresponding to the Lopingian.

The New Zealand geologic time scale divides the Permian into three epochs, Pre-Telfordian (undivided), D'Urville (divided into the Makarewan, Waiitian, and Puruhauan stages), and Aparima (Flettian, Barrettian, Mangapirian, and Telfordian stages). The Pre-Telfordian epoch corresponds approximately to the Asselian, Sakmarian, and Artinskian stages; the D'Urville epoch is roughly contemporary with the Kungurian stage and Guadalupian epoch; and the Aparima epoch is closely contemporary with the Lopingian epoch.

## Paleogeography

During the Permian, all the Earth's major landmasses were collected into a single supercontinent known as Pangaea, with the microcontinental terranes of Cathaysia to the east. Pangaea straddled the equator and extended toward the poles, with a corresponding effect on ocean currents in the single great ocean ("Panthalassa", the "universal sea"), and the Paleo-Tethys Ocean, a large ocean that existed between Asia and Gondwana. The Cimmeria continent rifted away from Gondwana and drifted north to Laurasia, causing the Paleo-Tethys Ocean to shrink. A new ocean was growing on its southern end, the Neotethys Ocean, an ocean that would dominate much of the Mesozoic Era. A magmatic arc, containing Hainan on its southwesternmost end, began to form as Panthalassa subducted under the southeastern South China. The Central Pangean Mountains, which began forming due to the collision of Laurasia and Gondwana during the Carboniferous, reached their maximum height during the early Permian around 295 Ma, comparable to the present Himalayas, but became heavily eroded as the Permian progressed. The Kazakhstania block collided with Baltica during the Cisuralian, while the North China Craton, the South China Block and Indochina fused to each other and Pangea by the end of the Permian. The Zechstein Sea, a hypersaline epicontinental sea, existed in what is now northwestern Europe.

Large continental landmass interiors experience climates with extreme variations of heat and cold ("continental climate") and monsoon conditions with highly seasonal rainfall patterns. Deserts seem to have been widespread on Pangaea. Such dry conditions favored gymnosperms, plants with seeds enclosed in a protective cover, over plants such as ferns that disperse spores in a wetter environment. The first modern trees (conifers, ginkgos and cycads) appeared in the Permian.

Three general areas are especially noted for their extensive Permian deposits—the Ural Mountains (where Perm itself is located), China, and the southwest of North America, including the Texas red beds. The Permian Basin in the U.S. states of Texas and New Mexico is so named because it has one of the thickest deposits of Permian rocks in the world.

### Paleoceanography

Sea levels dropped slightly during the earliest Permian (Asselian). The sea level was stable at several tens of metres above present during the Early Permian, but there was a sharp drop beginning during the Roadian, culminating in the lowest sea level of the entire Palaeozoic at around present sea level during the Wuchiapingian, followed by a slight rise during the Changhsingian.

## Climate

The Permian was cool in comparison to most other geologic time periods, with modest pole to Equator temperature gradients. At the start of the Permian, the Earth was still in the Late Paleozoic icehouse (LPIA), which began in the latest Devonian and spanned the entire Carboniferous period, with its most intense phase occurring during the latter part of the Pennsylvanian epoch. A significant trend of increasing aridification can be observed over the course of the Cisuralian. Early Permian aridification was most notable in Pangaean localities at near-equatorial latitudes. Sea levels also rose notably in the Early Permian as the LPIA slowly waned. At the Carboniferous-Permian boundary, a warming event occurred. In addition to becoming warmer, the climate became notably more arid at the end of the Carboniferous and beginning of the Permian. Nonetheless, temperatures continued to cool during most of the Asselian and Sakmarian, during which the LPIA peaked. By 287 Ma, temperatures warmed and the South Pole ice cap retreated in what was known as the Artinskian Warming Event (AWE), though glaciers remained present in the uplands of eastern Australia, and perhaps also the mountainous regions of far northern Siberia. Southern Africa also retained glaciers during the late Cisuralian in upland environments. The AWE also witnessed aridification of a particularly great magnitude.

In the late Kungurian, cooling resumed, resulting in a cool glacial interval that lasted into the early Capitanian, though average temperatures were still much higher than during the beginning of the Cisuralian. Another cool period began around the middle Capitanian. This cool period, lasting for 3–4 Myr, was known as the Kamura Event. It was interrupted by the Emeishan Thermal Excursion in the late part of the Capitanian, around 260 million years ago, corresponding to the eruption of the Emeishan Traps. This interval of rapid climate change was responsible for the Capitanian mass extinction event.

During the early Wuchiapingian, following the emplacement of the Emeishan Traps, global temperatures declined as carbon dioxide was weathered out of the atmosphere by the large igneous province's emplaced basalts. The late Wuchiapingian saw the finale of the Late Palaeozoic Ice Age, when the last Australian glaciers melted. The end of the Permian is marked by a temperature excursion, much larger than the Emeishan Thermal Excursion, at the Permian-Triassic boundary, corresponding to the eruption of the Siberian Traps, which released more than 5 teratonnes of CO2, more than doubling the atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration. A -2% δ18O excursion signifies the extreme magnitude of this climatic shift. This extremely rapid interval of greenhouse gas release caused the Permian-Triassic mass extinction, as well as ushering in an extreme hothouse that persisted for several million years into the next geologic epoch, the Triassic.

The Permian climate was also extremely seasonal and characterised by megamonsoons, which produced high aridity and extreme seasonality in Pangaea's interiors. Precipitation along the western margins of the Palaeo-Tethys Ocean was very high. Evidence for the megamonsoon includes the presence of megamonsoonal rainforests in the Qiangtang Basin of Tibet, enormous seasonal variation in sedimentation, bioturbation, and ichnofossil deposition recorded in sedimentary facies in the Sydney Basin, and palaeoclimatic models of the Earth's climate based on the behaviour of modern weather patterns showing that such a megamonsoon would occur given the continental arrangement of the Permian. The aforementioned increasing equatorial aridity was likely driven by the development and intensification of this Pangaean megamonsoon.

### Marine biota

Permian marine deposits are rich in fossil mollusks, brachiopods, and echinoderms. Brachiopods were highly diverse during the Permian. The extinct order Productida was the predominant group of Permian brachiopods, accounting for up to about half of all Permian brachiopod genera. Brachiopods also served as important ecosystem engineers in Permian reef complexes. Amongst ammonoids, Goniatitida were a major group during the Early-Mid Permian, but declined during the Late Permian. Members of the order Prolecanitida were less diverse. The Ceratitida originated from the family Daraelitidae within Prolecanitida during the mid-Permian, and extensively diversified during the Late Permian. Only three families of trilobite are known from the Permian, Proetidae, Brachymetopidae and Phillipsiidae. Diversity, origination and extinction rates during the Early Permian were low. Trilobites underwent a diversification during the Kungurian-Wordian, the last in their evolutionary history, before declining during the Late Permian. By the Changhsingian, only a handful (4–6) genera remained. Corals exhibited a decline in diversity over the course of the Middle and Late Permian.

### Terrestrial biota

Terrestrial life in the Permian included diverse plants, fungi, arthropods, and various types of tetrapods. The period saw a massive desert covering the interior of Pangaea. The warm zone spread in the northern hemisphere, where extensive dry desert appeared. The rocks formed at that time were stained red by iron oxides, the result of intense heating by the sun of a surface devoid of vegetation cover. A number of older types of plants and animals died out or became marginal elements.

The Permian began with the Carboniferous flora still flourishing. About the middle of the Permian a major transition in vegetation began. The swamp-loving lycopod trees of the Carboniferous, such as Lepidodendron and Sigillaria, were progressively replaced in the continental interior by the more advanced seed ferns and early conifers as a result of the Carboniferous rainforest collapse. At the close of the Permian, lycopod and equisete swamps reminiscent of Carboniferous flora survived only in Cathaysia, a series of equatorial islands in the Paleo-Tethys Ocean that later would become South China.

The Permian saw the radiation of many important conifer groups, including the ancestors of many present-day families. Rich forests were present in many areas, with a diverse mix of plant groups. The southern continent saw extensive seed fern forests of the Glossopteris flora. Oxygen levels were probably high there. The ginkgos and cycads also appeared during this period.

### Insects

Insects, which had first appeared and become abundant during the preceding Carboniferous, experienced a dramatic increase in diversification during the Early Permian. Towards the end of the Permian, there was a substantial drop in both origination and extinction rates. By the start of the Permian, there was already an active coevolutionary arms race between insects and plant reproductive structures, evidenced by both insect-caused damage in plants and defensive structures in plants aimed at minimising predation by insects. The dominant insects during the Permian Period were early representatives of Paleoptera, Polyneoptera, and Paraneoptera. Palaeodictyopteroidea, which had represented the dominant group of insects during the Carboniferous, declined during the Permian. This is likely due to competition by Hemiptera, due to their similar mouthparts and therefore ecology. Primitive relatives of damselflies and dragonflies (Meganisoptera), which include the largest flying insects of all time, also declined during the Permian. Holometabola, the largest group of modern insects, also diversified during this time. "Grylloblattidans", an extinct group of winged insects thought to be related to modern ice crawlers, reached their apex of diversity during the Permian, representing up to a third of all insects at some localities. Mecoptera (sometimes known as scorpionflies) first appeared during the Early Permian, going on to become diverse during the Late Permian. Some Permian mecopterans, like Mesopsychidae have long proboscis that suggest they may have pollinated gymnosperms. The earliest known beetles appeared at the beginning of the Permian.

Early beetles such as members of Permocupedidae were likely xylophagous, feeding on decaying wood. Several lineages such as Schizophoridae expanded into aquatic habitats by the L

## Poin-Poin Kunci

- Prior to the introduction of the term Permian, rocks of equivalent age in Germany had been named the Rotliegend and Zechstein, and in Great Britain as the New Red Sandstone.
- The Permian Period is divided into three epochs, from oldest to youngest, the Cisuralian, Guadalupian, and Lopingian, colloquially known as the Early, Middle and Late Permian, respectively.
- The Cisuralian Series is named after the strata exposed on the western slopes of the Ural Mountains in Russia and Kazakhstan.
- The Guadalupian Series is named after the Guadalupe Mountains in Texas and New Mexico, where extensive marine sequences of this age are exposed.
- The Lopingian was first introduced by Amadeus William Grabau in 1923 as the "Loping Series" after Leping, Jiangxi, China.
- The Russian Tatarian Stage includes the Lopingian, Capitanian and part of the Wordian, while the underlying Kazanian includes the rest of the Wordian as well as the Roadian.

## Kesimpulan

The story of early life reminds us that everything alive today is the peak of a long and fragile chain of events. From ancient microbes to lush forests, every great leap began as a small change that endured through time, and understanding it helps us appreciate how special this planet truly is.

id.contentMarkdown:
---
title: "The Compound Effect: Efek Kecil yang Besar"
excerpt: "Memahami bagaimana tindakan kecil sehari-hari, jika dilakukan secara konsisten, dapat menghasilkan perubahan luar biasa dalam kehidupan Anda."
meta_title: "The Compound Effect: Efek Kecil yang Besar | Motivasi"
meta_description: "Pelajari bagaimana the compound effect dapat mengubah hidup Anda melalui tindakan kecil yang konsisten. Strategi praktis untuk produktivitas dan pengembangan diri."
category: "motivasi"
tags: ["compound effect", "konsistensi", "pengembangan diri", "produktivitas", "kebiasaan"]
