## Paleobiologi

Eoraptor dianggap omnivora, meskipun giginya sangat mirip dengan Buriolestes, yang dianggap karnivora. Ia adalah pelari cepat dan, saat menangkap mangsanya, ia akan menggunakan cakar dan gigi untuk mencabik-cabik mangsanya. Tidak seperti dinosaurus karnivora di kemudian hari, ia tidak memiliki sendi geser pada artikulasi rahang bawah, yang dapat digunakan untuk memegang mangsa besar. Selain itu, hanya sebagian giginya yang melengkung dan bertepi gergaji, tidak seperti gigi pada mulut theropoda selanjutnya. Gigi heterodon Eoraptor terdiri dari gigi bergerigi dan melengkung di rahang atas, seperti gigi theropoda, dan gigi berbentuk daun di rahang bawah, seperti gigi sauropodomorph basal. Eoraptor mempunyai 4 gigi di premaxilla dan 18 gigi di maxilla, formula gigi yang tidak berbeda dengan Herrerasaurus.

## Paleoekologi

Selama periode Trias Akhir, Formasi Ischigualasto merupakan dataran banjir aktif secara vulkanik yang ditutupi oleh hutan, dengan iklim hangat dan lembab, namun bergantung pada variasi musiman termasuk curah hujan yang tinggi. Vegetasinya terdiri dari pakis, ekor kuda, dan tumbuhan runjung raksasa, yang membentuk hutan dataran tinggi di sepanjang tepi sungai. Sisa-sisa Herrerasaurus tampaknya merupakan yang paling umum di antara karnivora Formasi Ischigualasto. Sereno (1993) mencatat bahwa Eoraptor ditemukan dalam "hubungan erat" dengan therapsida, rauisuchian, archosaurus, Saurosuchus dan dinosaurus Herrerasaurus dan Pisanosaurus, yang semuanya hidup di lingkungan paleoennya. Herbivora diwakili oleh rhynchosaurus seperti Hyperodapedon; aetosaurus; cynodont seperti Chiniquodon, dicynodont kannemeyeriid seperti Ischigualastia; dan traversodontida seperti Exaeretodon. Jumlah herbivora non-dinosaurus ini jauh lebih banyak dibandingkan dinosaurus awal. Fosil dinosaurus, termasuk Eoraptor hanya mewakili sekitar 6% dari total sampel yang telah ditemukan dari Formasi Ischigualasto (Rogers et al., 1993), yang menunjukkan bahwa jumlah dinosaurus lebih sedikit dibandingkan tetrapoda lainnya.

## Pendalaman: Penemuan

Herrerasaurus diberi nama oleh ahli paleontologi Osvaldo Reig setelah Victorino Herrera, seorang penggembala kambing Andes yang pertama kali melihat fosilnya di singkapan dekat kota San Juan, Argentina, pada tahun 1959. Batuan ini, yang kemudian menghasilkan Eoraptor, adalah bagian dari Formasi Ischigualasto dan berasal dari tahap Carnian akhir pada periode Trias Akhir. Reig menamai dinosaurus kedua dari bebatuan ini dalam publikasi yang sama dengan Herrerasaurus; dinosaurus ini, Ischisaurus cattoi, sekarang dianggap sebagai sinonim junior dan remaja Herrerasaurus.

Reig percaya Herrerasaurus adalah contoh awal karnosaurus, tetapi hal ini menjadi bahan perdebatan selama 30 tahun berikutnya, dan genus tersebut diklasifikasikan secara beragam selama waktu itu. Pada tahun 1970, Steel mengklasifikasikan Herrerasaurus sebagai prosauropoda. Pada tahun 1972, Peter Galton mengklasifikasikan genus tersebut sebagai tidak dapat didiagnosis selain Saurischia. Kemudian, dengan menggunakan analisis kladistik, beberapa peneliti menempatkan Herrerasaurus dan Staurikosaurus di dasar pohon dinosaurus sebelum pemisahan antara ornithischia dan saurischia. Beberapa peneliti mengklasifikasikan sisa-sisa tersebut sebagai non-dinosaurus.

Dua kerangka separa lain dengan bahan tengkorak diberi nama Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis oleh Fernando Novas pada tahun 1986, tetapi spesies ini juga kini dianggap sinonim. Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis ditemukan pada tahun 1975 dan dijelaskan oleh Novas (1986), yang menganggapnya sebagai saurischia primitif dan kemungkinan theropoda. Novas (1992) dan Sereno dan Novas (1992) memeriksa sisa-sisa Frenguellisaurus dan menemukan bahwa mereka merujuk pada Herrerasaurus. Ischisaurus cattoi ditemukan pada tahun 1960 dan dideskripsikan oleh Reig pada tahun 1963. Novas (1992) dan Sereno dan Novas (1992) meninjau sisa-sisanya dan menemukan bahwa mereka juga dapat dirujuk ke Herrerasaurus.

Tengkorak Herrerasaurus lengkap ditemukan pada tahun 1988 oleh tim ahli paleontologi yang dipimpin oleh Paul Sereno. Berdasarkan fosil baru, penulis seperti Thomas Holtz dan José Bonaparte mengklasifikasikan Herrerasaurus di dasar pohon saurischia sebelum perbedaan antara prosauropoda dan theropoda. Namun, Sereno lebih suka mengklasifikasikan Herrerasaurus (dan Herrerasauridae) sebagai theropoda primitif. Kedua klasifikasi ini menjadi yang paling persisten, dengan Rauhut (2003) dan Bittencourt dan Kellner (2004) mendukung hipotesis theropoda awal, dan Max Langer (2004), Langer dan Benton (2006), serta Randall Irmis dan rekan penulisnya (2007) mendukung hipotesis saurischia basal. Jika Herrerasaurus memang merupakan theropoda, hal ini menunjukkan bahwa theropoda, sauropodomorph, dan ornithischia menyimpang bahkan lebih awal dari herrerasaurid, sebelum Carnian tengah, dan bahwa "ketiga garis keturunan secara independen mengembangkan beberapa ciri dinosaurus, seperti sendi pergelangan kaki yang lebih maju atau acetabulum terbuka". Pandangan ini selanjutnya didukung oleh catatan teknologi yang menunjukkan jejak kaki tridaktil (berjari tiga) berukuran besar yang hanya dapat dikaitkan dengan dinosaurus theropoda. Jejak kaki ini berasal dari Formasi Carnian Los Rastros awal di Argentina, yang beberapa juta tahun mendahului Herrerasaurus.

Oleh karena itu, studi tentang dinosaurus awal seperti Herrerasaurus dan Eoraptor memiliki implikasi penting terhadap konsep dinosaurus sebagai kelompok monofiletik (kelompok yang diturunkan dari nenek moyang yang sama). Monofili dinosaurus secara eksplisit diusulkan pada tahun 1970-an oleh Galton dan Robert T. Bakker, yang menyusun daftar sinapomorfi kranial dan pascakranial (ciri-ciri anatomi umum yang berasal dari nenek moyang yang sama). Penulis selanjutnya mengusulkan sinapomorfi tambahan. Sebuah studi ekstensif tentang Herrerasaurus oleh Sereno pada tahun 1992 menunjukkan bahwa dari sinapomorfi yang diusulkan ini, hanya satu fitur kranial dan tujuh fitur pascakranial yang sebenarnya berasal dari nenek moyang yang sama dan yang lainnya disebabkan oleh evolusi konvergen. Analisis Sereno mengenai Herrerasaurus juga membawanya untuk mengusulkan beberapa sinapomorfi dinosaurus baru.

## Pendalaman: Keterangan

Herrerasaurus adalah karnivora bipedal bertubuh ringan dengan ekor panjang dan kepala relatif kecil. Orang dewasa memiliki tengkorak dengan panjang hingga 56 cm (22 inci) dan panjang total hingga 6 m (20 kaki) dan berat 350 kg (770 lb). Spesimen yang lebih kecil memiliki panjang sekitar 4,5 m (15 kaki) dan berat sekitar 200 kg (440 lb).

Herrerasaurus sepenuhnya bipedal. Ia memiliki kaki belakang yang kuat dengan paha pendek dan kaki agak panjang, menunjukkan bahwa ia kemungkinan besar adalah pelari yang gesit. Kakinya mempunyai lima jari, tetapi hanya tiga jari tengahnya (jari II, III, dan IV) yang mempunyai bobot. Jari-jari kaki bagian luar (I dan V) kecil; jari kaki pertama memiliki cakar kecil. Ekornya, sebagian menjadi kaku karena proyeksi tulang belakang yang tumpang tindih, menyeimbangkan tubuh dan juga merupakan adaptasi terhadap kecepatan. Tungkai depan Herrerasaurus kurang dari setengah panjang tungkai belakangnya. Lengan atas dan lengan bawah agak pendek, sedangkan manus (tangan) memanjang. Dua jari pertama dan ibu jari berakhir dengan cakar yang melengkung dan tajam untuk menggenggam mangsa. Digit keempat dan kelima berupa rintisan kecil tanpa cakar.

Herrerasaurus menampilkan ciri-ciri yang ditemukan pada berbagai kelompok dinosaurus, dan beberapa ciri yang ditemukan pada archosaurus non-dinosaurus. Meskipun sebagian besar cirinya mirip dengan dinosaurus, ada beberapa perbedaan, terutama pada bentuk tulang pinggul dan kakinya. Panggulnya seperti dinosaurus saurischia, tetapi ia memiliki tulang acetabulum (tempat pertemuan tulang paha dengan panggul) yang hanya terbuka sebagian. Ilium, tulang pinggul utama, hanya ditopang oleh dua sakral, suatu sifat basal. Namun, pubisnya mengarah ke belakang, suatu sifat turunan seperti yang terlihat pada dromaeosaurid dan burung. Selain itu, ujung pubis memiliki bentuk sepatu bot, seperti pada avetheropoda; dan pusat tulang belakang berbentuk jam pasir seperti yang ditemukan pada Allosaurus.

Herrerasaurus memiliki tengkorak yang panjang dan sempit yang hampir tidak memiliki semua spesialisasi yang menjadi ciri dinosaurus kemudian, dan lebih mirip dengan archosaurus yang lebih primitif seperti Euparkeria. Ia memiliki lima pasang fenestrae (bukaan tengkorak) di tengkoraknya, dua pasang di antaranya untuk mata dan lubang hidung. Di antara mata dan lubang hidung terdapat dua fenestra antorbital dan sepasang lubang kecil seperti celah sepanjang 1 sentimeter (0,39 inci) yang disebut fenestrae promaxillary.

Herrerasaurus memiliki sendi fleksibel di rahang bawah yang dapat meluncur maju mundur untuk menghasilkan gigitan. Spesialisasi tengkorak ini tidak biasa terjadi pada dinosaurus tetapi telah berevolusi secara independen pada beberapa kadal. Bagian belakang rahang bawah juga memiliki fenestrae. Rahangnya dilengkapi gigi bergerigi besar untuk menggigit dan memakan daging, serta lehernya ramping dan fleksibel.

Menurut Novas (1993), Herrerasaurus dapat dibedakan berdasarkan ciri-ciri berikut: adanya fenestra premaxilla-maxilla, dan bagian dorsal fenestra laterotemporal kurang dari sepertiga lebar bagian ventral; adanya rabung pada permukaan lateral tulang jugal, dan fossa supratemporal yang menoreh dalam yang memanjang melintasi proses medial postorbital; proses skuamosa ventral subkuadrat mempunyai depresi lateral, dan tulang kuadratojugal tumpang tindih dengan wajah kuadrat posterodorsal; proses pterigoid kuadrat mempunyai tepi ventral berbentuk palung yang terbalik, dan adanya proses gigi posterodorsal bergaris ramping; tulang surangular mempunyai proses anterior bercabang untuk artikulasi dengan proses gigi posterodorsal; tuberositas internal humerus menonjol ke proksimal dan dipisahkan dari kepala humerus melalui alur yang dalam (juga terdapat pada coelophysoid); memiliki tangan yang membesar, yaitu 60% dari ukuran humerus+radius, dan entepicondyle humerus berbentuk seperti punggung bukit dengan cekungan anterior dan posterior; dan batas posterior tangkai iliaka membentuk sudut siku-siku dengan batas dorsal batang pada iskium.

Menurut Sereno (1993), Herrerasaurus dapat dibedakan berdasarkan ciri-ciri berikut, yang semuanya tidak diketahui pada herrerasaurid lain: lubang melingkar terdapat pada ekepikondilus humerus, ciri yang juga terdapat pada Saturnalia; kondilus ulnaris humerus berbentuk pelana, dan permukaan artikular ulnaris pada ulna berbentuk cembung; permukaan artikular ulnare lebih kecil dibandingkan dengan ulna, suatu ciri yang tidak diketahui pada Staurikosaurus dan Sanjuansaurus; centrale ditempatkan distal ke radiale; proses subnarial yang luas pada premaxilla, dan depresi supratemporal yang luas (dicatat oleh Sereno dan Novas, 1993); umbi basal dan kondilus oksipital lebarnya tidak sama (dicatat oleh Sereno dan Novas, 1993).

## Pendalaman: Klasifikasi

Herrerasaurus awalnya dianggap sebagai genus dalam Carnosauria, yang kemudian mencakup bentuk yang mirip dengan Megalosaurus dan Antrodemus (yang terakhir mungkin setara dengan Allosaurus), meskipun Herrerasaurus hidup jutaan tahun sebelum mereka dan oleh karena itu masih mempertahankan banyak fitur primitif. Klasifikasi karnosaurus ini diubah oleh Rozhdestvensky dan Tatarinov pada tahun 1964, yang mengklasifikasikan Herrerasaurus dalam keluarga Gryponichidae di dalam Carnosauria. Pada tahun yang sama, Walker menerbitkan pendapat berbeda bahwa Herrerasaurus malah bersekutu dengan Plateosauridae, meskipun berbeda dalam memiliki sepatu kemaluan. Walker juga mengusulkan bahwa Herrerasaurus mungkin dekat dengan Poposaurus (sekarang dianggap sebagai pseudosuchian) dan theropoda yang tidak disebutkan namanya dari Dockum Group of Texas (sekarang ditugaskan ke rauisuchian Postosuchus). Pada tahun 1985, Charig mencatat bahwa Herrerasaurus memiliki klasifikasi yang tidak pasti, menunjukkan kemiripan dengan "prosauropoda" dan "karnosaurus". Romer (1966), hanya mencatat bahwa Herrerasaurus adalah prosauropoda yang mungkin termasuk dalam Plateosauridae. Dalam deskripsi Staurikosaurus, Colbert mencatat bahwa ada banyak kesamaan antara taksonnya dan Herrerasaurus, tetapi mengklasifikasikannya dalam famili terpisah, dengan Herrerasaurus di Teratosauridae. Pada tahun 1970, Bonaparte juga mengusulkan kesamaan antara Herrerasaurus dan Staurikosaurus, dan ketika mengklasifikasikan keduanya dengan jelas seperti di Saurischia, dia menyatakan bahwa mereka tampak seolah-olah tidak dapat ditempatkan dalam keluarga saat ini.

Hal ini selanjutnya didukung oleh Benedetto pada tahun 1973, yang menamai taksa tersebut sebagai famili baru Herrerasauridae, yang ia klasifikasikan sebagai saurischians, mungkin dalam Theropoda tetapi tidak dalam Sauropodomorpha. Namun, pada tahun 1977 Galton mengusulkan agar Herrerasauridae hanya mencakup Herrerasaurus, dan menganggapnya sebagai Saurischian incertae sedis.

Dicadangkan pada tahun 1987 oleh Brinkman dan Sues, Herrerasaurus kadang-kadang dianggap asas kepada Ornithischia dan Saurischia, walaupun Brinkmann dan Sues masih menganggapnya berada di dalam Dinosauria. Mereka mendukung hal ini atas dasar bahwa Herrerasaurus memiliki jari kaki V yang besar, dan memiliki dinding medial yang berkembang dengan baik pada acetabulum. Brinkmann dan Sues menganggap Staurikosaurus dan Herrerasaurus tidak membentuk kelompok sejati yang disebut Herrerasauridae, dan sebaliknya mereka merupakan bentuk yang lebih primitif. Selain itu, mereka menganggap karakter yang digunakan Benedetto tidak valid, malah hanya mewakili keadaan plesiomorfik yang ditemukan di kedua taksa. Hal ini tidak disetujui pada tahun 1992 oleh Novas, yang menyatakan banyak sinapomorfi turunan dari Herrerasauridae, seperti sepatu kemaluan yang berbeda, tetapi masih mengklasifikasikannya sebagai basal dari Ornithischia dan Saurischia. Novas mendefinisikan keluarga tersebut sebagai nenek moyang paling tidak umum dari Herrerasaurus dan Staurikosaurus dan semua keturunannya. Definisi Herrerasauridae yang berbeda sebagai klade paling inklusif termasuk Herrerasaurus tetapi bukan Passer domesticus pertama kali dikemukakan oleh Sereno (1998), dan lebih dekat mengikuti inklusi asli yang diusulkan oleh Benedetto. Kelompok lain, Herrerasauria dinamai oleh Galton pada tahun 1985, dan didefinisikan sebagai Herrerasaurus tetapi bukan Liliensternus atau Plateosaurus oleh Langer (2004), yang menggunakan definisi berbasis simpul untuk Herrerasauridae.

Dalam revisi Dinosauria basal, Padian dan May (1993) membahas definisi clade, dan mendefinisikannya kembali sebagai nenek moyang terbaru Triceratops dan burung. Mereka juga mendiskusikan pengaruh definisi ini terhadap taksa paling dasar, seperti Herrerasauridae, dan Eoraptor. Padian dan May menganggap bahwa karena Herrerasauridae dan Eoraptor tidak memiliki banyak ciri diagnostik Saurischia atau Ornithischia, maka mereka tidak dapat dimasukkan ke dalam Dinosauria.

Sebuah studi kemudian pada tahun 1994 oleh Novas malah mengklasifikasikan Herrerasaurus dalam Dinosauria, dan sangat mendukung posisinya dalam Saurischia, serta memberikan sinapomorfi yang dimilikinya bersama Theropoda. Novas menemukan bahwa ciri-ciri primitif yang tidak memiliki fossa brevis dan hanya memiliki dua tulang sakral hanyalah pembalikan yang ditemukan dalam genus tersebut. Pada tahun 1996, Novas melangkah lebih jauh dengan mendukung posisi theropoda untuk Herrerasaurus dengan filogen

## Pendalaman: Etimologi

Nama Ischigualasto berasal dari bahasa Cacán yang telah punah, dituturkan oleh kelompok pribumi yang disebut sebagai Diaguita oleh penjajah Spanyol dan berarti "tempat di mana bulan hinggap". Genus Ischigualastia dan spesies Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis, Pseudochampsa ischigualastensis, Pelorocephalus ischigualastensis dan Protojuniperoxylon ischigualastianus diberi nama setelah formasi tersebut.

## Pendalaman: Pengaturan wilayah

Formasi Ischigualasto terdapat di Cekungan Ischigualasto-Villa Unión, di sepanjang perbatasan antara Provinsi La Rioja dan San Juan, di tanah tandus Argentina Barat. Formasi ini paling banyak diekspos dan dipelajari di Taman Provinsi Ischigualasto (IPP), sebuah taman nasional Argentina dan Situs Warisan Dunia UNESCO yang menempati sebagian besar cekungan di provinsi San Juan. Di bagian barat taman, ketebalan maksimum formasi mencapai 691 meter (2.267 kaki), menyempit menjadi 397 meter (1.302 kaki) di wilayah timur. Sebaliknya, formasinya tipis dan sebagian besar tertutup oleh sedimen terkini di Taman Nasional Talampaya, yang bertetangga dengan Taman Provinsi Ischigualasto di La Rioja di utara. Namun, tidak semua paparan di La Rioja dibatasi. Kawasan Cerro Las Lajas yang sebelumnya terbengkalai, di ujung barat laut cekungan, mempertahankan singkapan setebal 1.059 meter (3.474 kaki) di wilayah geografis kecil. Singkapan lain yang cukup terbuka di La Rioja adalah Cerro Bola, yang menyimpan sedimen sepanjang hampir 800 meter (2.600 kaki).

Cekungan Ischigualasto-Villa Unión adalah sisa dari setengah graben kuno yang melestarikan rangkaian sedimen Trias setebal 3,5 kilometer (11.000 kaki). Formasi Ischigualasto mewakili periode syn-rift kedua di dalam cekungan, yang berarti bahwa sedimennya berpindah dalam interval singkat ketika rifting diaktifkan kembali untuk memperluas cekungan lebih lanjut. Keretakan tersebut diakomodasi oleh pergerakan di Valle Fértil, sebuah patahan aktif di sepanjang tepi barat cekungan.

Secara stratigrafi, formasi tersebut merupakan bagian dari Grup Agua de la Peña, sebuah nama yang mencakup formasi Trias Akhir di Cekungan Ischigualasto-Villa Unión. Formasi Ischigualasto terletak di atas Formasi Los Rastros, satuan pertengahan Carnian yang didominasi oleh batulumpur hijau. Hal ini kemudian ditindih oleh Formasi Los Colorados, yang sebagian besar merupakan batupasir merah berumur Norian. Warna sedimen Formasi Ischigualasto yang relatif pucat sangat kontras dengan pendahulu dan penerusnya, membantu membedakan ketiga formasi di lapangan.

## Pendalaman: Sedimentologi

Formasi Ischigualasto merupakan lingkungan yang didominasi sungai seperti yang ditunjukkan oleh jenis batuannya: lapisan batupasir fluvial (saluran sungai) kasar, dan endapan batupasir, batulempung, dan paleosol dataran banjir yang lebih halus. Tufa bentonit tipis tersebar di seluruh formasi, berasal dari abu vulkanik.

## Pendalaman: Tempat tidur batu pasir

Batuan yang paling kasar dalam formasi ini adalah konglomerat sungai kerikil-batuan saluran lag (yaitu, lapisan kerikil, sedimen sungai pertama yang tenggelam dan terkubur). Ini membentuk lapisan paling bawah dari banyak lapisan batu pasir, terkikis menjadi sedimen berbutir halus di bawahnya. Lapisan datar seperti pita adalah jenis batu pasir sungai yang paling umum, dan beberapa lapisan mempertahankan riak atau bukit pasir di bawah air. Lapisan batupasir yang miring menunjukkan pertambahan sedimen, baik ke arah hilir maupun ke arah lateral (berupa titik batangan). Lapisan batupasir menempati berbagai ukuran dan proporsi, mulai dari endapan saluran tunggal yang relatif kecil (tebal 2 meter, lebar 10 meter), hingga kompleks besar yang terdiri dari beberapa sungai jalinan (tebal 20 meter, lebar 2000 meter). Batupasir dan batulanau juga terdapat di sekitar dataran banjir, dalam bentuk cekungan jurang, saluran terbengkalai, dan endapan tanggul.

Sungai-sungai kuno dan aliran sungai sebagian besar mengalir ke arah utara atau timur laut dari dataran tinggi vulkanik yang mengapit bagian selatan lembah prasejarah. Di tepi tenggara cekungan modern, di mana Formasi Ischigualasto agak tipis, indikator aliran cenderung mengarah ke barat laut, kemungkinan dialihkan oleh aliran basal. Lapisan batupasir juga cenderung lebih kecil dan jumlahnya lebih sedikit di bagian timur cekungan, sedangkan paleosol lebih banyak.

## Pendalaman: Batulumpur dan paleosol

Sebagian besar sedimen dataran banjir berbutir halus. Banyak dari lapisan batulumpur yang lebih kasar merupakan endapan di tepian sungai, terletak di atas saluran-saluran yang terbengkalai dan hamparan jurang. Sedimen terbaik terawetkan sebagai paleosol (tanah fosil), yang terdiri dari delapan varietas, diberi label A hingga H. Paleosol tipe A adalah tanah berpasir yang kaya akan kuarsa dan mika, dengan bintik-bintik tidak jelas, cetakan akar, dan tidak ada struktur internal. Kemungkinan besar merupakan protosol atau entisol, tanah muda yang tumbuh di sepanjang tepian sungai dimana jumlah butir silisiklastik melebihi jumlah bahan organik. Paleosol lainnya sebagian besar ditemukan di antara lapisan batulempung atau batulumpur daripada lapisan berpasir. Paleosol tipe B memiliki proporsi smektit dan mika yang tinggi, sisi licin yang sering, celah berbentuk baji (retakan lumpur pada penampang melintang), dan ciri redoksimorfik yang kuat seperti gleying dan mottling. Mereka dapat diklasifikasikan sebagai jenis vertisol, yang hidup di iklim musiman yang hangat dengan permukaan air yang tinggi hampir sepanjang tahun. Paleosol tipe C mirip dengan tipe B, namun berbeda dalam banyaknya nodul berkapur dan kurangnya fitur redoksimorfik. Meskipun juga merupakan vertisol, mereka berkorelasi dengan iklim yang kurang lembap, yang dibasahi oleh curah hujan berkala dan bukan oleh air tanah.

Paleosol tipe D mempunyai smektit dan kaolinit yang tinggi, bintik-bintik halus, dan banyak sekali bintil hematit dan lapisan lempung (cakrawala argilik). Mereka tergolong argilisols atau alfisols, terkubur di lingkungan yang relatif kering dan stabil seperti hutan, jauh dari pengaruh air. Paleosol Tipe E adalah tanah blok sederhana yang dikemas dengan struktur berkapur dan cakrawala karbonat yang berbeda di samping smektit dan mika. Mereka adalah kalsisol, tanah gurun yang selalu kering dan stabil yang terbentuk di iklim dengan sedikit curah hujan. Paleosol tipe F merupakan peralihan antara tipe D dan tipe E, karena keduanya mempunyai horizon yang kaya akan lempung dan karbonat serta ketiga mineral lempung utama: smektit, mika, dan kaolinit.

Paleosol tipe G dan H berbeda karena berasal dari batuan vulkanik, bukan sedimen. Paleosol tipe G adalah tanah berwarna-warni dan berpasir dengan cakrawala berbeda yang kaya akan smektit, silika, dan besi oksida. Mereka berkembang di atas lapisan abu berbasis feldspar dan merupakan salah satu jenis tanah yang paling luas secara lateral dalam formasi tersebut, karena abu vulkanik menutupi wilayah yang luas tanpa memperhatikan iklim atau ketersediaan air. Paleosol tipe H, sebaliknya, adalah variasi paleosol granular langka yang berkembang di atas lava basal yang telah terdegradasi dan pelapukan selama proses pembentukan tanah.

## Pendalaman: Subdivisi

Formasi ini terbagi menjadi empat anggota di Taman Provinsi Ischigualasto, dengan masing-masing anggota menunjukkan pola sedimentologi dan kandungan fosil yang berbeda. Anggota-anggota ini digambarkan secara informal pada tahun 2006 dan secara resmi diberi nama pada tahun 2009. Dari atas (yang termuda dan tertinggi secara stratigrafi) hingga terbawah (yang tertua dan terendah secara stratigrafi), mereka adalah:

Anggota Quebrada de la Sal (Unit IV): ~60 meter (200 kaki). Anggota berbutir kasar hampir kekurangan kandungan fosil. Sebagian besar sedimen berwarna coklat atau merah, meskipun batulumpur abu-abu atau berbintik-bintik masih terdapat secara sporadis, tidak seperti Formasi Los Colorados di atasnya. Bagian atas anggota (dan Formasi Ischigualasto secara keseluruhan) ditentukan oleh lapisan batulumpur abu-abu terakhir di Cekungan Ischigualasto-Villa Unión. Segala macam fitur batupasir dapat ditemukan di anggota ini. Paleosol terbatas dan mirip dengan anggota La Peña, dengan tipe A dan pada tingkat lebih rendah tipe D sebagai varietas yang paling umum. Paleosol tipe B, F, dan G ada tetapi sangat jarang.

Anggota Valle de la Luna (UNIT III): ~450 meter (1.480 kaki). Anggota paling tebal dalam formasi. Batulumpur dataran banjir kaya smektit berwarna abu-abu tua merupakan litologi yang paling umum, terutama di bagian timur cekungan. Ciri-ciri batupasir merupakan hal yang umum dan berkembang dengan baik di bagian barat cekungan, begitu pula dengan endapan saluran di tepian sungai yang terbengkalai dengan proporsi sedimen berkapur yang tinggi. Fosil tetrapoda terus mengalami penurunan prevalensi dibandingkan dengan anggota sebelumnya, tetapi fosil tumbuhan melimpah secara lokal di endapan saluran yang ditinggalkan. Cekungan bagian barat memiliki proporsi paleosol tipe A, D, dan G yang tinggi, cekungan tengah memiliki lebih banyak tipe B, dan cekungan timur sebagian besar bertipe A dan B. Paleosol tipe C, E, dan F praktis tidak ada di luar cekungan timur.

Anggota Cancha de Bochas (UNIT II): ~130 meter (430 kaki). Anggota berbutir halus terutama terdiri dari batulumpur berbintik-bintik merah/hijau/abu-abu. Fosil berlimpah, terutama pada lapisan paling awal dari anggota tersebut. Nodul berkapur juga banyak dan digunakan untuk membedakan anggota ini dari anggota La Peña dan Valle de la Luna. Slickensides, root cast, dan ciri-ciri perubahan tanah lainnya juga sering dijumpai. Terdapat lapisan batupasir saluran tunggal dan saluran ganda, begitu pula endapan cekungan dan tanggul. Batuan vulkanik tidak hanya mencakup tufa, tetapi juga ekstrusi basal tebal di bagian timur cekungan. Anggota ini menampung semua jenis paleosol kecuali tipe G. Ia juga satu-satunya anggota yang memiliki paleosol tipe H. Tipe A paling umum ditemukan secara keseluruhan, tipe C paling umum di wilayah tengah, dan tipe E, F, dan B paling sering ditemukan di wilayah timur.

Anggota La Peña (UNIT I): ~50 meter (160 kaki). Anggota berbutir kasar dengan fosil yang tidak umum namun terpelihara dengan baik. Basisnya ditentukan oleh lapisan konglomerat saluran masif pertama di atas Formasi Los Rastros. Batupasir fluvial multisaluran umumnya berwarna abu-abu kecoklatan, meskipun endapan saluran tunggal dan batang titik yang terisolasi tampaknya tidak ada, berbeda dengan formasi lainnya. Terdapat endapan cekungan cekungan tetapi tipis dan berlumpur, dan batulumpur dataran banjir berwarna abu-abu kehijauan, berpasir, dan kaya akan smektit. Paleosol jarang ditemukan; cekungan barat mempunyai paleosol tipe A dan sangat jarang tipe D sedangkan cekungan timur sebagian besar mempunyai tipe B.

Singkapan di Cerro Las Lajas malah dibagi menjadi tiga subunit: bagian bawah yang mengandung fosil (11 hingga 310 meter di atas dasar singkapan) dengan endapan sungai yang berkelok-kelok, bagian tengah yang miskin fosil (310 hingga 740 meter di atas dasar) dengan paleosol dengan kelembapan tinggi, dan bagian atas (740 hingga 1070 meter di atas dasar) dengan endapan sungai yang dikepang dan lapisan tufa yang dilas, tetapi tidak ada fosil.

## Pendalaman: Penanggalan radiometrik

Lapisan abu vulkanik yang berlapis-lapis di atas dasar dan di bawah puncak Formasi Ischigualasto di Taman Provinsi Ischigualasto memberikan kontrol kronostratigrafi yang tepat mengenai durasi formasi. Kedua lapisan abu tersebut menghasilkan umur masing-masing 231,4 ± 0,3 Ma dan 225,9 ± 0,9 Ma. Perkiraan usia ini berasal dari penanggalan radiometrik 40Ar/39Ar pada sampel sedimen yang pertama kali dianalisis pada tahun 1993 dan dikalibrasi ulang pada tahun 2011. Formasi secara keseluruhan membentang di batas Carnian-Norian (kira-kira 227 Ma), meskipun keragaman terbesar terjadi pada anggota formasi yang berumur Carnian yang lebih tua (anggota La Peña dan Cancha de Bochas). Pergantian fauna besar-besaran dan hilangnya keanekaragaman terjadi di bagian awal Anggota Valle de la Luna, sesaat sebelum dimulainya Norian. Menurut penanggalan U-Pb, sebuah studi tahun 2021 menerbitkan usia 228,91 ± 0,14 juta tahun yang lalu untuk lapisan abu pada tingkat ini.

Sebuah studi tahun 2020 memperkirakan tiga tufa di Cerro Las Lajas melalui penanggalan U-Pb. Tufa tertua berada pada ketinggian 107 meter di atas dasar singkapan, sesaat sebelum fosil paling awal ditemukan di situs tersebut. Ia memiliki umur 229,25 ± 0,1 juta tahun yang lalu. Tufa kedua, i

## Poin-Poin Kunci

- Tulang dinosaurus primitif ini pertama kali ditemukan pada tahun 1991, oleh ahli paleontologi Universitas San Juan Ricardo Martínez dan Paul Sereno, selama kerja lapangan yang dilakukan oleh Universitas Chicago dan Universitas San Juan.
- Eoraptor adalah dinosaurus kecil, dengan spesimen yang diketahui berukuran panjang 1,2–1,3 m (3,9–4,3 kaki), dan berat sekitar atau kurang dari 10 kg (22 lb).
- Pada tahun 1993 Paul Sereno dan rekan-rekannya mendeskripsikan dan menamai Eoraptor, dan menetapkannya sebagai salah satu dinosaurus paling awal.
- Eoraptor dianggap omnivora, meskipun giginya sangat mirip dengan Buriolestes, yang dianggap karnivora.
- Selama periode Trias Akhir, Formasi Ischigualasto merupakan dataran banjir aktif secara vulkanik yang ditutupi oleh hutan, dengan iklim hangat dan lembab, namun bergantung pada variasi musiman termasuk curah hujan yang tinggi.
- Herrerasaurus diberi nama oleh ahli paleontologi Osvaldo Reig setelah Victorino Herrera, seorang penggembala kambing Andes yang pertama kali melihat fosilnya di singkapan dekat kota San Juan, Argentina, pada tahun 1959.

## Kesimpulan

Dinosaurus bukan sekadar monster dari film; mereka adalah mahakarya evolusi yang mengisi planet ini selama puluhan juta generasi. Semakin kita mempelajarinya, semakin kita menyadari bahwa dunia purba itu penuh dengan kejutan, dan banyak cerita yang masih terkubur menunggu untuk ditemukan.

# Eoraptor: The First Dinosaur on Earth

Few creatures ignite the human imagination like dinosaurs. These animals ruled Earth's landmasses for more than 165 million years, far longer than humans have existed. This article brings you closer to them, from anatomy and behavior to the environments that shaped their lives in the Mesozoic Era.

Eoraptor () is a genus of small, lightly built, basal sauropodomorph dinosaur. One of the earliest-known dinosaurs and one of the earliest sauropodomorphs, it lived approximately 231 to 228 million years ago, during the Late Triassic in Western Gondwana, in the region that is now northwestern Argentina. The type and only species, Eoraptor lunensis, was first described in 1993, and is known from an almost complete and well-preserved skeleton and several fragmentary ones. Eoraptor had multiple tooth shapes, which suggests that it was omnivorous.

![Eoraptor: The First Dinosaur on Earth](/images/topics/dinosaurus.svg)
*Gambar: Eoraptor: The First Dinosaur on Earth*

## History of discovery

The bones of this primitive dinosaur were first discovered in 1991, by University of San Juan paleontologist Ricardo Martínez and Paul Sereno, during field work conducted by the University of Chicago and the University of San Juan. The holotype specimen PVSJ 512 was discovered in muddy siltstone belonging to the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in Argentina. The fossils in this formation were deposited in the Carnian stage of the Triassic period, approximately 235 to 228 million years ago. It took almost 12 months to collect the holotype, which was then shipped to the Field Museum of Natural History in Chicago for preparation by William F. Simpson and Bob Masek. The fossil was first put on display in Chicago and was then returned to San Juan, Argentina, where it went on display at the Museum of Natural Sciences.

The genus Eoraptor was described and named by Paul Sereno, Catherine Forster, Raymond R. Rogers, and Alfredo M. Monetta in 1993. The name is derived from the Greek word eós (ἠώς) meaning 'dawn', a reference to its primitive nature, and the Latin word raptor meaning 'plunderer', a reference to its presumed carnivorous nature and its grasping hand. The specific name lunensis is derived from the Latin words luna ('moon') and the suffix -ensis ('inhabitant'), a reference to its place of discovery: the Valle de la Luna ('Valley of the Moon'), so named for its arid, otherworldly appearance evocative of a lunar landscape. The type species Eoraptor lunensis means 'dawn plunderer from the Valley of the Moon'.

## Description

Eoraptor was a small dinosaur, with the known specimens measuring 1.2–1.3 m (3.9–4.3 ft) in length, and weighing around or less than 10 kg (22 lb). It had a lightly built skull with a slightly enlarged external naris. As in early sauropodomorphs such as Buriolestes and Pampadromaeus and coelophysoids (which would appear millions of years later), Eoraptor had a kink in its upper jaws, between the maxilla and the premaxilla. Paul Sereno et al. (2013) observed that the lower jaw had a mid-mandibular joint. It ran digitigrade, and upright on its hind legs. The femur of the holotype specimen PVSJ 512 is 152 millimetres (6.0 in), and the tibia is 157 millimetres (6.2 in), suggesting that it was a fast runner. Its forelimbs are only half the length of its hindlimbs, suggesting that it was bipedal. All of its long bones have hollow shafts. Eoraptor had five digits on each 'hand', the three longest of which ended in large claws and were presumably used to handle prey. Scientists have surmised that the fourth and fifth digits were too tiny to be of any use in hunting. The ilium is supported by three sacral vertebrae (atypical of the plesiomorphic two sacrals of basal sauropodomorphs), unlike that of the coeval Herrerasaurus which is supported by only two sacrals, a basal trait. Eoraptor had vertebral centra that are hollow, a feature present in some of its ancestors.

The original describers, Paul Sereno et al. (1993), supported the notion that Eoraptor was an adult specimen based on the closure of sutures in the vertebral column, and the partial fusion of the scapulocoracoid. Bonaparte (1996) interpreted the relatively large orbital opening in the skull as a juvenile trait. Ronald Tykoski agreed (2005) and suggested that certain skull features of the type specimen suggested that it was young, specifically, the skull bones are not completely fused, relatively large orbits, and a short snout. Later Sereno et al. (2013) considered the type specimen as a young adult approaching skeletal maturity, considering that it contained traits of both maturity and immaturity.

According to Sereno et al. (1993), Eoraptor can be distinguished based on the fact that its premaxillary and anterior maxillary teeth are leaf-shaped, the external nares are slightly enlarged, and the premaxilla is observed to have a slender posterolateral process. Max Langer and Michael Benton (2006) noted that Eoraptor can be distinguished based on the fact that the proximal part of its fibula is extremely transversely compressed.

## Classification

In 1993 Paul Sereno and his colleagues described and named Eoraptor, and determined it to be one of the earliest dinosaurs. Its age was determined by several factors, not least because it lacked the specialized features of any of the major groups of later dinosaurs, including its lack of specialized predatory features. In 1995, Sereno posited that Eoraptor is the earliest-recorded theropod, and is closest to "the hypothetical dinosaurian condition than any other dinosaurian subgroup." The precise placement of Eoraptor within Dinosauria has been unstable, with opinion often varying between a basal saurischian and a basal theropod. When it was first described by Sereno and Forster in 1993, it was regarded as a theropod, based on its "functionally tridactyl hand" and other anatomical features. In 2011, a study conducted by Hans-Dieter Sues, Sterling J. Nesbitt, David S. Berman and Amy C. Henrici featuring a description of Daemonosaurus, also concluded that there is now enough fossil evidence to confidently classify Eoraptor as a theropod. The study noted that the "transitional suite of character states" of the recently discovered dinosaurs, Daemonosaurus and Tawa further support that Eoraptor is a basal theropod, and not a basal saurischian or a basal sauropodomorph. On the other hand, several studies from 2012 onward have recovered Eoraptor as an early sauropodomorph, rather than a theropod. The following phylogenetic tree illustrates the relationships of Eoraptor among the major theropod groups based on various studies conducted in the 2010s.

Philip Currie (1997) found Eoraptor anatomically closer to what would be considered the ancestral morphotype of both saurischian and ornithischian dinosaurs. In 2011, Martinez et al. (the team that described Eodromaeus) found Eoraptor to be a basal sauropodomorph, with characteristic features from the group. Michael Benton expressed his hesitation to this, and claimed that it is "quite a shift" to remove Eoraptor from Theropoda and then place it in Sauropodomorpha. A subsequent study by Apaldetti, Martinez, Alcober, and Pol published in 2011 found Eoraptor to be a saurischian close to sauropodomorphs and theropods, though was unable to resolve which of the two branches, if either, it fell within. Sereno et al. (2013) redescribed the holotype skeleton and concluded that Eoraptor was not a theropod but a basal sauropodomorph, consistent with the earlier observation made by Martinez et al. (2011).

A large phylogenetic analysis of early dinosaurs by Matthew Baron, David Norman and Paul Barrett (2017) found Eoraptor to be the earliest diverging member of Theropoda, within the larger clade Ornithoscelida. A phylogenetic analysis published with the description of new Buriolestes remains in 2018, based on Langer et al. (2017) placed Eoraptor in a clade of early sauropodomorphs, alongside Buriolestes, Panphagia, Pampadromaeus, and Saturnalia. In their 2025 description of the early bagualosaurian sauropodomorph Huayracursor, Hechenleitner and colleagues recovered Eoraptor as one of the earliest-diverging members of the Sauropodomorpha, diverging after Buriolestes but before all other members of this clade. ## Paleobiology

Eoraptor is thought to have been an omnivore, although its dentition is quite similar to that of Buriolestes, which is considered carnivorous. It was a swift sprinter and, upon catching its prey, it would use claws and teeth to tear the prey apart. Unlike later carnivorous dinosaurs, it lacked a sliding joint at the articulation of the lower jaw, with which to hold large prey. Furthermore, only some of its teeth were curved and saw-edged, unlike those in the mouths of later theropods. The heterodont dentition of Eoraptor consists of both serrated, recurved teeth in the upper jaw, like the teeth of theropods, and leaf-shaped teeth in the lower jaw, like the teeth of basal sauropodomorphs. Eoraptor had 4 teeth in the premaxilla and 18 teeth in the maxilla, a dental formula not dissimilar to that of Herrerasaurus.

## Paleoecology

During the Late Triassic period, the Ischigualasto Formation was a volcanically active floodplain covered by forests, with a warm and humid climate, but subject to seasonal variations including strong rainfall. Vegetation consisted of ferns, horsetails, and giant conifers, which formed highland forests along the banks of rivers. Herrerasaurus remains appear to have been the most common among the carnivores of the Ischigualasto Formation. Sereno (1993) noted that Eoraptor was found in "close association" with therapsids, rauisuchians, archosaurs, Saurosuchus and the dinosaurs Herrerasaurus and Pisanosaurus, all of whom lived in its paleoenvironment. Herbivores were represented by rhynchosaurs such as Hyperodapedon; aetosaurs; cynodonts like Chiniquodon, kannemeyeriid dicynodonts such as Ischigualastia; and traversodontids such as Exaeretodon. These non-dinosaurian herbivores were much more abundant than early dinosaurs. Dinosaur fossils, including those of Eoraptor only represent approximately 6% of the total sample that has been recovered from the Ischigualasto Formation (Rogers et al., 1993), which suggests that dinosaurs were less numerous than other tetrapods.

## Deep Dive: Discovery

Herrerasaurus was named by paleontologist Osvaldo Reig after Victorino Herrera, an Andean goatherd who first noticed its fossils in outcrops near the city of San Juan, Argentina, in 1959. These rocks, which later yielded Eoraptor, are part of the Ischigualasto Formation and date from the late Carnian stage of the Late Triassic period. Reig named a second dinosaur from these rocks in the same publication as Herrerasaurus; this dinosaur, Ischisaurus cattoi, is now considered a junior synonym and a juvenile of Herrerasaurus.

Reig believed Herrerasaurus was an early example of a carnosaur, but this was the subject of much debate over the next 30 years, and the genus was variously classified during that time. In 1970, Steel classified Herrerasaurus as a prosauropod. In 1972, Peter Galton classified the genus as not diagnosable beyond Saurischia. Later, using cladistic analysis, some researchers put Herrerasaurus and Staurikosaurus at the base of the dinosaur tree before the separation between ornithischians and saurischians. Several researchers classified the remains as non-dinosaurian.

Two other partial skeletons with skull material were named Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis by Fernando Novas in 1986, but this species, too, is now thought to be a synonym. Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis was discovered in 1975 and was described by Novas (1986), who considered it a primitive saurischian and possibly a theropod. Novas (1992) and Sereno and Novas (1992) examined the Frenguellisaurus remains and found them referable to Herrerasaurus. Ischisaurus cattoi was discovered in 1960 and described by Reig in 1963. Novas (1992) and Sereno and Novas (1992) reviewed its remains and found them also to be referable to Herrerasaurus.

A complete Herrerasaurus skull was found in 1988 by a team of paleontologists led by Paul Sereno. Based on the new fossils, authors such as Thomas Holtz and José Bonaparte classified Herrerasaurus at the base of the saurischian tree before the divergence between prosauropods and theropods. However, Sereno favored classifying Herrerasaurus (and the Herrerasauridae) as primitive theropods. These two classifications have become the most persistent, with Rauhut (2003) and Bittencourt and Kellner (2004) favoring the early theropod hypothesis, and Max Langer (2004), Langer and Benton (2006), and Randall Irmis and his coauthors (2007) favoring the basal saurischian hypothesis. If Herrerasaurus were indeed a theropod, it would indicate that theropods, sauropodomorphs, and ornithischians diverged even earlier than herrerasaurids, before the middle Carnian, and that "all three lineages independently evolved several dinosaurian features, such as a more advanced ankle joint or an open acetabulum". This view is further supported by ichnological records showing large tridactyl (three-toed) footprints that can be attributed only to a theropod dinosaur. These footprints date from the early Carnian Los Rastros Formation in Argentina, which predates Herrerasaurus by several million years.

The study of early dinosaurs such as Herrerasaurus and Eoraptor, therefore, has important implications for the concept of dinosaurs as a monophyletic group (a group descended from a common ancestor). The monophyly of dinosaurs was explicitly proposed in the 1970s by Galton and Robert T. Bakker, who compiled a list of cranial and postcranial synapomorphies (common anatomical traits derived from the common ancestor). Later authors proposed additional synapomorphies. An extensive study of Herrerasaurus by Sereno in 1992 suggested that of these proposed synapomorphies, only one cranial and seven postcranial features were actually derived from a common ancestor and that the others were attributable to convergent evolution. Sereno's analysis of Herrerasaurus also led him to propose several new dinosaurian synapomorphies.

## Deep Dive: Description

Herrerasaurus was a lightly built bipedal carnivore with a long tail and a relatively small head. Adults had skulls up to 56 cm (22 in) long and were up to 6 m (20 ft) in total length and 350 kg (770 lb) in weight. Smaller specimens were about 4.5 m (15 ft) long and weighed about 200 kg (440 lb).

Herrerasaurus was fully bipedal. It had strong hind limbs with short thighs and rather long feet, indicating that it was likely a swift runner. The foot had five toes, but only the middle three (digits II, III, and IV) bore weight. The outer toes (I and V) were small; the first toe had a small claw. The tail, partially stiffened by overlapping vertebral projections, balanced the body and was also an adaptation for speed. The forelimbs of Herrerasaurus were less than half the length of its hind limbs. The upper arm and forearm were rather short, while the manus (hand) was elongated. The first two fingers and the thumb ended in curved, sharp claws for grasping prey. The fourth and fifth digits were small stubs without claws.

Herrerasaurus displays traits that are found in different groups of dinosaurs, and several traits found in non-dinosaurian archosaurs. Although it shares most of the characteristics of dinosaurs, there are a few differences, particularly in the shape of its hip and leg bones. Its pelvis is like that of saurischian dinosaurs, but it has a bony acetabulum (where the femur meets the pelvis) that was only partially open. The ilium, the main hip bone, is supported by only two sacrals, a basal trait. However, the pubis points backwards, a derived trait as seen in dromaeosaurids and birds. Additionally, the end of the pubis has a booted shape, like those in avetheropods; and the vertebral centra have an hourglass shape as found in Allosaurus.

Herrerasaurus had a long, narrow skull that lacked nearly all the specializations that characterized later dinosaurs, and more closely resembled those of more primitive archosaurs such as Euparkeria. It had five pairs of fenestrae (skull openings) in its skull, two pairs of which were for the eyes and nostrils. Between the eyes and the nostrils were two antorbital fenestrae and a pair of tiny, 1-centimeter-long (0.39 in) slit-like holes called promaxillary fenestrae.

Herrerasaurus had a flexible joint in the lower jaw that could slide back and forth to deliver a grasping bite. This cranial specialization is unusual among dinosaurs but has evolved independently in some lizards. The rear of the lower jaw also had fenestrae. The jaws were equipped with large serrated teeth for biting and eating flesh, and the neck was slender and flexible.

According to Novas (1993), Herrerasaurus can be distinguished based on the following features: the presence of a premaxilla-maxilla fenestra, and the dorsal part of laterotemporal fenestra is less than a third as wide as the ventral part; the presence of a ridge on the lateral surface of the jugal bone, and a deeply incised supratemporal fossa that extends across the medial postorbital process; the subquadrate ventral squamosal process has a lateral depression, and the quadratojugal bone overlaps the posterodorsal quadrate face; the pterygoid process of the quadrate has an inturned, trough-shaped ventral margin, and the presence of a slender ribbed posterodorsal dentary process; the surangular bone has a forked anterior process for articulation with the posterodorsal dentary process; the humerus' internal tuberosity is proximally projected and separated from the humeral head by a deep groove (also present in coelophysoids); possesses enlarged hands, which are 60% of the size of the humerus+radius, and the humeral entepicondyle is ridge-like with anterior and posterior depressions; and the posterior border of the ilial peduncle forms a right angle with the dorsal border of the shaft on the ischium.

According to Sereno (1993), Herrerasaurus can be distinguished based on the following features, all of which are unknown in other herrerasaurids: a circular pit is present on the humeral ectepicondyle, a feature also present in Saturnalia; a saddle-shaped ulnar condyle of the humerus, and the articular surface for the ulnare on the ulna is convex; the articular surface of the ulnare is smaller than that of the ulna, a feature unknown in Staurikosaurus and Sanjuansaurus; the centrale is placed distal to the radiale; a broad subnarial process of the premaxilla, and a broad supratemporal depression (noted by Sereno and Novas, 1993); the basal tuber and the occipital condyle are subequal in width (noted by Sereno and Novas, 1993).

## Deep Dive: Classification

Herrerasaurus was originally considered to be a genus within Carnosauria, which then included forms similar to Megalosaurus and Antrodemus (the latter is probably equivalent to Allosaurus), even though Herrerasaurus lived many millions of years before them and therefore would have retained multiple primitive features. This carnosaurian classification was amended upon by Rozhdestvensky and Tatarinov in 1964, who classified Herrerasaurus within the family Gryponichidae inside Carnosauria. The same year, Walker published a differing opinion that Herrerasaurus instead was allied with Plateosauridae, although it differed in possessing a pubic boot. Walker also proposed that Herrerasaurus may instead be close to Poposaurus (now considered a pseudosuchian) and the unnamed theropod from the Dockum Group of Texas (now assigned to the rauisuchian Postosuchus). In 1985, Charig noted that Herrerasaurus was of uncertain classification, showing similarities to both "prosauropods" and "carnosaurians". Romer (1966), simply noted that Herrerasaurus was a prosauropod possibly within Plateosauridae. In the description of Staurikosaurus, Colbert noted that there were many similarities between his taxon and Herrerasaurus, but classified them in separate families, with Herrerasaurus in Teratosauridae. In 1970, Bonaparte also proposed similarities between Herrerasaurus and Staurikosaurus, and while classifying them both clearly as in Saurischia, he stated that they appeared as though they could not be placed in a current family.

This was further supported by Benedetto in 1973, who named for the taxa the new family Herrerasauridae, which he classified as saurischians, possibly within Theropoda but not in Sauropodomorpha. However, in 1977 Galton proposed that Herrerasauridae only included Herrerasaurus, and found it to be Saurischian incertae sedis.

Proposed in 1987 by Brinkman and Sues, Herrerasaurus has at times been considered basal to Ornithischia and Saurischia, although Brinkmann and Sues still considered it to be inside Dinosauria. They supported this on the basis that Herrerasaurus has a large pedal digit V, and has a well developed medial wall on the acetabulum. Brinkmann and Sues considered Staurikosaurus and Herrerasaurus to not form a true group called Herrerasauridae, and that instead they were successively more primitive forms. Also, they considered the characters used by Benedetto to be invalid, instead representing only the plesiomorphic state that was found in both taxa. This was disagreed with in 1992 by Novas, who stated many derived synapomorphies of Herrerasauridae, such as a distinct pubic boot, but still classified them as basal to Ornithischia and Saurischia. Novas defined the family as the least common ancestor of Herrerasaurus and Staurikosaurus and all its descendants. A differing definition of Herrerasauridae as the most inclusive clade including Herrerasaurus but not Passer domesticus was first suggested by Sereno (1998), and more closely follows the original inclusion proposed by Benedetto. Another group, Herrerasauria was named by Galton in 1985, and defined as Herrerasaurus but not Liliensternus or Plateosaurus by Langer (2004), who used the node-based definition for Herrerasauridae.

In a revision of basal Dinosauria, Padian and May (1993) discussed the definition of the clade, and redefined it as the latest common ancestor of Triceratops and birds. They also discussed what this definition would do to the most basal taxa, such as Herrerasauridae, and Eoraptor. Padian and May considered that since both Herrerasauridae and Eoraptor lack many diagnostic features of Saurischia or Ornithischia, that they could not be considered inside Dinosauria.

A later 1994 study by Novas instead classified Herrerasaurus within Dinosauria, and strongly supported its position within Saurischia, as well as provided synapomorphies that it shared with Theropoda. Novas found that the primitive features of lacking a brevis fossa and having only two sacral vertebrae were simply reversals found in the genus. ## Deep Dive: Etymology

The name Ischigualasto is derived from the extinct Cacán language, spoken by an indigenous group referred to as the Diaguita by the Spanish conquistadors and means "place where the moon alights". The genus Ischigualastia and the species Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis, Pseudochampsa ischigualastensis, Pelorocephalus ischigualastensis and Protojuniperoxylon ischigualastianus were named after the formation.

## Deep Dive: Regional setting

The Ischigualasto Formation is found in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin, along the border between La Rioja and San Juan Provinces, in the badlands of Western Argentina. The formation is most widely exposed and studied in Ischigualasto Provincial Park (IPP), an Argentine national park and UNESCO World Heritage Site which occupies a large portion of the basin in San Juan province. In the western part of the park, the maximum thickness of the formation amounts to 691 metres (2,267 ft), narrowing to 397 metres (1,302 ft) in the eastern area. Conversely, the formation is thin and mostly covered by recent sediments in Talampaya National Park, which neighbors Ischigualasto Provincial Park in La Rioja to the north. Not every exposure in La Rioja is so limited, however. The previously neglected Cerro Las Lajas area, at the northwest tip of the basin, preserves an outcrop up to 1,059 metres (3,474 feet) thick in a small geographic area. Another well-exposed outcrop in La Rioja is Cerro Bola, which preserves nearly 800 metres (2,600 feet) of sediment.

The Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin is the remnant of an ancient half-graben which preserves a 3.5-kilometre (11,000 ft)-thick series of Triassic sediments. The Ischigualasto Formation represents the second syn-rift period within the basin, meaning that its sediments were emplaced during a brief interval when rifting was reactivated to widen the basin further. The rifting was accommodated by movement on Valle Fértil, a dormant fault along the western edge of the basin.

Stratigraphically, the formation is part of the Agua de la Peña Group, a name encompassing Late Triassic formations within the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin. The Ischigualasto Formation overlies the Los Rastros Formation, a mid-Carnian unit dominated by green mudstone. It is subsequently overlain by the Los Colorados Formation, which is primarily Norian-age red sandstone. The comparatively pale color of the Ischigualasto Formation's sediments strongly contrasts with its predecessor and successor, helping to distinguish the three formations in the field.

## Deep Dive: Sedimentology

The Ischigualasto Formation was a river-dominated environment as indicated by its rock types: coarse fluvial (river channel) sandstone beds, and finer floodplain deposits of sandstones, mudstones, and paleosols. Thin bentonite tuffs are scattered through the entire formation, derived from volcanic ash.

## Deep Dive: Sandstone beds

The coarsest rocks in the formation are channel lag pebble-cobble river conglomerates (i.e., gravel beds, the first river sediments to sink and become buried). These form the lowermost layer of many sandstone beds, eroding into underlying fine-grained sediments. Flat, ribbon-like layers are the most common variety of river sandstone, and some layers preserve underwater ripples or dunes. Slanted sandstone layers indicate sediment accretion, either downstream or laterally (in the form of point bars). Sandstone beds occupy a range of sizes and proportions, from relatively small single-channel deposits (2 meters thick, 10 meters wide), up to massive complexes of multiple superimposed braided rivers (20 meters thick, 2000 meters wide). Sandstone and siltstone also occur in the surrounding floodplain, in the form of crevasse splays, abandoned channels, and levee deposits.

The ancient rivers and streams mainly flowed towards the north or northeast from volcanic highlands flanking the southern part of a prehistoric valley. At the southeastern edge of the modern basin, where the Ischigualasto Formation is somewhat thinner, flow indicators trend towards a northwestward orientation, possibly redirected by basalt flows. The sandstone beds also tend to be smaller and less numerous in the eastern part of the basin, while paleosols are more voluminous.

## Deep Dive: Mudstones and paleosols

Most floodplain sediments were fine-grained. Many of the coarser mudstone layers are overbank deposits, laid down over abandoned channels and crevasse splays. The finest sediments are preserved as paleosols (fossilized soil), of which there were eight varieties, labelled A through H. Type A paleosols are sandy soils rich in quartz and mica, with indistinct mottling, root casts, and no internal structure. They were probably protosols or entisols, young soils developing along streambanks where siliciclastic grains outnumber organic material. The other paleosols are mostly found among claystone or mudstone beds rather than sandy layers. Type B paleosols have high proportions of smectite and mica, frequent slickensides, wedge-shaped crevices (mudcracks in cross-section), and strong redoximorphic features such as gleying and mottling. They can be classified are a type of vertisol, emplaced in a warm seasonal climate with a high water table during much of the year. Type C paleosols are similar to type B, yet differ in their abundance of calcareous nodules and a paucity of redoximorphic features. Though also vertisols, they correlate with a less humid climate, moistened by periodic rainfall rather than groundwater.

Type D paleosols have high smectite and kaolinite, fine mottling, and distinctively numerous hematite nodules and clay films (argillic horizons). They are classified as argillisols or alfisols, buried in relatively dry and stable environments such as forests, away from the influence of water. Type E paleosols are simple blocky soils packed with calcareous structures and a distinct carbonate horizon alongside smectite and mica. They are calcisols, perpetually dry and stable desert soils forming in a climate with little precipitation. Type F paleosols are intermediate between type D and type E, since they have both clay- and carbonate-rich horizons and all three major clay minerals: smectite, mica, and kaolinite.

Type G and H paleosols are distinct in that they are derived from volcanic rocks, rather than sediments. Type G paleosols are colorful and sandy soils with distinct horizons rich in smectite, silica, and iron oxides. They develop above feldspar-based ash beds and are among the most laterally extensive soil type in the formation, since volcanic ash covers a broad area without regard to climate or water availability. Type H paleosols, on the other hand, are a rare variety of granular paleosol developing above basalt lavas which have been degraded and weathered during the process of soil formation.

## Deep Dive: Subdivisions

The formation is subdivided four members in Ischigualasto Provincial Park, with each member showing a distinctive pattern of sedimentology and fossil content. These members were informally delineated in 2006 and formally named in 2009. From top (youngest and stratigraphically highest) to bottom (oldest and stratigraphically lowest), they are:

Quebrada de la Sal Member (Unit IV): ~60 metres (200 ft). A coarse-grained member nearly lacking in fossil content. Most sediments are brown or red in color, though grey or mottled mudstones still occur sporadically, unlike the overlying Los Colorados Formation. The upper extent of the member (and the Ischigualasto Formation as a whole) is defined by the last grey mudstone bed in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin. All variety of sandstone features can be found in this member. Paleosols are limited and similar to those of the La Peña member, with type A and to a lesser extent type D as the most common varieties. Type B, F, and G paleosols are present but exceedingly rare.

Valle de la Luna Member (UNIT III): ~450 metres (1,480 ft). The thickest member in the formation. Dark grey smectite-rich floodplain mudstone is the most common lithology, especially in the eastern part of the basin. Sandstone features are common and well-developed in the western part of the basin, as are abandoned channel overbank deposits with a high proportion of calcareous sediments. Tetrapod fossils continue to decrease in prevalence relative to earlier members, but plant fossils are locally abundant in abandoned channel deposits. The western basin has a high proportion of type A, D, and G paleosols, the central basin has more type B, and the eastern basin is mostly type A and B. Type C, E, and F paleosols are practically absent outside of the eastern basin.

Cancha de Bochas Member (UNIT II): ~130 metres (430 ft). A fine-grained member mainly composed of mottled red/green/gray mudstone. Fossils are abundant, especially in the earliest layers of the member. Calcareous nodules are also abundant and used to distinguish this member from the La Peña and Valle de la Luna members. Slickensides, root casts, and other hallmarks of soil alteration are frequently encountered as well. Both single-channel and multi-channel sandstone beds are present, as are crevasse splay and levee deposits. Volcanic rocks include not just tuff, but also a thick basalt extrusion in the eastern part of the basin. This member hosts every type of paleosol except for type G. It is also the only member where type H paleosols are present. Type A is most common overall, type C is the most common in the middle, and types E, F, and B are most frequently found in the eastern area.

La Peña Member (UNIT I): ~50 metres (160 ft). A coarse-grained member with uncommon but well-preserved fossils. Its base is defined by the first massive channel conglomerate layer above the Los Rastros Formation. Multi-channel fluvial sandstone is common and tannish-grey in color, though isolated single-channel and point bar deposits are seemingly absent, in contrast to the rest of the formation. Crevasse splay deposits are present but thin and silty, and floodplain mudstone is greenish-gray, sandy, and rich in smectite. Paleosols are uncommon; the western basin has type A and very rare type D paleosols while the eastern basin mostly has type B.

The outcrop at Cerro Las Lajas is instead divided into three subunits: a fossiliferous lower section (11 to 310 meters above the base of the outcrop) with meandering river deposits, a fossil-poor middle section (310 to 740 meters above base) with high-humidity paleosols, and an upper section (740 to 1070 meters above base) with braided river deposits and welded tuff beds, but no fossils.

## Deep Dive: Radiometric dating

Interlayered volcanic ash layers above the base and below the top of the Ischigualasto Formation in Ischigualasto Provincial Park provide precise chronostratigraphic control on the formation's duration. The two ash beds have yielded ages of 231.4 ± 0.3 Ma and 225.9 ± 0.9 Ma, respectively. These age estimates were derived from 40Ar/39Ar radiometric dating on sediment samples first analyzed in 1993 and recalibrated in 2011. The formation as a whole spans the Carnian-Norian boundary (at approximately 227 Ma), though the greatest diversity occurs in the older Carnian-age members of the formation (the La Peña and Cancha de Bochas members). A major faunal turnover and loss of diversity occurs in the early part of the Valle de la Luna Member, shortly before the start of the Norian. According to U-Pb dating, a 2021 study published an age of 228.91 ± 0.14 Ma for an ash bed at this level.

A 2020 study dated three tuffs at Cerro Las Lajas via U-Pb dating. The oldest tuff is at 107 meters above the base of the outcrop, shortly before the earliest fossils at the site. It has an age of 229.25 ± 0.1 Ma. The second tuff, i

## Poin-Poin Kunci

- The bones of this primitive dinosaur were first discovered in 1991, by University of San Juan paleontologist Ricardo Martínez and Paul Sereno, during field work conducted by the University of Chicago and the University of San Juan.
- Eoraptor was a small dinosaur, with the known specimens measuring 1.2–1.3 m (3.9–4.3 ft) in length, and weighing around or less than 10 kg (22 lb).
- In 1993 Paul Sereno and his colleagues described and named Eoraptor, and determined it to be one of the earliest dinosaurs.
- Eoraptor is thought to have been an omnivore, although its dentition is quite similar to that of Buriolestes, which is considered carnivorous.
- During the Late Triassic period, the Ischigualasto Formation was a volcanically active floodplain covered by forests, with a warm and humid climate, but subject to seasonal variations including strong rainfall.
- Herrerasaurus was named by paleontologist Osvaldo Reig after Victorino Herrera, an Andean goatherd who first noticed its fossils in outcrops near the city of San Juan, Argentina, in 1959.

## Kesimpulan

Dinosaurs were not movie monsters; they were masterpieces of evolution that filled this planet for tens of millions of generations. The more we study them, the more we realize how surprising the ancient world was, and how many stories still lie buried, waiting to be found.
