# Pantone and Spot Colors in CorelDRAW


![Pantone and Spot Colors in CorelDRAW — ilustrasi topik](/images/topics/coreldraw.svg)
*Image: Pantone and Spot Colors in CorelDRAW*

Every designer eventually faces this classic moment: a client arrives disappointed because their logo's color on brochure A doesn't exactly match what appeared on print shop B's banner. Same file, same conversation — different result. This is where two crucial terms enter the meeting room: **spot color** and **Pantone**.

Together they represent the printing industry's answer to one fundamental problem: how do you guarantee a color looks identical on any machine, in any city, in any year? This article digs into the concept from its roots — single-ink philosophy versus CMYK mixing, the fascinating story of Pantone's birth inside a near-bankrupt print company, the intricate details of its numbering system, practical usage in software like **CorelDRAW**, and the family of color systems most people never hear about.

## Spot Color vs Process Color: Two Ink Philosophies

Start with the technical definitions. In **offset printing**, a ***spot color*** (or *solid color*) is any color generated by an ink — pure or mixed — that is printed using **a single run**. By contrast, a ***process color*** is produced by printing a series of dots of different colors that blend in the viewer's eye.

The most widespread offset process itself consists of four spot colors: **cyan, magenta, yellow, and key (black)** — known as **CMYK**. The majority of the world's printed material runs through this process. More advanced workflows use six spot colors (the **hexachromatic process**, CMYKOG), adding **orange and green** to compensate for CMYK's weak reproduction of faint tints.

But offset technicians worldwide use *spot color* even more specifically: any color from a **non-standard ink** — metallic, fluorescent, or custom hand-mixed. The production consequences are clear: every spot color requires its own lithographic film; all areas sharing a spot color print from the same film — meaning the same lithographic plate. Each spot's dot gain, screen angle, and line frequency get tuned to its purpose. Even spot lamination and UV coatings are sometimes called "spot colors" — they share the defining traits: separate film, separate print run.

## The Pantone Story: From $50,000 Debt to Global Standard

Pantone began in New Jersey in the 1950s as the commercial printing company of brothers Mervin and Jesse Levine — M & J Levine Advertising. In 1956, they hired a recent Hofstra University graduate named **Lawrence Herbert** as a part-time employee. Herbert applied his chemistry knowledge to systematize and simplify the company's stock of pigments and production of colored inks.

By 1962, Herbert was running the ink and printing division at a profit while the commercial-display division sat US$50,000 in debt. He purchased the company's technological assets from the Levine Brothers for US$50,000 (roughly $530,000 in today's money) — and renamed it "**Pantone**."

Its flagship product became legendary: **Pantone Guides** — stacks of thin cardboard or plastic sheets, roughly 6×2 inches (15×5 cm), printed on one side with series of related color swatches and bound into small *fan decks*. One "page" might hold several yellows at varying tints. The idea behind it all was elegant: letting designers perform ***color matching*** when designs enter production — **regardless of the equipment producing the color**. Graphic designers and reproduction houses adopted it widely.

Operational details reveal how seriously color is taken: Pantone recommends repurchasing guides **annually**, because the swatch inks yellow over time. Color variance occurs within editions depending on paper stock (coated, matte, uncoated), and between editions whenever the specific stock changes.

The corporate journey twisted too: X-Rite, a supplier of color measurement instruments and software, bought Pantone for **US$180 million in October 2007**. X-Rite was then acquired by Danaher Corporation in 2012, and in September 2023 its business segment (including Pantone) spun off as Veralto. A modern shockwave hit the design community in **2022**: the Pantone–Adobe dispute removed Pantone color coordinates from Photoshop and other Adobe software — colors in artists' digital documents turned black unless they paid a separate $15 monthly subscription. Artists accused both companies of holding their work hostage.

## How the PMS Works, Down to Its Numbers

At its heart, the **Pantone Color Matching System (PMS)** is a standardized color reproduction system — holding **2,161 colors as of 2019**. With standardized colors, different manufacturers in different locations can reference the same system and guarantee matches **without ever contacting each other**.

Beneath those numbers lies careful ink architecture. About **30% of the system's 1,114 spot colors** (as of year 2000) **cannot be simulated with CMYK** — instead they're mixed from **13 base pigments** (14 including black) in specified amounts, called base colors. The numbering history runs deep: 387 colors numbered 100–487 arrived in 1975; lighter shades 600–732 followed in 1991; original four-digit colors introduced in 1987 were remapped into three digits.

The system also opened doors for special colors: **metallics**, **fluorescents/neons**, and **pastels** — each with dedicated number ranges, like 56 fluorescents (801–814 and 901–942, the first seven being Dayglo-era base colors), packaging metallics at 10101–10454 with base Silver 10077 and Rose Gold 10412, plus pastels at 9140–9163. Since most Pantone colors sit **outside the printable CMYK gamut**, only in **2001** did Pantone begin providing screen-based RGB translations — many still falling outside sRGB. A companion system called **Goe** (launched September 2007 with 2,058 new colors, ten base colors plus clear coating, complete with GoeSticks and an online community) was discontinued in November 2013 — though its four new base colors were inherited into PMS.

## Why Brands — Even Nations — Love Spot Color

Pantone colors are described by allocated numbers — say, "PMS 130" — and are almost always used in **branding**: logos and marketing collateral need standardized inks that match consistently across presses, print runs, and suppliers.

The phenomenon scales up to nations: Pantone colors have entered **government legislation and military standards** describing flag and seal colors. In January 2003, the Scottish Parliament debated petition PE512 to officially call the blue of Scotland's flag "***Pantone 300***." Canada, South Korea, motorsport's FIA, and US states like Texas have all designated specific Pantone colors for their flags.

There's even a dark side that turns beneficial: because the process is complicated, spot colors effectively **prevent counterfeiting** of money, passports, bonds, and other critical documents. Banknote printing uses secret spot-color formulae — some visible to the naked eye, others appearing only under special lights or chemicals. Russia's banknotes offer a visible example, printed with metallic spot colors.

## Practice in CorelDRAW and Other Design Software

For **CorelDRAW** users, good news: it's officially listed among applications capable of generating spot colors as **additional channels** in prepress artwork — alongside Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, QuarkXPress, and Scribus. The typical workflow: objects destined for spot printing receive a spot swatch (a specific PMS color) instead of a CMYK mix, so when exported to the print workflow, that color exits as a separate channel ready for its own film and plate.

Its neighbor Photoshop has distinctive tricks of its own: generating ***soft edges*** (feathered edges) for spot colors, plus dissolve effects from layer patterns applicable to any spot color — useful for clear varnish areas meant to fade gently. But one economic principle always applies: **cost and risk grow with every added spot color** — process inks and films multiply in complexity, and each print needs additional runs. The golden rule: reserve spot colors for hues that truly demand precision — usually one or two brand colors — and let everything else work in CMYK.


![Pantone and Spot Colors in CorelDRAW](/images/topics/desain-alt.svg)
*Image: Pantone and Spot Colors in CorelDRAW*

## The Bigger Family: Color Systems Beyond Pantone

Though Pantone dominates the United States and Europe, it isn't alone. Spot color classification has produced thousands of discrete colors with unique names or numbers across industry standards:

- **Toyo Ink** (the Toyo Color Finder System) — common in Japan;
- **DIC Color System Guide** — also Japanese, built on Munsell color theory;
- **ANPA color palette** — 300 colors from America's newspaper publishers association for newspaper work;
- **GCMI** — package-printing color standards from the Glass Packaging Institute;
- **HKS** — a system from three German ink manufacturers (Hostmann-Steinberg, Kast + Ehinger, H. Schmincke & Co) containing 120 spot colors and 3,250 tones for coated and uncoated papers;
- **RAL CLASSIC** — Europe's color matching system, mainly used for varnish and powder coating.

And here's the closing caveat: because each system creates its colors from scratch, **spot colors from one system may be impossible to find within another's library**. Cross-system conversion is always approximation, never perfect equivalence.

## Spot Color in a Real Production Pipeline

Understanding where spot colors travel after leaving your design file makes every workflow decision clearer. The journey typically looks like this: your layout assigns a named spot swatch to specific objects; during prepress, the file separates into plates — one per ink; each spot color generates its own lithographic film; that film burns its own plate; and the press applies the ink in its dedicated run.

Every stage carries tunable variables: dot gain, screen angle, and line frequency for each spot get calibrated according to purpose — fine text needs different settings than broad flood areas. Special finishes ride the same rails: since spot lamination and UV coatings also demand separate films and runs, printers treat them as honorary spot colors when quoting jobs. And digital embellishments follow suit — techniques like clear dry ink on production presses even allow feathered, soft-edged spot areas: think a varnish layer that fades gracefully over a product photo, masked precisely in Photoshop before entering the spot channel.

The economics deserve respect at every step. Each additional spot multiplies setup complexity — more films, more plates, more press passes, more chances for misregistration. That's why seasoned designers audit their files before sending them out: is this fifth spot color truly earning its keep, or can it live happily inside CMYK?

## Pantone Beyond the Pressroom: Culture, Fashion, and Lessons Learned

Pantone's empire stretches far beyond ink cans. Its color management spans design-to-production workflows across physical and digital formats — coated and uncoated paper stocks, cotton, polyester, nylon, even plastics — serving graphic design, fashion design, product design, textiles, and manufacturing alike. When a fashion house dyes fabric or an appliance maker colors polymer housings, the same numbered language keeps everyone honest.

Its cultural footprint grew famous too: the annual *Color of the Year* announcement routinely makes mainstream news — as early as 2007, media attention greeted the choice of blue iris, No. 18-3943, partly by the company's own design. A color-naming company becoming a trendsetting institution is one of branding history's quiet miracles.

But recent years delivered a sobering lesson too. The 2022 Adobe dispute — coordinates vanishing from Photoshop, documents turning black, a $15 monthly ransom — exposed how dependent creative workflows had become on proprietary color data living inside someone else's software. Whatever settlement followed, the takeaway endures: maintain your own records of critical brand colors, understand which values are physical standards versus licensed approximations, and never let a subscription lapse decide what your logo looks like.

And remember the cross-system reality from earlier: Toyo, DIC, HKS, RAL, ANPA, GCMI — each builds colors from scratch, so perfect matches across systems don't exist. International projects should therefore anchor specs to one primary system with documented approximations elsewhere. Precision in color, like precision everywhere in design, is less about perfection and more about disciplined communication.

## Three Questions Before Committing a Spot Color

Let's end the technical journey with a decision filter you can apply in any client meeting:

**Question one: Does the brand demand exact matching across suppliers?** If a logo appears on packaging from three factories, signage from two fabricators, and merchandise from an online marketplace — standardized PMS inks are the only reliable contract. Consistency across presses, runs, and vendors is precisely what spot colors were invented for.

**Question two: Does the color live outside CMYK's gamut?** Metallics, fluorescents, and many saturated hues physically cannot be simulated by four process inks — remember, roughly 30% of Pantone spot colors resist CMYK simulation entirely. If the brand identity depends on such a hue (a Rose Gold base, a Dayglo-era fluorescent), CMYK isn't an option; it's a betrayal.

**Question three: Does the budget tolerate extra runs?** Every added spot means additional films, plates, and press passes — costs that multiply across reprint cycles. If the answer is no, negotiate: can the identity survive a documented CMYK approximation for secondary applications while reserving true spot printing for hero items like business cards and flagship packaging?

Answer all three honestly, and the choice makes itself. Add two housekeeping habits: replace aging swatch guides annually since their inks yellow over time — and always confirm which paper stock (coated, matte, uncoated) your guide represents, because the same PMS number shifts between stocks. Color precision is ultimately a maintenance discipline, not a one-time purchase.

## Conclusion

Spot colors and Pantone teach a big lesson about professional design: beauty on screen is only half the job — the other half is ensuring that color reproduces identically in the physical world, on machines you've never seen, in cities you've never visited. From Lawrence Herbert's pigment chemistry in 1962, to fan decks replaced yearly against yellowing, to 13 base pigments mixing hues beyond CMYK's reach, to parliaments debating "Pantone 300" for national flags — everything converges on one obsession: consistency.

The practice inside CorelDRAW now makes sense too: a spot color isn't just another palette entry but a production promise — separate channel, separate film, extra press run, and costs that need justification. Use it for brand colors that can't afford mistakes, simulate the rest in CMYK, and communicate your choices to the printer from day one.

And once you understand why a color needs a name and number — why "blue" isn't enough, but must become "Pantone 300" — you've changed classes: from someone who designs images, to someone who engineers color reality across machines, media, and continents.

# Era Reiwa: Kaisar Baru, Harapan Baru untuk Jepang


![Era Reiwa — ilustrasi topik](/images/topics/sejarah-jepang.svg)
*Gambar: Era Reiwa*

Pada siang hari tanggal 1 April 2019, jutaan orang Jepang menempel di depan layar televisi kantor mereka, warung ramen, dan stasiun kereta. Semua menunggu satu hal: pengumuman nama zaman baru negara itu. Ketika Sekretaris Kabinet Yoshihide Suga mengangkat papan kaligrafi bertuliskan dua kanji sederhana — **令和**, Reiwa — gelombang pencarian internet langsung melumpuhkan server di seluruh negeri. Dalam beberapa jam, seluruh Jepang belajar cara menulis nama zamannya sendiri. Tidak ada drama, tidak ada kontroversi besar, hanya rasa penasaran kolektif yang hangat dan sedikit terharu.

Era Reiwa resmi dimulai pada 1 Mei 2019, sehari setelah Kaisar Akihito turun takhta, ketika putranya naik sebagai **Kaisar Naruhito**, kaisar ke-126 dalam garis takhta tertua dunia. Berbeda dengan Heisei yang dibuka oleh wafatnya seorang kaisar, Reiwa dibuka oleh sebuah pilihan: seorang pria yang memilih pensiun dengan hormat agar negerinya tidak terbebani. Dan sebagaimana zaman-zaman lain dalam sejarah Jepang, era ini segera diuji oleh peristiwa-peristiwa yang tidak ada dalam skenario mana pun — pandemi global, Olimpiade tanpa penonton, pembunuhan mantan perdana menteri, gempa di malam tahun baru, hingga rekor pasar saham yang menunggu 34 tahun untuk pecah.

## Makna di Balik Dua Kanji 令和

Setiap nama era di Jepang selalu menyimpan pesan, dan Reiwa menyimpan salah satu pesan paling indah. Kanji pertama, **rei** 令, memiliki arti baik, mulia, atau perintah; kanji kedua, **wa** 和, berarti harmoni atau damai. Terjemahan resmi pemerintah Jepang ke bahasa Inggris memilih frasa *beautiful harmony*, keselarasan nan indah, sementara sebagian sarjana menafsirkannya lebih luas sebagai kedamaian yang lahir dari keteraturan yang baik.

Yang membuat Reiwa istimewa bukan hanya maknanya, tetapi asal-usulnya. Selama lebih dari seribu tahun, semua nama era Jepang diambil dari kitab-kitab klasik Tionghoa. Reiwa memecah tradisi itu total: namanya diambil dari **Man'yōshū**, antologi puisi tertua Jepang yang disusun pada abad kedelapan. Sumbernya adalah prakata sebuah rangkaian puisi tentang bunga plum yang digubah oleh Ōtomo no Tabito, yang menggambarkan suasana awal musim semi: bulan yang elok, udara yang bersih, angin yang tenang, para sahabat berkumpul menikmati keindahan bersama.

Pilihan ini disengaja dan penuh simbolisme. Dengan mengambil nama dari sastra Jepang sendiri, negara itu seperti berkata bahwa zamannya kini berdiri di atas akarnya sendiri, bukan pinjaman dari luar. Bagi banyak orang Jepang, momen pengumuman Reiwa menjadi refleksi nasional tentang identitas: bangsa yang cukup percaya diri untuk merujuk pada keindahan budayanya sendiri.

### Proses Pemilihan Nama yang Rahasia

Cara nama ini dipilih juga menarik untuk diketahui. Sebuah panel berisi sembilan cendekiawan lintas bidang — dari peraih Nobel hingga penulis novel ternama — diminta mengusulkan kandidat nama secara rahasia. Pemerintah kemudian menyaring, berunding dengan parlemen, dan menyerahkan keputusan akhirnya kepada kabinet. Bahkan keluarga kekaisaran tidak ikut menentukan. Hasilnya diumumkan dengan upacara sederhana: sekretaris kabinet mengangkat papan bertuliskan nama zaman di hadapan kamera dunia.

Reiwa bahkan meninggalkan jejak di dunia teknologi. Konsorsium Unicode menciptakan titik kode khusus, U+32FF, untuk glif gabungan dua kanji Reiwa — sesuatu yang belum pernah dilakukan untuk nama era mana pun sebelumnya. Kalender Jepang bergaya nenggō yang dicetak di dokumen resmi, tiket kereta, dan kartu nama pun otomatis berganti tahun: tahun 2019 menjadi Reiwa 1, dan begitu seterusnya hingga kini.

## Transisi Takhta: Menyambut Kaisar ke-126

Keesokan harinya setelah pengumuman nama, tepatnya 30 April 2019, Jepang menyaksikan upacara turun taktha yang belum terjadi selama dua abad. Kaisar Akihito, yang telah memerintah tiga puluh tahun penuh empati, melepaskan jabatannya secara sukarela melalui undang-undang khusus. Keesokan paginya, 1 Mei 2019, Putra Mahkota Naruhito duduk di takhta sebagai kaisar ke-126, dan era Reiwa dimulai.

Naruhito membawa gaya kepemimpinan simbolis yang berbeda dari ayahnya, namun sama hangatnya. Ia lulusan Universitas Oxford yang meneliti sejarah transportasi air Sungai Thames, fasih berbahasa Inggris, dan dikenal sebagai pendukung vokal kesetaraan gender serta hak penyandang disabilitas. Permaisurinya, **Masako**, adalah mantan diplomat karier lulusan Harvard yang pernah berjuang melawan tekanan hidup istana, kisah yang membuat banyak perempuan Jepang merasakan kedekatan personal dengan pasangan kekaisaran ini.

Dalam pidato-pidato awalnya, Naruhito menegaskan komitmennya mendekatkan diri pada rakyat, menghayati penderitaan mereka, dan menjaga perdamaian — nada yang sangat relevan bagi generasi yang semakin jarang mendengar cerita langsung tentang peperangan. Transisi yang lancar dan khidmat ini menjadi bukti bahwa monarki simbolik Jepang dapat beradaptasi dengan zaman tanpa kehilangan martabatnya.

## Tahun Pertama yang Penuh Harapan

Beberapa bulan pertama era Reiwa terasa seperti musim semi yang sesungguhnya. Pada Juni 2019, Osaka menjadi tuan rumah KTT G20 pertama yang digelar di Jepang, mempertemukan para pemimpin dunia di kota dagang tua itu. Wisatawan asing membanjiri negeri ini dalam jumlah rekor, mata uang yen relatif kuat, dan semangat kebangkitan pasca-era Heisei terasa nyata. Orang-orang memberi nama anak dengan kanji yang dipakai di Reiwa, produk-produk edisi spesial era baru laris di pasaran, dan kalimat pembuka surat kabar resmi berganti menjadi salam Reiwa.

Ada juga momen-momen kecil yang menghangatkan hati saat itu. Kaisar Naruhito melakukan kunjungan pertamanya ke wilayah-wilayah yang masih memulihkan diri dari bencana Heisei, menegaskan pesan bahwa era baru tidak akan melupakan luka lama. Debat publik tentang masa depan keluarga kekaisaran juga terbuka lebih lebar, termasuk pertanyaan yang selama ini tabu: apakah seorang perempuan boleh naik takhta, mengingat Putri Aiko adalah anak tunggal pasangan kekaisaran. Reiwa tampak siap menjadi era keterbukaan.

Namun alam semesta punya rencana lain. Di penghujung tahun pertama itu, sebuah virus bernama SARS-CoV-2 mulai menyebar diam-diam dari Wuhan, dan dunia — termasuk Jepang — belum tahu bahwa dekade barunya akan dimulai dengan ujian terbesarnya.

## Pandemi yang Mengubah Segalanya

Awal 2020, pandemi COVID-19 melanda Jepang seperti melanda seluruh planet. Pemerintah menerapkan keadaan darurat yang meminta warga mengurangi mobilitas, gedung-gedung ditutup, masker menjadi bagian wajib penampilan harian, dan jalanan Tokyo yang biasanya sesak berubah sunyi seperti film fiksi ilmiah. Ekonomi wisata yang sedang memuncak tiba-tiba kolaps, dan perusahaan-perusahaan belajar bekerja dari rumah dengan susah payah.

Pandemi ini juga menampar Jepang dengan cermin yang jujur. Negara yang terkenal canggih ternyata masih bergantung pada mesin faks dan dokumen kertas, sehingga pemerintahan pun mendirikan **Badan Digital** pada 2021 untuk mempercepat transformasi digital birokrasi. Sistem kesehatan diuji batas-batasnya, dan kesenjangan ekonomi antara pekerja tetap dan tidak tetap melebar saat pandemi memukul sektor jasa tempat mayoritas kaum muda bekerja.

Yang patut diapresiasi adalah respons sosialnya. Tidak ada konflik besar soal masker atau vaksin seperti di sebagian negara Barat. Warga Jepang menaati protokol dengan ketertiban khas mereka, kampanye vaksinasi berjalan efektif setelah start lambat, dan masyarakat kembali membuktikan kekuatan kohesinya di masa sulit. Pandemi juga menggeser prioritas politik: perhatian beralih ke ketahanan rantai pasokan, kemandirian produksi semikonduktor, dan kesejahteraan pekerja digital.

## Olimpiade Tokyo 2020: Panggung yang Ditunda

Tidak ada peristiwa yang lebih melambangkan pergulatan era Reiwa awal selain Olimpiade Tokyo 2020. Digelar pertama kali di Jepang modern sebagai simbol kebangkitan, olimpiade ini harus ditunda satu tahun — penundaan pertama dalam sejarah Olimpiade modern — karena pandemi. Anggaran membengkak, opini publik terbelah, dan banyak orang Jepang menuntut pembatalan total demi keselamatan.

Namun pada Juli 2021, api olimpiade tetap menyala di Stadion Nasional Tokyo, tanpa penonton domestik di tribun. Meski suasananya hampa, pertandingan itu memberi dunia momen hariah yang langka di tengah pandemi: atlet-atlet bertanding dengan masker, podium yang disambut tepuk tangan kosong, dan debat olahraga baru seperti skateboarding yang debut di panggung utama. Untuk tuan rumah, hasilnya membanggakan: Jepang mencatat panen medali terbaik dalam sejarahnya, termasuk 27 emas, didorong generasi atlet muda yang menginspirasi anak-anak di seluruh negeri.

Olimpiade yang ditunda itu kelak dinilai sebagai metafora sempurna era Reiwa: rencana besar yang harus direvisi berkali-kali, harga yang mahal, namun di ujungnya tetap meninggalkan kebanggaan yang tak terbantahkan.

## Politik Bergolak dan Tragedi yang Mengejutkan

Di balik gemerlap olimpiade, politik Jepang era Reiwa mengalami guncangan yang tidak pernah dibayangkan siapa pun. Pada Juli 2022, dunia dikejutkan oleh berita yang terasa mustahil: mantan Perdana Menteri **Shinzō Abe**, politisi paling berpengaruh di generasinya, dibunuh saat berkampe di Nara. Pelakunya menembak dengan senjata rakitan buatan sendiri, dan motifnya membuka kotak Pandora: hubungan historis antara elite politik Jepang dan organisasi Gereja Unifikasi yang telah lama dikeluhkan korban pemerasan sumbangannya.

Kematian Abe memicu gelombang duka sekaligus amarah. Upacara kenegaraan untuk sang mantan perdana menteri di September 2022 berlangsung di tengah protes anti-pemerintah yang besar, karena publik mempertanyakan penggunaan dana negara dan keterlibatan politik dengan sekte tersebut. Tragedi ini mengubah wajah politik Jepang: partai penguasa terpaksa mengaudit hubungannya dengan organisasi keagamaan, dan kepercayaan publik pada elite mengalami goyangan baru.

Bahaya fisik kembali datang pada April 2023 ketika Perdana Menteri Fumio Kishida selamat dari upaya pengeboman saat berkampanye di Wakayama — insiden yang mengingatkan dunia betapa langkanya kekerasan politik di Jepang, dan betapa era Reiwa ingin menguji segalanya. Namun ujian terberat bagi partai penguasa justru datang dari dalam: skandal **slush fund** 2023-2024, ketika faksi-faksi besar partai terbukti menyimpan dana kampanye yang tidak dilaporkan selama bertahun-tahun. Skandal itu menghantam kepercayaan publik secara brutal, memaksa mundurnya menteri-menteri, dan menghancurkan popularitas pemerintahan Kishida.

Peta politik pun berubah cepat. Pada Oktober 2024, Shigeru Ishiba mengambil alih kepemimpinan partai dan pemerintahan, namun segera menghadapi pemilihan umum yang membuat koalisi penguasa kehilangan mayoritas absolut di parlemen untuk pertama kalinya sejak 2009. Setelah setahun penuh navigasi politik minoritas yang berat, tongkat kepemimpinan berpindah lagi pada akhir 2025 kepada **Sanae Takaichi**, yang mencatat sejarah sebagai perempuan pertama yang menjabat perdana menteri Jepang. Bagi sebuah negara yang dulu dikenal stabil secara politik, tempo pergantian pimpinan ini terasa seperti era baru yang sungguh-sungguh baru.

| Perdana Menteri | Masa Jabatan | Catatan Penting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shinzō Abe | sampai September 2020 | Masa jabatan terpanjang dalam sejarah; dibunuh 2022 |
| Yoshihide Suga | 2020-2021 | Memimpin di puncak pandemi |
| Fumio Kishida | 2021-2024 | Selamat dari upaya pembunuhan; tersandung skandal dana |
| Shigeru Ishiba | 2024-2025 | Kehilangan mayoritas parlemen |
| Sanae Takaichi | 2025-sekarang | Perempuan pertama sebagai PM |


![Era Reiwa](/images/topics/sejarah-alt.svg)
*Gambar: Era Reiwa*

## Alam Tetap Menguji

Sebagaimana zaman-zaman sebelumnya, era Reiwa tidak luput dari amukan alam. Pada 1 Januari 2024, saat warga baru saja merayakan pergantian tahun, gempa berkekuatan 7,6 menghantam Semenanjung Noto di pantai laut Jepang. Ratusan jiwa melayang, ribuan rumah rusak, dan pemulihan berlangsung lambat karena wilayah itu sudah dilemahkan serangkaian gempa sebelumnya. Tragedi Noto menjadi pengingat getir bahwa hidup di atas pertemuan lempeng tektonik adalah bagian permanen dari identitas Jepang.

Badai hujan ekstrem dan taifun yang semakin liar juga melanda berbagai wilayah sepanjang era ini, memperkuat diskursus nasional tentang perubahan iklim dan adaptasi bencana. Di sisi lain, setiap bencana kembali memperlihatkan keajaiban sosial Jepang: evakuasi tertib, solidaritas tetangga, dan pemulihan yang gigih. Budaya bencana yang matang dari pengalaman Heisei kini menjadi warisan yang terus diasah.

## Jepang Baru: Rekor Saham, Wisatawan, dan Geliat Dunia

Jika Heisei dikenang sebagai era stagnasi, Reiwa menawarkan plot twist yang tidak diprediksi siapa pun. Setelah 34 tahun menanti, indeks Nikkei akhirnya menembus rekor tertinggi era gelembung pada Februari 2024 dan terus mencetak puncak-puncak baru. Kebangkitan pasar modal ini ditopang reformasi tata kelola perusahaan, masuknya investor asing, dan posisi Jepang sebagai tujuan aman bagi kapital global.

Yen yang melemah dalam beberapa tahun terakhir membawa dua wajah. Bagi wisatawan, Jepang tiba-tiba terasa terjangkau, dan hasilnya luar biasa: jumlah kunjungan asing menembus rekor sepanjang sejarah, melampaui 36 juta kunjungan dalam setahun. Kota-kota seperti Kyoto dan Tokyo kembali hidup dengan wisatawan, meski overtourism memicu perdebatan lokal tentang menjaga kenyamanan warga. Bagi rumah tangga Jepang sendiri, yen lemah berarti harga impor melonjak, memicu inflasi pertama dalam beberapa dekade — fenomena aneh yang justru dirindukan bank sentral, karena deflasi panjang akhirnya tampak berakhir.

Panggung dunia juga kembali menyala. Pada 2023, Hiroshima menjadi tuan rumah KTT G7 yang penuh simbolisme perdamaian, dihadiri para pemimpin dunia di kota yang pernah dilanda bom atom. Pada 2025, Osaka menyelenggarakan World Expo di pulau buatan Yumeshima dengan maskot lucu bernama Myaku-Myaku, menarik puluhan juta pengunjung dan menampilkan teknologi robotika serta medis terbaik Jepang. Namun hubungan regional tidak selalu mulus: perseteran diplomatik dengan China yang memanas pada 2025-2026 mengingatkan bahwa geopolitik Asia Timur tetap rapuh, dan posisi Jepang sebagai mitra strategis Barat di kawasan ini semakin sentral.

## Harapan di Balik Era Baru

Di tengah segala gejolak, apa yang membuat orang Jepang tetap menyebut Reiwa sebagai era harapan? Jawabannya mungkin terletak pada karakter era itu sendiri. Keselarasan nan indah bukan janji bahwa hidup akan mudah, melainkan imbauan bahwa harmoni bisa dibangun bahkan di tengah badai. Pandemi dilalui dengan solidaritas, tragedi politik dijawab dengan reformasi transparansi, dan stagnasi lama ditutup dengan kebangkitan yang perlahan namun nyata.

Ada juga harapan yang tumbuh dari institusi kekaisaran itu sendiri. Kaisar Naruhito dan Permaisuri Masako mewakili generasi yang lebih terbuka, lebih internasional, dan lebih peka pada isu-isu kemanusiaan. Debat tentang suksesi perempuan semakin mainstream, dan masyarakat semakin berani membicarakan bentuk masa depan monarki yang lebih inklusif. Dari istana ke perkantoran, dari sekolah hingga parlemen, Jepang era Reiwa sedang belajar bahwa tradisi dan perubahan tidak harus saling menghabisi.

## Keluarga Kekaisaran di Bawah Sorotan

Era Reiwa juga menjadi panggung perdebatan paling terbuka tentang masa depan keluarga kekaisaran. Pada Oktober 2021, Putri Mako, keponakan Kaisar Naruhito, menikah dengan kekasih masa kuliahnya dan secara resmi melepaskan status kerajaannya sesuai aturan yang mewajibkan putri meninggalkan keluarga kaisar begitu menikah dengan rakyat biasa. Pernikahan itu berlangsung tanpa upacara tradisional di tengah badai opini publik, dan pasangan itu memulai hidup baru di New York. Kisah ini memicu simpati luas sekaligus memperkeruh pertanyaan lama: mengapa perempuan istana harus membayar harga setinggi itu untuk cinta?

Pertanyaan suksesi pun semakin mendesak karena hanya ada satu anak laki-laki muda di garis takhta. Putri Aiko, anak tunggal Kaisar Naruhito dan Permaisuri Masako, dinikmati publik sebagai sosok cerdas dan bersahaja, dan jajak pendapat rutin menunjukkan mayoritas warga mendukung kemungkinan seorang kaisar perempuan. Namun hukum suksesi masih mengharuskan garis keturunan laki-laki, menjadikan reformasi ini salah satu agenda politik tersulit era Reiwa.

Sementara itu, Kaisar Akihito dan Permaisuri Michiko menikmati masa pensiunnya dengan tenang, sesekali tampil di acara ilmiah dan musik. Citra dua kaisar yang saling menghormati, satu pensiun dengan anggun dan satu bertugas dengan hangat, memberi monarki Jepang citra baru: institusi tua yang mampu beradaptasi tanpa kehilangan wibawa.

## Keseharian Baru: Kerja, Harga, dan Digital

Di tingkat rumah tangga, era Reiwa mengubah ritme kehidupan kerja Jepang secara diam-diam namun menyeluruh. Reformasi gaya kerja yang digulirkan pemerintah mulai memangkas budaya lembur ekstrem, dan pandemi memaksa perusahaan menerima kerja dari rumah yang dulu dianggap mustahil dalam budaya tatap muka. Istilah-istilah baru seperti side gig dan remote work masuk percakapan sehari-hari generasi muda, sementara perdebatan kenaikan gaji menjadi isu nasional saat inflasi kembali hadir setelah puluhan tahun deflasi.

Kenaikan harga sendiri menjadi fenomena budaya yang unik di Jepang. Setiap kali produsen saus kecap atau mayones mengumumkan kenaikan harga, beritanya menghiasi headline nasional, sesuatu yang nyaris tak terbayangkan di negara lain. Bagi generasi yang dibesarkan oleh harga yang selalu turun, inflasi adalah pengalaman baru yang menuntut penyesuaian mental, dan serikat pekerja pun akhirnya mulai meraih kenaikan gaji tahunan terbesar dalam tiga dekade lewat musim negosiasi gaji.

Adopsi pembayaran digital juga melaju pesat. Masyarakat yang selama puluhan tahun setia pada uang tunai kini akrab dengan kode QR dan kartu e-money, didorong insentif pemerintah pasca-pandemi. Perubahan-perubahan kecil ini bila dirangkai membentuk potret Jepang yang sedang bergeser: tetap mencintai tradisi, tetapi tidak lagi menolak kenyamanan modern.

## Reiwa di Layar dan Budaya Populer

Sebagaimana lazimnya era baru, Reiwa langsung diserap industri hiburan. Nama zaman ini muncul dalam judul anime, lagu, dan gim, sementara kalender nenggō tetap menjadi bahasa resmi dokumen harian sehingga orang Jepang menghitung usia anak-anak mereka dalam tahun Reiwa. Menariknya, fenomena besar budaya pop awal era seperti gelombang global Demon Slayer justru menghidupkan nostalgia pada zaman Taisho, membuktikan bahwa Jepang modern senang menari antara masa lalu dan masa depan.

Boom retro Heisei juga berkobar di era ini. Anak-anak muda yang tidak sempat menikmati dekade 1990-an membeli ulang konsol game lawas, memutar playlist city pop, dan mengadopsi mode era gelembung dengan rasa ironis yang manis. Industri pariwisata pun memanen momentum ini: wisatawan asing datang bukan hanya untuk kuil dan sakura, tetapi juga untuk lokasi syuting anime, toko retro game, dan kafe bertema nostalgia.

Bagi banyak pengamat, kombinasi inilah identitas budaya Reiwa: bangsa yang cukup dewasa untuk merayakan masa lalunya tanpa berhenti bergerak maju. Dari kaligrafi nama era yang diambil dari puisi seribu dua ratus tahun, hingga gim mobile di saku remaja, rentang waktu yang sama dipegang dengan tenang oleh satu tangan.

## Wisatawan, Kota Sesak, dan Pintu yang Perlahan Terbuka

Ledakan wisatawan membawa sisi lain yang tidak selalu indah. Kyoto di jam-jam sibuk sesak hingga warga lokal kesulitan naik bus, Airbnb merambah permukiman tradisional, dan geisha harus berjalan di gang yang dipenuhi kamera turis. Pemerintah kota bahkan memasang larangan memotret di gang-gang tertentu dan menaikkan pajak akomodasi. Overtourism menjadi kata kunci baru dalam perencanaan kota Jepang, keseimbangan antara rezeki ekonomi dan kualitas hidup warga yang harus dijaga terus-menerus.

Di sisi lain, sektor pariwisata yang meledak itu memperlihatkan masalah struktural lama: kekurangan tenaga kerja akibat populasi menua. Hotel, restoran, dan pabrik kesulitan mencari pekerja, sehingga Jepang perlahan membuka pintu kepada pekerja asing melalui skema visa khusus, sesuatu yang nyaris tak terpikirkan satu dekade lalu. Komunitas Indonesia pun ikut tumbuh pesat sebagai salah satu kelompok pekerja dan pelajar asing terbesar di Jepang era ini.

Perubahan ini menggeser percakapan nasional tentang siapa orang Jepang dan bagaimana negeri ini akan bertahan. Dari debat imigrasi hingga teknologi robotika pelayan, Reiwa adalah era ketika Jepang akhirnya berdamai dengan satu kenyataan: untuk tetap harmonis di masa depan, ia perlu dunia lebih dari sebelumnya. Dan sebagaimana makna namanya, harmoni itu sedang dibangun pelan-pelan, dengan cermat, khas Jepang.

## Kesimpulan

Era Reiwa adalah bukti bahwa sejarah tidak pernah berhenti mengejutkan. Dimulai dengan kaligrafi indah yang diambil dari puisi seribu dua ratus tahun lampau, era ini langsung dilempar ke pusaran pandemi, olimpiade tanpa penonton, pembunuhan politik, gempa tahun baru, dan revolusi pasar saham yang menunggu tiga dekade. Melalui semua itu, Jepang tetap berdiri — tertib, tangguh, dan perlahan menemukan ritmenya kembali.

Bagi kita yang mengamati dari luar, Reiwa mengajarkan sesuatu yang universal. Sebuah zaman baru tidak diukur dari kemulusan awalnya, melainkan dari cara penduduknya menghadapi hal-hal yang tidak direncanakan. Orang Jepang memasuki Reiwa dengan harapan, diuji dengan keras, dan tetap memilih harmoni sebagai kompas. Barangkali itulah inti dari dua kanji 令和: bukan dunia yang menjadi indah dengan sendirinya, melainkan manusia yang memutuskan untuk menjaga keselarasan meski dunia bergolak. Dan jika sejarah Heisei adalah guru tentang jatuh, maka Reiwa yang baru berusia beberapa tahun ini sedang menulis pelajaran tentang bangkit.

en.contentMarkdown:
---
title: "The Reiwa Era: A New Emperor, New Hopes for Japan"
excerpt: "A new era name opened Emperor Naruhito's reign. From a pandemic and postponed Olympics to record stock highs — the full story of Japan under Reiwa."
meta_title: "The Reiwa Era: A New Emperor, New Hopes for Japan"
meta_description: "Understanding the Reiwa era: the meaning of 令和, Emperor Naruhito's transition, COVID-19, the Tokyo Olympics, and Japan's new hopes for the future."
category: "history"
tags: ["reiwa era", "emperor naruhito", "japanese history", "tokyo olympics", "japanese culture"]

# The Reiwa Era: A New Emperor, New Hopes for Japan


![The Reiwa Era — ilustrasi topik](/images/topics/sejarah-jepang.svg)
*Image: The Reiwa Era*

On the afternoon of April 1, 2019, millions of Japanese froze in front of television screens at their offices, ramen shops, and train stations. Everyone was waiting for one thing: the announcement of the nation's new era name. When Chief Cabinet Secretary Yoshihide Suga raised a calligraphy board bearing two simple kanji — **令和**, Reiwa — a tidal wave of online searches crashed servers across the country. Within hours, all of Japan was learning how to write the name of its own era. There was no drama, no major controversy, just a collective curiosity that felt warm and faintly moving.

The Reiwa era officially began on May 1, 2019, one day after Emperor Akihito stepped down, when his son ascended as **Emperor Naruhito**, the 126th monarch of the world's oldest continuous throne. Unlike Heisei, which opened with an emperor's death, Reiwa opened with a choice: a man respectfully choosing retirement so his country would not be burdened. And true to form for any Japanese era, this one was immediately tested by events no scriptwriter would dare invent — a global pandemic, Olympics without spectators, the assassination of a former prime minister, an earthquake on New Year's morning, and a stock market record that waited thirty-four years to be broken.

## The Meaning Behind Two Kanji

Every era name in Japan carries a message, and Reiwa holds one of the most beautiful. The first character, **rei** 令, means good, noble, or decree; the second, **wa** 和, means harmony or peace. The government's official English translation chose *beautiful harmony*, while some scholars read it more broadly as peace born of good order.

What makes Reiwa special is not just its meaning but its origin story. For over a thousand years, every Japanese era name had been drawn from classical Chinese texts. Reiwa shattered that tradition completely: its name comes from the **Man'yōshū**, Japan's oldest poetry anthology, compiled in the eighth century. The source is the preface to a series of plum blossom poems composed by Ōtomo no Tabito, describing an early spring scene — a lovely month, clear air, gentle wind, friends gathered to savor beauty together.

The choice was deliberate and deeply symbolic. By taking its name from Japan's own literature, the country seemed to say that its new era now stands rooted in its own soil rather than borrowed from abroad. For many Japanese, the announcement became a national moment of reflection about identity: a nation confident enough to cite the beauty of its own heritage.

### How the Name Was Chosen

The selection process itself is fascinating. A panel of nine intellectuals spanning fields — from Nobel laureates to celebrated novelists — secretly proposed candidate names. The government then screened them, consulted with parliament, and handed the final decision to the cabinet. Even the imperial family had no vote. The result was unveiled in a simple ceremony: the chief cabinet secretary lifting the board with the era name before the world's cameras.

Reiwa even left a mark on technology. The Unicode Consortium created a dedicated code point, U+32FF, for a combined glyph joining both kanji — something never done for any previous era name. Official documents, train tickets, and business cards printed with Japan's traditional nengō calendar automatically flipped years: 2019 became Reiwa 1, and so on to this day.

## The Succession: Welcoming the 126th Emperor

The day after the name reveal, on April 30, 2019, Japan witnessed an abdication ceremony unseen for two centuries. Emperor Akihito, who had reigned thirty years defined by empathy, voluntarily relinquished the throne through special legislation. The next morning, May 1, 2019, Crown Prince Naruhito took his seat as the 126th emperor, and the Reiwa era began.

Naruhito brought a symbolic leadership style distinct from his father's yet equally warm. An Oxford graduate who researched waterway transport history on the Thames, fluent in English, he is known as a vocal supporter of gender equality and disability rights. Empress **Masako**, his wife, is a former career diplomat educated at Harvard whose long struggle against palace pressures made many Japanese women feel personally connected to the couple.

In his early addresses, Naruhito pledged to stand close to his people, share in their joys and sorrows, and uphold peace — notes that resonate with generations increasingly distant from firsthand memories of war. The smooth, dignified transition proved that Japan's symbolic monarchy can adapt to modern times without losing its grace.

## A First Year Full of Promise

The first months of Reiwa felt like spring itself. In June 2019, Osaka hosted Japan's first G20 summit, gathering world leaders in the old merchant city. Foreign tourists flooded the country in record numbers, the yen held relatively strong, and post-Heisei renewal energy felt tangible everywhere. Parents named children using the kanji of Reiwa, special-edition products celebrating the new era sold briskly, and official correspondence switched to fresh Reiwa greetings.

There were small moments that warmed hearts too. Emperor Naruhito made early visits to regions still recovering from Heisei-era disasters, signaling that the new era would not forget old wounds. Public debate about the imperial family's future also opened wider, including the once-taboo question of whether a woman could ascend the throne, given that Princess Aiko is the imperial couple's only child. Reiwa seemed ready to become an era of openness.

But the universe had other plans. At the close of that first year, a virus called SARS-CoV-2 was spreading quietly out of Wuhan, and Japan — like everyone else — did not yet know its new decade would open with its greatest test.

## The Pandemic That Changed Everything

In early 2020, COVID-19 swept through Japan as it swept the planet. The government declared states of emergency urging people to stay home, venues closed, masks became mandatory daily wear, and Tokyo streets that normally overflowed fell silent like science fiction film sets. A tourism boom collapsed overnight, and businesses struggled painfully to shift toward remote work.

The pandemic also held up an honest mirror. A nation famed for high tech turned out to still depend on fax machines and paper documents, prompting the creation of a **Digital Agency** in 2021 to accelerate bureaucratic transformation. Health systems were stretched to limits, and economic inequality between permanent and nonpermanent workers widened as the virus battered the service sector where most young people work.

Yet the social response deserves admiration. Unlike parts of the West, Japan saw no major mask or vaccine culture wars. Citizens followed protocols with characteristic discipline, the vaccination campaign succeeded after a slow start, and society once again demonstrated its cohesive strength in hardship. The crisis also reshuffled political priorities toward supply-chain resilience, domestic semiconductor production, and digital worker welfare.

## Tokyo 2020: The Stage That Was Postponed

Nothing captures the early Reiwa struggle better than the Tokyo 2020 Olympics. Planned as a symbol of national revival, the Games were postponed by one full year — the first postponement in modern Olympic history — because of the pandemic. Budgets ballooned, public opinion split, and many Japanese demanded outright cancellation in the name of safety.

Still, in July 2021, the Olympic flame burned at Tokyo's National Stadium — without domestic spectators in the stands. Though the atmosphere felt hollow, the Games gave the world a rare dose of hope mid-pandemic: athletes competing in masks, podiums greeted by empty-handed applause, and new sports like skateboarding debuting on the grandest stage. For the host nation, the outcome was glorious: Japan posted its best medal haul ever, including 27 golds, powered by young athletes who inspired children nationwide.

The postponed Olympics now reads as a perfect metaphor for early Reiwa: a grand plan revised again and again, paid for dearly, yet ultimately leaving behind pride nobody can deny.

## Turbulent Politics and Shocking Tragedy

Behind the Olympic spotlight, Reiwa politics suffered shocks nobody imagined. In July 2022, the world reeled at news that seemed impossible: former Prime Minister **Shinzō Abe**, the most influential politician of his generation, was assassinated while campaigning in Nara. The gunman used a homemade weapon, and his motive opened Pandora's box: the historical ties between political elites and the Unification Church, long lamented by families drained by coerced donations.

Abe's death triggered waves of grief and fury alike. His state funeral in September 2022 proceeded amid large anti-government protests, as citizens questioned state funding and the political-sect entanglement. The tragedy redrew Japan's political landscape: the ruling party was forced to audit its religious affiliations, and public trust in elites took another hit.

Physical danger returned in April 2023 when Prime Minister Fumio Kishida survived a pipe-bomb attack while campaigning in Wakayama — an incident reminding the world how rare political violence is in Japan, and how determined the era seemed to test everything. Yet the ruling party's harshest trial came from within: the **slush fund scandal** of 2023–2024, revealing that major party factions had hidden unreported campaign money for years. It crushed public confidence brutally, forced ministerial resignations, and wrecked the Kishida government's popularity.

The political map then shifted rapidly. In October 2024, Shigeru Ishiba took over the party and government, only to face a general election that stripped the ruling coalition of its absolute majority for the first time since 2009. After a grueling year navigating minority politics, leadership passed again in late 2025 to **Sanae Takaichi**, who made history as Japan's first female prime minister. For a nation once famous for political stability, this pace of change feels genuinely like a brand-new era.

| Prime Minister | Tenure | Key Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shinzō Abe | until September 2020 | Longest-serving in history; assassinated 2022 |
| Yoshihide Suga | 2020–2021 | Led at the pandemic peak |
| Fumio Kishida | 2021–2024 | Survived assassination attempt; undone by fund scandal |
| Shigeru Ishiba | 2024–2025 | Lost parliamentary majority |
| Sanae Takaichi | 2025–present | First woman to serve as PM |


![The Reiwa Era](/images/topics/sejarah-alt.svg)
*Image: The Reiwa Era*

## Nature Keeps Testing

As in every age before it, the Reiwa era has not escaped nature's fury. On January 1, 2024, just as residents welcomed the new year, a magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck the Noto Peninsula along the Sea of Japan coast. Hundreds died, thousands of homes were damaged, and recovery crawled slowly because the region had already been weakened by earlier quakes. Noto stood as a grim reminder that life atop tectonic plate collisions remains a permanent part of Japanese identity.

Extreme rains and increasingly violent typhoons have battered various regions throughout the era, strengthening national discourse on climate change and disaster adaptation. On the brighter side, each catastrophe keeps revealing Japan's social miracle: orderly evacuations, neighborly solidarity, and stubborn rebuilding. The disaster culture matured during Heisei has become a living inheritance, continuously sharpened.

## New Japan: Records, Tourists, and a Rising Market

If Heisei is remembered as stagnation, Reiwa offers a plot twist nobody predicted. After waiting thirty-four years, the Nikkei index finally broke its bubble-era record in February 2024 and kept printing fresh highs. The rally rests on corporate governance reform, surging foreign investment, and Japan's status as safe harbor for global capital.

A weakening yen over recent years has worn two faces. For tourists, Japan suddenly feels affordable, and the results are spectacular: foreign arrivals smashed all-time records, exceeding 36 million visits in a single year. Cities like Kyoto and Tokyo buzz with visitors again, though overtourism sparks local debates about preserving residents' comfort. For Japanese households, the weak yen sends import prices soaring, igniting the first inflation in decades — a strange phenomenon the central bank actually welcomes, since the long deflation finally appears to have ended.

The world stage lit up again too. In 2023, Hiroshima hosted a deeply symbolic G7 summit of peace, gathering world leaders in the atomic-bombed city. In 2025, Osaka staged World Expo on the artificial island of Yumeshima, complete with the adorable mascot Myaku-Myaku, drawing tens of millions of visitors and showcasing Japan's finest robotics and medical technology. Regional relations are not always smooth, however: diplomatic tensions with China flaring through 2025–2026 remind everyone that East Asian geopolitics remain fragile, and Japan's role as the West's strategic partner grows ever more central.

## Hope Beneath the New Era

Amid all the turbulence, why do the Japanese still call Reiwa an era of hope? Perhaps because of the era's very character. Beautiful harmony never promised easy living; instead, it urges that harmony can be built even inside storms. The pandemic was weathered with solidarity, political tragedy answered with transparency reforms, and long stagnation closed by a slow but real revival.

Hope also grows from the imperial institution itself. Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako represent a more open, international, humanitarian-minded generation. Debate over female succession grows mainstream, and society speaks more boldly about an inclusive future for the monarchy. From palace to office, schoolhouse to parliament, Reiwa Japan is learning that tradition and change need not destroy each other.

## The Imperial Family Under the Spotlight

Reiwa also became the stage for history's most open debate about the imperial family's future. In October 2021, Princess Mako, Emperor Naruhito's niece, married her college sweetheart and formally relinquished her royal status under rules requiring princesses to leave the imperial family upon marrying commoners. The wedding proceeded without traditional ceremonies amid a storm of public opinion, and the couple began a new life in New York. The story drew widespread sympathy while sharpening an old question: why must palace women pay such a steep price for love?

Succession questions grew more urgent with only one young male in the line. Princess Aiko, the emperor and empress's only child, is publicly cherished as bright and unpretentious, and regular polls show a majority of citizens supporting the possibility of a female emperor. Yet succession law still requires male lineage, making this reform one of Reiwa politics' hardest agendas.

Meanwhile, Emperor Emeritus Akihito and Empress Michiko enjoy a quiet retirement, occasionally appearing at scientific and musical events. The image of two emperors in mutual respect — one retiring gracefully, one serving warmly — gives Japan's monarchy a fresh face: an ancient institution adapting without losing its dignity.

## Daily Life: Work, Prices, and Going Digital

At the household level, Reiwa quietly but thoroughly rewired Japanese working life. Government work-style reforms began trimming extreme overtime culture, and the pandemic forced companies to accept remote work once deemed impossible in a face-to-face society. New vocabulary like side gig entered young people's daily conversations, while wage hikes became a national issue as inflation returned after decades of deflation.

Rising prices themselves became a uniquely cultural phenomenon in Japan. Whenever a soy sauce or mayonnaise maker announces a price increase, it headlines national news — nearly unimaginable elsewhere. For generations raised on falling prices, inflation demands psychological adjustment, and labor unions finally secured their largest annual raises in three decades through spring wage negotiations.

Digital payment adoption accelerated too. A society loyal to cash for decades now embraces QR codes and e-money cards, nudged by post-pandemic government incentives. Strung together, these small shifts sketch a Japan in transition: still devoted to tradition, no longer refusing modern convenience.

## Reiwa on Screens and in Pop Culture

As with any new era, entertainment absorbed Reiwa instantly. The era name appears across anime titles, songs, and games, while the nengō calendar remains official language for everyday documents — Japanese parents literally measure their children's ages in Reiwa years. Curiously, early-era pop phenomena like Demon Slayer's global wave revived nostalgia for the Taisho period, proof that modern Japan loves dancing between past and future.

The Heisei retro boom burns bright in this era as well. Youngsters who never experienced the 1990s rebuy vintage consoles, spin city pop playlists, and adopt bubble-era fashion with sweet irony. Tourism harvests this momentum: visitors come not only for temples and cherry blossoms but for anime filming locations, retro game shops, and nostalgia-themed cafes.

For many observers, this combination defines Reiwa's cultural identity: a nation mature enough to celebrate its past without standing still. From the calligraphy of an era name drawn from a twelve-hundred-year-old poem to mobile games in teenagers' pockets, one hand calmly holds both ends of time.

## Tourists, Crowded Cities, and Doors Slowly Opening

The tourist boom carried a less glamorous side. Kyoto at rush hour became so packed that locals struggled to board buses, short-term rentals crept into traditional neighborhoods, and geisha walked lanes crowded with tourist cameras. City governments responded with photography bans in certain alleys and higher lodging taxes. Overtourism became the new keyword in Japanese urban planning — a constant balancing act between economic windfall and residents' quality of life.

The exploding tourism sector also exposed an old structural problem: labor shortages driven by an aging population. Hotels, restaurants, and factories struggled to find staff, so Japan gradually opened its doors to foreign workers through special visa schemes — unthinkable a decade earlier. The Indonesian community, among others, grew rapidly as one of the largest groups of foreign workers and students in this era's Japan.

These shifts moved the national conversation about who the Japanese are and how the country will endure. From immigration debates to service robotics, Reiwa is the era when Japan finally made peace with one reality: to stay harmonious in the future, it needs the world more than ever. And true to its name, that harmony is being built slowly and carefully, in the most Japanese way possible.

## Conclusion

The Reiwa era proves history never stops surprising us. Opened with elegant calligraphy drawn from a twelve-hundred-year-old poem, the era was immediately thrown into pandemics, spectator-less Olympics, political assassination, a New Year's earthquake, and a stock market revolution three decades in waiting. Through it all, Japan kept standing — orderly, resilient, slowly finding its rhythm back.

For outside observers, Reiwa teaches something universal. A new age is measured not by flawless beginnings but by how its people face the unplanned. The Japanese entered Reiwa with hope, were tested hard, and still chose harmony as their compass. That may be the essence of the two kanji 令和: the world does not turn beautiful on its own; rather, people decide to preserve harmony even while the world shakes. And if Heisei's history was the lesson in falling, Reiwa — only a handful of years old — is busy writing the lesson in rising.
